Source: README.md

Systems engineering agents

MBSE Agents helps an AI assistant investigate systems, understand relationships, explain engineering decisions, develop connected artifacts, and challenge claims against their evidence. It supports work from early concepts through operations, architecture, assurance and change review.

The agent combines a systems-engineering reasoning core with task and domain skills. Use it to think through an unfamiliar problem, examine an existing project, or produce the particular artifacts a decision requires. The skill catalog describes the available entry points.

Start with your system

Launch Codex in this checkout, or install selected skills into an existing project. The local installer needs Python 3.10+ and no third-party packages or credentials. Use python3 on Linux/macOS or py on Windows.

git clone https://github.com/ajhcs/mbse-agents.git
cd mbse-agents
python3 scripts/install.py --list
python3 scripts/install.py --project /path/to/project --skill mbse-systems-engineering --skill mbse-requirements --skill mbse-architecture --dry-run
python3 scripts/install.py --project /path/to/project --skill mbse-systems-engineering --skill mbse-requirements --skill mbse-architecture

Use $mbse-systems-engineering to investigate this system and the decision we need to make. Work from the supplied material. Explain the boundary, relevant stakeholders, dependencies and competing interpretations. Develop the necessary engineering artifacts, retain source IDs and existing decisions, and identify the evidence that would change your recommendation.

Choose a focused task skill when the work is already clear. Domain skills cover aerospace, defense, automotive, medical devices and electronic systems. The workflows guide explains how to combine them, and the first-use tutorial supplies a brief and a complete path to reviewing the result.

Learn from engineering work

The gallery connects domain baselines, executable teaching models and historical project studies. The historical cases emphasize projects from before 2015 and connect original source material to retrospective questions about system boundaries, interfaces, decisions, operations, organizations and evidence.

The cold-storage alarm walkthrough connects stakeholder needs, requirements, architecture, procedures and saved reference-model observations. Domain simulation evidence identifies the exact models and assumptions behind generated analyses. Each case distinguishes original project evidence, new analysis, executed model results and work that still needs physical or program evidence.

Assess engineering judgment

The benchmark and quiz system assesses problem framing, systems thinking, causal reasoning, evidence interpretation, technical judgment and communication. Artifact tasks assess existing-project review and change handling as well as drafting. Automatic quiz results and independently reviewed reasoning are reported separately.

Use the evaluation protocol to compare a model alone with the same model using the agent skills. Instruction changes should be supported by observed performance; a passing package check is not a model-quality result.

Use the host that fits your work

Codex, Claude Code, Databricks, ChatGPT, and portable hosts have distinct discovery and installation mechanisms. Guides identify documented adaptations and the checks actually performed. Plugin distribution describes the generated portable package; the source checkout keeps its canonical skills under .agents/skills.

The installer preserves existing project instructions, host settings and local skill edits. CSE provides optional executable engineering analysis and model methods; Ingenium supports editable presentation. Available connectors determine which live tools the host can use. See model and tool crosswalks.

Develop and verify

python3 scripts/catalog.py --write
python3 scripts/validate.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

Model guidance, source checks, and contribution instructions describe the maintained contracts. The source is MIT-licensed. Referenced standards and historical materials remain under their publishers' terms.

Source: docs/SUBMISSIONS.md

Distribution and discovery

Start with the repository's skill catalog and installation guide. The catalog and examples describe shipped content. They make no marketplace, model-quality, certification, or vendor-compatibility claim.

For broader distribution, follow OpenAI plugin packaging and check the current submission requirements. This repository has not been submitted to a plugin directory. Do not publish or contact external communities without a concrete release and the maintainer's publication direction.

Static documentation

The public reading entrypoint covers installation, a supplied first task, workflows, historical cases, teaching examples and the judgment benchmark. The separate review packet opens the dated assessment records. Their selected reading content and local images are bundled in HTML; external primary-source links still require network access.

Build with the optional pinned dependencies in requirements-docs.txt, then run python3 scripts/render_preview.py --check. Publish the complete docs/site directory only after release review. Its manifest binds source and output hashes; it does not constitute a deployment receipt, model-quality result or engineering approval. See build and review details.

Source: docs/approved-scope.md

Approved expansion scope

Decision recorded 2026-11-13. This is the implementation record for the user's numbered review of the 74 proposed changes. It preserves the approved scope; completion is established by the implementation and its evidence, not this plan.

Product direction

Build a leading systems engineering agent plugin: useful engineering reasoning, understanding, explanation, investigation, design and review across substantial systems and their lifecycle. Broaden the work and historical gallery. Codex, Claude and Databricks are important host contexts; support claims must identify what has actually been exercised. CSE supplies complementary computable analysis and diagram methods; Ingenium informs editable presentation.

The user reports substantial downloads and inbound organizational interest. This informs the product direction; it is not a verified usage count, customer contract, endorsement, or permission to use an organization's marks.

Accepted decisions

Original items Implementation intent
1 Replace unsupported public expertise/performance claims through a reviewed release.
2–3 Expand ambition and supported engineering work; connect portable agent guidance with optional CSE computation.
4 Remove founder review from the shipped engineering catalog; preserve its source in the archive.
5–9 Harden the domain examples through explicit models, corrected logic, executed simulations and generated evidence. Preserve the engineering substance and establish each supported claim.
10 Bolster source-grounded standards reasoning and claim-level provenance.
11–12 Expand the gallery substantially, with review coverage and strong historical project representation.
13–15 Strengthen evidence lifecycle, trusted outcome counting and schema/provenance checks.
16–19 Complete interfaces, precise artifact links, retained execution history and revision/reverification examples.
20–22 Build a benchmark and quiz system for systems thinking, judgment, communication, review and actual skill activation; measure and improve performance.
23 Exercise existing multi-file projects, emphasizing projects from before 2015.
24–28 Fresh cases, producer/reviewer separation, provenance, independent assessment, predeclared release criteria and reproducible packets.
29–34 Connected example records, shared baselines, identifier lifecycle, relationship meanings, portable source records and general risk/control records.
37–41 Clear routing, complete discovery copy, useful prompts, version-specific crosswalks and an end-to-end tutorial.
42–47 Working launcher commands, installation diagnostics, honest host support, model guidance, native packaging and versioned release.
49–54 Packaged license, correct modification detection, staged-content verification, recoverable installation, local diff, restore and removal.
58–64 Reproducible public documentation, complete references, deep links, source-derived diagrams, generated metadata and useful navigation.
66–67 Deliberate document printing and clear separation of historical/internal guidance.

The omitted proposals 35, 36, 48, 55, 56, 57, 65, 68, 69, 70, 71, 72, 73 and 74 are discarded. They are not a deferred roadmap. Focused regression tests needed to verify an approved code change remain part of that change; this does not reopen the discarded general testing/platform-expansion programs.

Evidence commitments

Strengthening a claim means supplying analysis, a justified model, an executable experiment, or directly applicable source evidence. A Boolean proof establishes the declared Boolean property. A simulation establishes behavior of the specified model under its inputs. Neither silently becomes physical reliability, regulatory approval, historical project evidence, or stakeholder acceptance.

The benchmark must test how an agent understands and communicates engineering, not only whether it can invoke tools or reproduce expected vocabulary. Automatic quiz scores, independently reviewed reasoning, artifact-task performance and host activation are distinct results. Preserve failures and tune on development cases; use fresh cases for subsequent assessment.

Work streams

  1. Agent reasoning, composition and domain contracts.
  2. Domain simulation and evidence packages; historical engineering cases.
  3. Judgment quizzes, project tasks, independent assessment and tuning.
  4. Installation, recovery, host adaptation and portable plugin packaging.
  5. Public documentation, editable source-derived diagrams and release evidence.

The release report records actual completed work and remaining gates against these streams. No sales, subscription, telemetry, business-pilot or unrelated maintenance-policy program is included.

Source: docs/benchmark.md

Systems engineering judgment benchmark

This benchmark asks whether an agent understands a system, makes defensible engineering judgments and explains them usefully. Writing a document or running a tool is only part of that work.

There are two complementary tracks:

Track What the participant does What can be assessed
Judgment questions Select a defensible response and explain the reasoning Selection accuracy against a proposed key; independently assessed reasoning, assumptions and communication
Engineering performance Work from supplied project facts or a multi-file baseline and deliver a useful result Problem understanding, preserved intent, causal analysis, artifacts, change propagation, evidence judgment and explanation

The question bank spans problem framing, lifecycle context, causal dependencies, evidence, requirements, interfaces, alternatives, uncertainty, human and organizational systems, communication, source interpretation and change review. Its historical questions use supplied facts from projects before 2015 and ask what transfers to a new situation. They do not reward recalling obscure accident details or treating an old document as a current requirement.

The current inventory and source locators are in the question bank. The historical gallery provides deeper studies. The question keys and reviewer criteria are authored proposals that received independent agent review. Their existence is not evidence of agent performance. The observed runs reached a selection ceiling in every arm and retained common reasoning gaps. Appropriate domain adjudication and harder performance work remain necessary for broader claims.

The initial three-arm diagnostic produced 24/24 selections in every arm. Independent review found that choosing the longest option answered 54 of 55 single-choice questions correctly. Those results establish no improvement from the skills. Version 0.2.0 revises the choices and two ambiguous stems, clarifies one system boundary and strengthens the scoring contract. The original questions, keys, code and results remain unchanged in the archive. The revised questions require fresh assessment; reducing a surface cue does not establish useful difficulty or valid keys.

Try a question

From the repository, use Python 3.10 or newer. On Windows, py can replace python3 in these commands.

python3 scripts/benchmark.py list --split practice
python3 scripts/benchmark.py practice --item SEJ-001
python3 scripts/benchmark.py practice --item SEJ-001 --answer A --reason "Explain why you selected this option."

Replace A and the explanation with your answer. Multiple-selection questions accept several letters after --answer. Feedback says whether the selection matches the proposed key and explains its basis. It does not automatically grade your explanation. A defensible challenge to a key is a finding to adjudicate.

Run an agent exercise

Prepare a fresh packet and give only that packet to a new participant chat:

python3 scripts/benchmark.py prepare --split development --arm task-domain --output /workspace/mbse-evaluation/development-task-domain

The packet contains the request, selected questions, a response template, a manifest of exact input hashes and the selected skills. It does not include keys, reviewer criteria, historical answers or other runs. The participant fills the response template and saves answers.json, preserving its schema_version and packet fields as well as the original packet inputs. These fields bind the answers to that packet and its input revision. Moving answers to another arm or new packet requires a new run; the scorer rejects an unchanged replay. The run fields record the actual producer, model, host, settings, times, tools and unavailable information. Use explicit unknown when a host does not expose a value; do not infer model identity from marketing names.

Use --item SEJ-003 --item SEJ-008 to select a small exercise or --dimension interfaces to focus on one reasoning area. Comparison arms are:

Arm Skills exposed
none No skill packages
task Relevant task packages
task-domain Relevant task and domain packages
catalog All shipped packages, for discovery and nonactivation assessment

Use identical selected questions and host/tool access across comparison arms. A none packet contains no skill files; it does not disable personal, global or parent-directory skills in the host. Record the effective discovery inventory and prevent unintended skill loading when evaluating a no-skill baseline. A fresh conversation alone does not establish host isolation. A full-catalog packet tests exposure; the evaluator must also observe which skills the host actually activates. Merely copying packages is not an activation result. Model settings, context, prior exposure and order effects also matter.

python3 scripts/benchmark.py score --packet /workspace/mbse-evaluation/development-task-domain --answers /workspace/mbse-evaluation/development-task-domain/answers.json --output /workspace/mbse-evaluation/development-score.json

The score reports each item, unanswered items, accuracy by reasoning dimension, an equal-dimension summary and a mathematical uniform-choice reference. For a single-choice question the reference is 1 / number of options; for a multiple-selection question it is 1 / number of nonempty subsets. This is not a claim about how an informed person or model guesses.

An incorrect or omitted selection receives no selection credit. No partial credit is inferred from a subset of a multiple-selection answer. An explanation may still reveal valuable reasoning or a flawed question; it needs separate assessment. Correct letters without sound explanation do not establish engineering competence.

Assess explanations independently

The reviewer receives the unchanged participant output, original facts and the separate reviewer key after production is finished. For each question, review the listed reasoning criteria on this scale:

Rating Meaning
0 Missing, contradicted or materially unsupported
1 Partly addressed, with a consequential gap or ambiguity
2 Addressed coherently using the supplied facts and appropriate limits

Review the selection and the key as well as the explanation. Record critical errors separately; a fluent response must not conceal an invented source, unsupported acceptance claim or important loss of stakeholder intent.

Generate a separate review template after production:

python3 scripts/benchmark.py review-template --packet /workspace/mbse-evaluation/development-task-domain --answers /workspace/mbse-evaluation/development-task-domain/answers.json --output /workspace/mbse-evaluation/review.json

The template contains no ratings. It binds the assessment to the exact answer bytes, packet manifest, key revision and selected reasoning criteria:

{
  "schema_version": 2,
  "answers_sha256": "SHA256_OF_THE_ACTUAL_ANSWERS_FILE",
  "packet_manifest_sha256": "SHA256_OF_THE_PACKET_MANIFEST",
  "key_sha256": "SHA256_OF_THE_KEY_FILE",
  "criteria_sha256": "HASH_GENERATED_BY_REVIEW_TEMPLATE",
  "reviewer": "identified-reviewer",
  "independent_of_production": true,
  "items": {
    "SEJ-003": {
      "criteria": [2, 1],
      "comment": "Explain the assessment against the actual response.",
      "critical_errors": []
    }
  }
}

Disposition every selected question and every reasoning criterion; the example above is only the file shape. Pass the file with score --review review.json. The tool labels it a reviewer-reported assessment. It cannot authenticate the reviewer's competence or prove independence from a name. Domain disagreements and consequential claims require appropriate expert adjudication.

Assess engineering performance

The performance bank is cases.json. Cases include broad systems questions, automotive and defense reasoning, historical transfer, source criticism and a concrete multi-file revision exercise. HO-13 supplies approved source wording, requirements, architecture, an old observation and a change request. The participant must preserve the inputs and produce a coherent revision and review.

python3 scripts/prepare_eval.py --case HO-13 --arm none --output /workspace/mbse-evaluation/change-baseline
python3 scripts/prepare_eval.py --case HO-13 --arm task-domain --output /workspace/mbse-evaluation/change-skills

Independent reviewers assess outputs against source facts and case criteria. Record located findings, important omissions, invented claims, preserved human edits, task completion and the effort needed to repair the result. These performance tasks are the primary evidence for an improvement in engineering reasoning. Quiz scores are a diagnostic, particularly when most participants choose the correct options.

Practice, development and evaluation

The bank separates practice, development and evaluation-public questions. Every split covers all reasoning dimensions. Practice supports feedback. Development supports examining failures and revising the agent. The reserved public evaluation split is withheld from the prepared development packet, but its questions and keys are in this public repository. It is not a secret or leak-proof test set. Historical projects may also be familiar from model training. Version 0.2.0 was revised after authors and reviewers inspected the full bank; none of its splits should be described as untouched by the development process.

After a producer has seen a question or key, record the exposure and use a new reviewed variant for a credible later assessment. Do not tune on the reserved set and then describe it as untouched. A future protected evaluation must be held outside the producer's accessible repository and tools.

Before a comparison, state the workload, outcomes, errors that are unacceptable, required review, and conditions for retaining or rejecting a change. Use repeated independent runs where the decision justifies it. Separate gains in reasoning from longer answers, additional tool access or more expensive model settings.

python3 scripts/benchmark.py report /workspace/mbse-evaluation/baseline-score.json /workspace/mbse-evaluation/candidate-score.json

The report requires matching questions, bank and key revisions and distinct run IDs. It validates outcome fields and recomputes selection aggregates before reporting them. Packet checks require every mandatory input and every file in the declared skill packages, and reconcile the arm with actual package exposure. These consistency checks do not authenticate the producer or prevent a person from deliberately fabricating a complete record. It presents descriptive results; it does not automatically announce a winner, statistical significance or release readiness. Follow the evaluation protocol for recorded judgments and the limits of current evidence.

Inspect question construction

python3 scripts/benchmark.py diagnose
python3 scripts/benchmark.py diagnose --bank evals/archive/benchmark-0.1.0/evals/benchmark/items.json --keys evals/archive/benchmark-0.1.0/evals/benchmark/keys.json

The diagnostic reports keyed positions and actual accuracy for selecting the longest or shortest option by character count and by word count, both overall and by split. It exposes item lengths, ties and the deterministic tie rule. Multiple-selection questions are excluded from these single-option shortcuts. Use the results to investigate cues alongside independent content review, rather than imposing a numeric threshold as a substitute for question quality. Output can be preserved with --output to a fresh path. Score, diagnostic and review template commands refuse existing output files, including dangling symlinks.

Source: docs/crosswalk-reference.md

Model and evidence crosswalks

These mappings are proposed engineering practice, not normative equivalents, vendor endorsements, or a promise of supported automation. Confirm the tool, metamodel/profile, edition, extensions, and exchange configuration for the project.

Engineering concepts and SysML v1-style views

This table retains the repository's illustrative v1-style vocabulary. Select an actual language/profile version before creating or exchanging model elements. It is not a tested mapping for every tool that advertises SysML support.

Engineering intent Capella / Arcadia content SysML v1-style content Linked records
Stakeholder context Operational actors, capabilities, activities Actors, use cases, context blocks Needs and ConOps
Functional behavior System/logical functions and exchanges Activities, states, interactions Requirements and scenarios
Physical allocation Components, physical functions, links Blocks, parts, ports, allocations Design decisions and budgets
Requirement satisfaction Requirement integration/links as configured Requirements and satisfy/derive/trace relations Controlled requirement baseline
Verification Linked scenario/analysis results Test cases and verify relations Procedure, configuration, outcome
Hazard/threat control Linked analysis and allocated behavior Profile-specific analysis and requirements Risk/control/evidence records

SysML v2 work

SysML v2 uses definitions and usages for the concepts below. Keep its source model and notation distinct from v1 blocks/stereotypes; a similar engineering intent does not establish a lossless conversion.

Engineering intent Relevant SysML v2 concepts Work still requiring project decisions
Structure and external interaction Parts, ports, connections, and interfaces Boundary, multiplicity, exchanged items, responsibility
Behavior and modes Actions and states Conditions, transitions, timing, failure and recovery meaning
Responsibility and requirements Allocations, requirements, and satisfy requirement usages Relation semantics, actual allocation, satisfaction rationale
Verification planning Verification cases Procedure, configuration, result, and evidence applicability

Concept names were checked in OMG SysML 2.0 Part 1, formal/2026-03-02, sections 7.6, 7.11–7.15, 7.17–7.18, 7.21, and 7.24. The OMG version catalogs identify the published language and transformation specifications. This narrow terminology check does not validate a parser, exporter, transformation, or tool integration. Use the project's supported version and verify representative round trips before adopting an exchange.

Tools and controlled exchange

Cameo/CATIA Magic, Rhapsody, and Sparx Enterprise Architect can express SysML/UML concepts with their configured profiles. Exact element creation and export behavior depend on the version and extensions; do not invent stereotype names. DOORS/DOORS Next can provide linked controlled requirements. Simulink or other analysis tools can provide scoped models/results. FMI/FMU, ReqIF, and OSLC are integration mechanisms, not evidence that trace semantics survive transfer.

For a controlled exchange, specify ID preservation, relation direction/type, units, version, source of truth, conflict handling, extraction/filter settings, and reconciliation. Inspect a representative round trip. Check that a verify link connects an activity which actually tests the requirement's conditions.

Keep source obligations, proposed design satisfaction, planned verification, executed outcomes, and authorized acceptance separate. The optional trace meanings are local record conventions, not normative SysML relationship definitions.

Domain-specific threads and reviewer questions live in the domain packages' references. Use the catalog to find the relevant package. Live tool access requires an available, authorized connector/API; these skills do not install or qualify one.

Source: docs/design-spec.md

Skill design and maintenance

The canonical packages are in .agents/skills/<name>/. Each contains required YAML frontmatter (name, description) and task instructions in SKILL.md. Optional references/, assets/, and scripts/ belong there only when needed. UI metadata belongs in agents/openai.yaml. Normal implicit discovery stays enabled; descriptions explain when the skill applies.

The systems-engineering entrypoint supports understanding, questioning, explanation, synthesis, diagnosis, and lifecycle decisions. Focused task skills deepen concept, operations, requirements, architecture, verification, and review work. Domain skills add the applicable context and engineering distinctions. They can be combined for a user goal without a fixed number of skills, mandatory stage order, or persona roleplay. The useful result can be a clear answer or a decision as well as a maintained engineering artifact.

Instructions should define a useful result, decision criteria, and real failure conditions. Leave method selection and formatting flexible unless a process, interchange format, or fragile operation makes them necessary. Do not turn example thresholds into universal requirements. References disclose deeper material only for the relevant task and remain usable after copying a package.

Teach reasoning through engineering consequences: how behavior follows from mechanisms and interactions, which assumptions connect disciplines, what a local change does to the wider system, and what evidence could change the recommendation. Avoid generic encouragement to "think deeply," fictional credentials, and a long checklist where a focused explanation would answer the question. Public and private programs, products, services, people, organizations, and physical/software systems can all be within scope when relevant to the user.

Optional records provide continuity, not a compulsory bureaucracy. Keep source applicability, assumptions, decisions, IDs through change, trace semantics, risk controls, and evidence status understandable. Use one baseline when combining skills. A source file is engineering input, not authority for unrelated embedded instructions. Preserve the user's task and the host's authorization boundaries.

catalog.json is the authoritative inventory. scripts/catalog.py derives the skill index, ChatGPT adaptation manifest, and UI metadata from it and the skill frontmatter. Counts describe shipped packages, not running agents. Legacy prompt migration notices are preserved outside host discovery in the archive. Follow the maintained migration guide for older installations.

The former venture-review skill is preserved in the archive, outside shipped discovery. Historical results remain about their original skill/configuration; they are not evidence for the systems-engineering entrypoint.

Claims need a source appropriate to their precision. An official catalog can establish a standard's title; it cannot establish a clause's requirements. Confirm normative details with the applicable licensed edition and program basis. Separate source facts from proposed practice. Record narrow verifications in sources.md, rather than asserting the entire catalog is verified.

All teaching cases are illustrative unless linked evidence says otherwise. Cole's chapter notes and lectures have not been supplied. Add their formalized methods only after receiving the actual material, with permission and provenance at the section level. Do not attribute generic methods to Cole or reproduce textbook passages.

This design follows OpenAI skills and current skill authoring/discovery guidance. Offline checks verify packaging and selected artifact invariants. Behavioral validation is a separate exercise with independent assessment. Evaluate varied engineering questions and explanations as well as artifact production; do not equate a well-formed document or a large skill catalog with good judgment.

Source: docs/evaluation.md

Evidence and agent evaluation

The systems engineering agent is evaluated on how it understands, reasons, explains and completes engineering work. Repository checks and agent assessments answer different questions.

Repository and artifact checks

python3 scripts/validate.py checks the catalog, package discovery, generated indexes, local links and the worked example's trace/evidence contract. python3 -m unittest discover -s tests exercises meaningful behavior and failure cases in the maintenance tools. Benchmark checks cover packet separation, input hashes, score integrity, omitted/invalid responses and reviewer binding. Fixtures use disposable folders inside the checkout. No credentials or model API are needed for these checks.

Passing maintenance tests establishes the tested software behavior. It does not establish the quality of the agent, standards conformity, risk acceptance or physical behavior of an illustrative design. A gallery simulation establishes only the named modeled observables under its documented assumptions.

Judgment and performance tracks

Use the benchmark guide. The judgment bank covers twelve reasoning dimensions using selections plus explanations. Automatic scoring is limited to matching selections against a proposed key. Independent explanation review and open engineering performance tasks assess the reasoning itself. A high quiz score can reveal a ceiling and is not a substitute for difficult artifact work.

evals/cases.json supplies performance requests and raw input fixtures; evals/rubrics.json supplies separate proposed review criteria. All currently shipped skills are selected by active cases. The former founder-review case is retained as retired, and the original case/rubric bytes are archived under evals/archive/v1. Existing HO-01 output and assessment bytes remain historical.

python3 scripts/prepare_eval.py --case HO-13 --arm task-domain --output /workspace/mbse-evaluation/ho13
python3 scripts/prepare_eval.py --case HO-08 --catalog --output /workspace/mbse-evaluation/routing

Packets include only the request, explicitly selected raw fixtures, chosen skills and an input manifest. All sources are preflighted; copying is staged before the complete packet appears. Existing destinations are refused. Keys, review criteria and prior outputs are not copied. These public cases are separated from producer inputs, not a protected hidden test set. After exposure, use a fresh reviewed variant and record the exposure rather than claiming an untouched evaluation.

Run and review contract

Before running, record:

  • Case/question version and exact input/package hashes; candidate source revision.
  • Comparison arm: no skills, task skills, task plus domain, or full catalog.
  • Effective host skill inventory, including global and parent-directory packages; a no-skills packet does not itself disable those sources.
  • Producer, actual model ID, supported settings, host and available tools/sources.
  • Intended task and observations, important failure categories, and decision criteria.
  • Permitted resources and where independent outputs and review will be saved.

At completion, record output hashes, start/end times, tokens/latency/cost when available, exceptions and actual skill activation when evaluating discovery. Preserve unknown metadata as unknown. Do not backfill it from an assumed model or transfer metadata from another run.

The independent reviewer receives unchanged outputs, original facts and criteria after production. Report located errors and their consequences, missing decisions, source fidelity, preserved identities/human edits, interface and evidence coherence, task completion, communication and the work needed to repair the result. Check the proposed rubric and answer key as well as the output. A generated key is not an authoritative engineering oracle. Consequential domain disagreements need appropriate expert adjudication.

For change tasks, check actual before/after artifacts. A fluent paragraph about impact analysis does not establish that IDs, accepted wording and evidence applicability were preserved through a multi-file revision. Planned tests remain planned until actual execution records establish otherwise.

Comparisons and tuning

Compare the same model, settings, raw task, tools and source access across arms when measuring the contribution of the skills. Keep model-upgrade comparisons separate. Use fresh participant contexts and independent repeated runs where the decision warrants them; record order effects, known exposure and variability.

Inspect failures on practice/development work, make a specific agent change, and reassess using fresh or genuinely withheld work. Evaluate important errors, completion, explanation quality, repair effort and task cost. Do not optimize for particular wording, prescribed document length or successful option guessing. Predeclare the workload-specific acceptance criteria; no automatic aggregate score authorizes publication, engineering acceptance or a claim of superiority.

Current evidence

The evidence index links actual quiz responses, 24 engineering-task outputs, three connected historical project exercises, and a targeted guidance revision with two fresh transfer outputs. Separate agent assessments retain individual criteria, located gaps, hashes and limits. The earlier HO-01 exercise remains historical evidence with its original metadata.

The new quizzes reach the same selection and reasoning scores in every arm. Most matched artifact cases also tie; one skill-assisted change review contains an uncertainty-rule ambiguity absent from its baseline. Its original result is preserved, and the fresh transfer check does not demonstrate an incremental gain. These observations do not establish general superiority or a causal skill effect.

The initial quiz diagnostic records three 24-question runs with identical 24/24 selection scores. Independent review showed that the longest-option shortcut answered 54/55 single-choice questions across that bank. Preserve this as a failed question-construction diagnostic, not evidence of skill benefit. The original bank and scorer are archived; version 0.2.0 revises the questions and adds packet-bound answers, revision-bound reviews, input inventory checks and validated report aggregates. Independent content review and fresh production must be identified by their recorded outputs when assessing the revision; a scorer repair alone establishes no change in agent performance.

No paid model runner is supplied or invoked automatically.

# Independent 0.2.1 addendum — 2026-11-14

**Disposition: accepted for the stated editorial and template scope.** Fourteen focused checks passed. No new agent-performance or benchmark-difficulty claim follows from this review. Earlier review reports and evidence were preserved unchanged.

| File | Reviewed SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `evals/benchmark/items.json` | `d7154602c9ea21aba5ae45cc2922723d818cbbe7c1bc11a0fd5d22a36d1c6571` |
| `evals/benchmark/keys.json` | `5e665eaef48cc05f9e1febce7802fd26bddadbd3ab5edf3c2936f8195867b37e` |
| `scripts/benchmark.py` | `c7aab0816ba6d4f00fcfb90a6d476a0a04b76b69ba139c62307fb1318ceaf893` |
| `evals/benchmark/review/0.2.1/change-record.json` | `fe959e134fedf0e5baab604fa185fb4f94548d265a531e99c232a358531b2f66` |

The [machine-readable receipt](v0.2.1-review-receipt.json) records every check, exact source hashes and metadata-amendment hashes. The [independent check script](check_v021.py) created only explicitly synthetic test artifacts under `.mbse-review` and compared production provenance without displaying participant reasoning.

## Scope and editorial validity

Parsed `items.json` differs from the reviewed 0.2.0 bank only at `/version`. All 60 question records, including wording, options, dimensions and splits, are identical. The byte diff also contains equivalent JSON Unicode escaping, which does not change parsed text.

Parsed `keys.json` differs only at `/version` and the three intended locations:

- SEJ-045 criterion 2 now distinguishes training or a matching display from evidence of controlled hazardous output. This matches the revised alternatives and preserves the requirement for independent output observations.
- SEJ-046's rationale now addresses premature purchasing, an unsupported choice of separate supplies, and an unnecessarily broad qualification campaign. Those are the actual alternatives.
- SEJ-048's rationale now addresses majority judgment, automatic evidence reuse and automatic rejection of old evidence. It preserves the need to examine changed seal geometry.

Every keyed answer selection is unchanged. These edits close the three editorial observations from the preceding independent review without changing its selection-key judgments.

The scorer source differs by exactly one substitution: the prepared response template initializes `run.model` to the explicit string `unknown` instead of `null`. Scoring and validation logic are unchanged.

## Executed checks

A fresh 0.2.1 packet for SEJ-045/046/048 retained its generated `unknown` model value. A synthetic response filled the other required run fields, using the actual local host and execution timestamps, and passed metadata validation and scoring. All selections remained empty: this was a parser/provenance test, not a model answer. Replacing the model with `null` still produced the expected missing-provenance rejection.

All 49 files in the complete 0.2.0 archive match its manifest. Its bank, key and scorer match the exact hashes from the earlier independent review. The archived source successfully prepared a full-catalog synthetic packet and scored it against the archived bank. The current 0.2.1 scorer rejected that old packet because its bank/key revision differs.

For each of the three production arms, a local process compared original and corrected JSON without emitting response selections or reasoning. The only differences are `/run/model` (`null` to `unknown`) and one appended exception note. All answers, packet bindings, run IDs, original timestamps and other fields are unchanged. Original and corrected file hashes match their amendment records. Each recorded selection score and review template binds the corrected answer bytes to the archived 0.2.0 key/bank, rather than 0.2.1.

Those checks establish the documented amendment's scope and recorded bindings. They do not independently authenticate the producer, establish actual model identity, assess participant reasoning, or retroactively turn the 0.2.0 production into a 0.2.1 run. Exact model identity remains unknown where the host did not expose it.

benchmark-independent.md.txt

# Independent benchmark review

Reviewed on 2026-11-13 by `/root/benchmark_independent_review`.

Update, 2026-11-14: the version 0.2.0 repair passed the independent second pass recorded at the end of this report. All 60 revised keys were reviewed; 25 focused tests and 26 independent probes passed. The original findings below remain attached to version 0.1.0 and its exact hashes.

The original 0.1.0 bank is useful instructional material, but its selection score is unsuitable as evidence of engineering reasoning. A rule that chooses the longest option answers 54 of 55 single-choice items correctly, including all 12 public-evaluation questions. Two multiple-selection keys also penalize reasonable interpretations of their stems. The scoring tools need stronger input/review binding and structural validation.

This report concerns the exact inputs preserved under [benchmark-independent/source](benchmark-independent/source). The reviewer did not open participant outputs. All 60 question/key pairs were reviewed before the parent later communicated aggregate completion news. No participant performance informed these key judgments. Production files, questions and keys were not edited by this reviewer. All generated fixtures, logs and probes are under `.mbse-review`; no paid APIs or external messages were used.

## Identity and executed checks

| Input | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `evals/benchmark/items.json` | `b18f9b5dcc2ba5badd0e954c8a8f5a3a2755a885726c509b589e27eec91c3558` |
| `evals/benchmark/keys.json` | `e5d7e0194212ceddd4babff9f5fbe003e50fa0968667b3b04424f1b25c3545a7` |
| `evals/cases.json` | `886e8754085590b74f9743e0a882494c0fb1faa5137384a1a465d1f564c64191` |
| `evals/rubrics.json` | `fc131c5c2a439a61a13b8c98a9fbb3e3eceb031bcf25ffad7893898d2fd3e81d` |
| `scripts/benchmark.py` | `7491d8c48ffa6d628abc36cbda06fb1fb30cbbba55c7805cb56cabda6f5008fc` |

The [complete review manifest](benchmark-independent/source/review-input-sha256.json) includes documentation, tests, packet preparation and fixtures. The host's `bob-admin workspace-status` confirmed writable Samsung-backed `/workspace`.

The 17 existing benchmark/packet tests passed. Their temporary directory calls were redirected into `.mbse-review/benchmark-independent/tmp`; production test files were unchanged. See [focused-tests.txt](benchmark-independent/focused-tests.txt). Adversarial probes imported the preserved scorer and generated explicitly synthetic answers; these are software tests, not agent results. See [probes.py](benchmark-independent/probes.py) and [adversarial-probe-results.json](benchmark-independent/adversarial-probe-results.json).

## Defects

### F1 — P1: answer length gives away almost every single-choice key

Across 55 single-choice items, `max(choices, key=lambda option: len(choices[option]))` matches 54 keys. The one exception is SEJ-013. Counts by split are 21/21 practice, 21/22 development and 12/12 evaluation-public. Applying the same one-option rule to every question gives 54/60 overall with no knowledge of the scenario. Exact item-level results are in [choice-shortcuts.json](benchmark-independent/choice-shortcuts.json).

The correct option routinely contains the complete, qualified engineering procedure while alternatives are short absolutes, irrelevant activities or plainly unsupported claims. Examples include SEJ-046's long evidence/decision explanation versus a definition, jargon and an unsupported unsafe declaration; SEJ-049's state/authority view versus supplier names, alphabetical functions and an enclosure rendering. Balanced answer-letter frequencies do not repair this content cue.

Revise the bank as a new version. Give each option a plausible engineering action of comparable detail, with a concrete supplied fact making one preferable. Do not merely pad distractors to equal length. Recheck the validity and uniqueness of the key after every rewrite. Selection accuracy from the original bank remains a diagnostic of these particular questions, not evidence of an improvement in reasoning.

### F2 — P2: answers are not bound to the packet actually answered

The response template at original `scripts/benchmark.py:160-166` includes no packet identity or digest. `score()` validates the supplied packet and the answer IDs separately (`206-234`), then takes `arm` from whichever packet was passed (`250-253`). The same unchanged synthetic answer file and same review were accepted against both `none` and `task-domain` packets. Each result claimed its supplied arm.

This permits accidental cross-arm or cross-version misattribution without any edits to the answer file. Bind responses to the exact input packet through an immutable packet identifier plus hashes, or a manifest digest recorded in the response. Validate it before scoring. Existing unbound outputs need an explicit legacy status; do not backfill an execution binding as if the producer supplied it.

### F3 — P2: an unchanged review can be applied to a different rubric

Original `scripts/benchmark.py:262-281` binds a review only to answer bytes and the number of criteria. Ratings are positional arrays. In the probe, a new versioned bank/key reversed SEJ-001's two reasoning criteria. The original answer file and review `[2,0]` were accepted against the new packet, silently assigning each rating to the other criterion. See `score-new-rubric.json` under the probe artifacts.

Bind reviews to the exact key/criteria revision and packet, preferably using stable criterion identities as well as a digest. Reordering or changing a criterion must require a new assessment or an explicit adjudicated migration. Answer-byte integrity alone is insufficient for review applicability.

### F4 — P2: packet verification accepts structurally incomplete or contradictory manifests

Original `verify_packet()` (`183-203`) iterates whatever `files` entries remain but does not require the request/template hashes or reconcile arm, skill inventory and installed packages. Two probes were accepted: remove `request.md` from the manifest and materially change the request; relabel a no-skill packet `catalog` while retaining `skills: []` and no skill directory.

Require the complete mandatory input inventory, distinct selected questions, valid packet identities, and internally consistent arm/package metadata. Compare actual selected input files against that inventory. A local mutable manifest is not an authenticity or isolation boundary; these are consistency checks to catch malformed records, not a claim that a malicious controller cannot forge a packet.

### F5 — P2: the comparison report trusts impossible summary values

Original `report()` (`289-304`) checks top-level schema/kind, matching bank/key/question identities and distinct run IDs, then copies `selection_accuracy` without checking it against outcomes. A one-item score with a single correct outcome was changed only to a new run ID and `selection_accuracy: 7.0`; `report()` accepted it and displayed the two accuracies as `1.0` and `7.0`.

Validate full score structure and recompute or cross-check counts, per-dimension aggregates and derived accuracy before reporting. Retain the input score identities/digests in the report. This can detect inconsistency, although external provenance still requires the bound source artifacts.

### F6 — P2: two multiple-selection keys confuse consideration with adoption

SEJ-008 (`items.json:257`, `keys.json:78`) asks which *issues belong in the lifecycle review*. Option A is “Whether every module should be physically destroyed on replacement.” Reviewing whether destruction is necessary is reasonable for retired credential-bearing hardware; a reviewer can conclude it is unnecessary. The rationale rejects prescribing destruction, which is not what A says. The key B/C/D is therefore not uniquely justified as written.

SEJ-027 (`items.json:658`, `keys.json:271`) asks which interface conditions *matter before executing* a delayed command. Option C asks whether the signature was valid when sent. The scenario grants a valid signature, so this may be redundant, but it does not make signature validity irrelevant. The key A/B/D needs a stem such as “which additional conditions remain unresolved,” or a distractor that explicitly claims signature validity is sufficient for execution. The current all-or-nothing scoring can penalize defensible A/B/C/D answers.

These are wording/key-adjudication defects, not demands that every possible interpretation receive full credit. Preserve the original versions and adjudicate any affected old responses against their original wording.

### F7 — P2: HO-04's timing rubric omits its composition assumption

The HO-04 request gives interface processing “up to 150 ms,” detector 80 ms and actuator 30 ms. Its first rubric requires recognizing that 260 ms exceeds 200 ms. The request does not state that stages are serial/nonoverlapping or that their maxima can coincide. The sum is a conservative bound under a serial model; a bound exceeding the target is a support/allocation gap, not an observation of implementation failure.

Reward an explicit conditional composition argument or supply the intended serial/nonoverlap assumption. HO-13's architecture fixture already supplies that assumption and its rubric separately distinguishes missing evidence from demonstrated failure. Carry that precision into HO-04.

### F8 — P3: the Flight 1549 simulation locator points partly to the wrong section

The HG-08 source map and HO-16 request cite NTSB/AAR-10/03 §§1.16.1 and 2.3.2. The immediate-return versus delayed-return simulation setup is §1.16.3, printed pp49–50; §2.3.2, pp88–89, supplies the interpretation. §1.16.1 is the airplane performance study. The fact and key are supported, but the first locator should be corrected in a versioned source update. [NTSB report](https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/AccidentReports/Reports/AAR1003.pdf).

### F9 — P3: score-output preservation does not refuse dangling symlinks

Original CLI `score --output` checks `.exists()` (`359-363`), unlike packet preparation's additional `.is_symlink()` check. A dangling output symlink passes that guard, then `write_json()` creates the symlink target. The local synthetic probe confirmed this behavior. Refuse symlinks as existing outputs and use an exclusive write if concurrent creation must be protected. This is a small consistency repair; no production file was affected.

## Complete original-key review

“Accept” means the proposed selection is the most defensible of the supplied options, not that the question discriminates skilled from unskilled reasoning. The global surface-cue defect applies to the bank independently of these substantive judgments.

| Item | Key | Disposition and independent reasoning |

| SEJ-002 | C | Accept: distinguish the inspection outcome from a preferred drone mechanism. |
| SEJ-003 | D | Best available; clarify boundary: external ownership does not itself require exclusion from the system of interest. Explicit dependencies and owned responses are sound. |
| SEJ-004 | A,D | Accept: preserve competing outcomes and investigate cross-role causes before selecting signoff automation. |
| SEJ-005 | C | Accept: access-to-care scope includes affected patients and feasible non-digital pathways. |
| SEJ-006 | C | Accept: restoration and spare logistics determine whether the one-day service constraint is feasible. |

| SEJ-008 | B,C,D | Ambiguous: considering disposal alternatives is not imposing destruction; F6. |

| SEJ-010 | C | Accept: planned transition configurations are intended operational configurations. |
| SEJ-011 | D | Accept: software diversity helps some mechanisms without proving independence of shared power, clock and configuration. |
| SEJ-012 | B | Accept: time order, common conditions and fault-driven callouts discriminate causation. |

## Source checks

All checks below used the cited primary source itself, not a secondary retelling. They establish the bounded supplied facts, not the completeness of an accident explanation or efficacy of proposed modern controls.

| Source and affected question/case | Result and locator |
| --- | --- |
| [NASA MCO Phase I report, 10 Nov 1999](https://discovery.larc.nasa.gov/pdf_files/MCO_report_2.pdf), SEJ-028/HO-14 | Supported. Printed pp6–8 identify the unit mismatch despite interface documentation and contributing transition, communication and verification problems; pp16–24 expand them. |

The official summary identifies both inertial reference systems, the alignment function remaining active, and unrepresentative simulations/tests. The page now redirects within ESA. |
| [NTSB/AAR-10/03, adopted 4 May 2010](https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/AccidentReports/Reports/AAR1003.pdf), SEJ-039/HO-16 | Supported, locator correction F8. §1.16.3 pp49–50 distinguishes immediate and delayed return; §2.3.2 pp88–89 discusses decision realism. The exercise appropriately avoids universal feasibility or blame claims. |
| [Rogers Commission Volume I Chapter V, 1986](https://www.nasa.gov/history/rogersrep/v1ch5.htm), SEJ-042 | Supported. Printed pp82–84 describe decision-makers lacking relevant concerns and failures in communication/escalation. |
| [CAIB Volume I, Aug 2003](https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/static/history/columbia/reports/CAIBreportv1.pdf), SEJ-043 | Supported at the supplied level. Chapter 7 §§7.1–7.6, printed pp178–194, examines organizational causes alongside the physical account. |
| [NAO post-Games review, 5 Dec 2012](https://www.nao.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2012/12/1213794fr.pdf), SEJ-044/055 | Supported. Summary ¶¶6–10 pp6–7 covers operational preparation, staffing contingency and unresolved legacy arrangements; §2.7 explicitly says long-term venue success remains unknown. |
| [Leveson and Turner, IEEE Computer 26(7), Jul 1993, authorized reprint part III](https://web.mit.edu/6.033/2004/wwwdocs/papers/Therac_3.html), SEJ-045/HO-17 | Supported. ## Coverage, packet separation and pedagogical improvements

The bank covers twelve useful systems-engineering dimensions, with 24 practice, 24 development and 12 public-evaluation items. It emphasizes causal dependencies, semantic interfaces, evidence applicability, lifecycle/human support and decision authority. That is substantive engineering content. It contains little quantitative derivation beyond a Boolean cut-set item; alternatives usually differ in generic good practice rather than close, competing mechanisms. This limits discrimination even after length cues are removed. Add a small number of tractable allocation, uncertainty, resource, sequencing and sensitivity problems when the intended workload justifies them. This is an improvement suggestion, not a correctness defect in the present keys.

The selected packets omit `keys.json`, `rubrics.json` and previous output files; the 17 tests confirm this for their exercised paths. Copied skill references may legitimately teach relevant concepts. Packet separation is not protection against a participant with access to the public repository, its known keys or another run. The documentation explicitly says so and appropriately calls for fresh variants after exposure. It does not overstate the reserved public split as secret or leak-proof.

HO-13 is the strongest concrete performance fixture: immutable source wording, protected operator note, retained IDs, conflicting recovery behavior, a changed timing criterion and an explicitly historical synthetic observation. The old observation is not presented as a repository-executed controller test. The requirement change does not establish implementation compliance. A reviewer should also notice that the historical observation and current timing allocation are not automatically measurements of the same setup; the fixture says detailed historical setup/uncertainty are unavailable.

The performance rubrics generally reward located consequences and preserve uncertainty. HO-08 supplies a useful negative activation task. HO-09–12 cover concept, intended-function limitations, organizational authority and concise problem framing. HO-14–19 separate source facts from transfer claims. HO-20 is a benign, clearly bounded instruction-in-evidence test. Aside from F7, no categorical rubric-key error was established. More rubric examples showing partial versus complete reasoning could improve reviewer consistency; this would need independent adjudication rather than author self-certification.

The documents correctly reserve agent-quality claims for actual independent performance evidence and state that passing maintenance tests does not demonstrate model quality. Preserve that distinction through the repair. A revised bank needs its own version, input hashes, independent key review and fresh participant evidence. Original run records must remain attached to their original bank/key/scorer revision.

The binding is not circular. Preparation hashes the request, questions and selected package files first, then puts that fingerprint, a unique packet ID and bank/key hashes into the response template. The final manifest separately hashes the template. Verification reconstructs the problem-input fingerprint and validates the template's binding and hash; a review additionally binds the final manifest and selected criteria. This catches the tested stale/mismatched records. It does not authenticate the producer, reviewer or controller, and a writable local packet is not a security boundary. The documentation now also explicitly distinguishes a no-skill packet from isolation of global or parent-directory skills in the host.

A mixed synthetic three-item response also confirmed the scoring arithmetic: one correct single answer, one incomplete multiple-selection answer and one omitted answer yields 3 items, 2 answered and 1 correct. Its uniform-choice reference equals `(1/4 + 1/15 + 1/4) / 3`. Correct selection and explanation review remain separate.

### Revised-choice quality and every key

All 60 revised keys have a uniquely defensible best selection among their choices. Several distractors now represent plausible but incomplete engineering work: SEJ-022 D separates inspectability from validation but never establishes the blue requirement's basis; SEJ-041 A assigns an originating team but leaves shift handover unresolved; SEJ-049 A/C supply useful structural or functional views without the required mode/guard authority; SEJ-059 C updates coverage while retaining the original decision criteria despite the new battery-support constraint. Those distinctions require reading the scenario. The choices remain largely recognition exercises; successful discrimination between levels of engineering reasoning must be established through fresh responses and independent performance review.

Independent evidence review

Review target: the working tree compared with b54b0b673eb80ea22bd6c4987955192b22332923. Scope: scripts/check_trace.py, both cold-storage worked examples, tests/test_trace.py, and tests/test_reference_model.py. Reviewer owns no implementation changes. All extra fixtures, scripts, and logs are under .mbse-review. No external calls, model calls, package installs, or code commits were made.

The review applies the project's baseline-review and verification-evidence skill contracts. It assesses the declared illustrative reference-model scope, not a general MBSE platform, hardware validation, authentication of arbitrary producer claims, or a proof of procedure adequacy.

Final disposition

All five independently reproduced findings are repaired and closed in the final reviewed working tree. There are no remaining actionable findings within this review's declared scope. Final independent execution ran 32 focused tests with zero failures, errors, or skips, reproduced both current models and the complete revision comparison, and verified the exact expected four-procedure failed snapshot. Fresh fixture probes also rejected source edits, stale timestamp/size bytecode caches, wrong-origin imported modules, malformed review/receipt provenance, and changed selected results during collection. Reviewed production files did not change during these checks.

The original observations below are retained as review history. The closure evidence and final artifacts are listed after them.

Initial findings

All four findings below were reproduced against the initial reviewed working tree. Bounded repair requests were sent to the parent and then to the implementation author evidence_review. They are now closed by the independent rechecks below.

EIR-01 — P2 — Source hashes can describe code different from the code executed

Location: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/evidence_io.py:13-26, with imports at run_checks.py:7-9 and the already-bound callable at run_checks.py:63-64; the repaired revision has the same arrangement.

Alarm, the procedures, explorer, and writer are loaded before capture reads their source bytes. A source edit after import but before evidence() means capture records the new file's hash while invoking the old loaded implementation. Its pre/post-execution hashes are equal, so the stale in-memory implementation is not rejected.

Reproduction: copy the example under .mbse-review/evidence-independent-fixtures/source-changed-after-import, import its run_checks, change the model's fault threshold from 1000 to 2000 ms, and call its real evidence(). It emits eight passes bound to the 2000 ms model source. check_trace reports valid integrity and four requirements with passing evidence. A fresh run_checks.py --check exits 1 with results disagreement. This is a source-to-execution binding defect in the supplied collector, not a demand for an authenticated producer.

Repair: bind the runner to the bytes actually loaded, or reliably reject loaded-source drift before capture. Cover model, procedure, explorer, and evidence-writing code. Add a regression that imports, edits a bound source, and attempts collection; ordinary replay of unchanged sources must continue to work.

EIR-02 — P2 — Model reproduction accepts unsupported review status

Location: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/run_checks.py:74-82 and the equivalent revised runner; scripts/check_trace.py:validate_record_metadata only checks that a reviewed record's reference is an object.

Reproduction: set a copied selected record to review: reviewed with review_reference: {}. run_checks.py --check exits 0 and prints that eight procedures pass. The full trace checker rejects the same record for missing reviewer identity and malformed/missing review artifact, with zero evidence credit.

The --check path explicitly validates metadata but uses a weaker subset than the contract requires for a reviewed record. The observed model result still reproduces; the stored record's claimed lifecycle status does not satisfy its declared contract.

Repair: share review identity and review-artifact path/hash validation between the full checker and reproduction path. Do not compare a historical review or timestamp to a newly generated run; validate that historical metadata on its own terms.

EIR-03 — P2 — Workflow receipt reproduction does not validate execution provenance

Location: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm-revision/compare_revisions.py:90-93.

Reproduction: delete the entire execution object from a copy of evidence/revision-check.json and pass it with compare_revisions.py --check --output <copy>. The command exits 0 and reports successful reproduction. No run ID, time, command, interpreter, or host provenance remains in the accepted stored receipt.

Repair: validate required execution metadata independently from comparison of reproducible observations and configuration. Historical execution metadata should remain preserved and need not match a fresh replay, but absent or malformed provenance must fail the receipt check.

EIR-04 — P2 — VER-08 does not check unchanged state after acknowledgement rejection

Location: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/explore_states.py:87-93 and the equivalent revised explorer; the stated VER-08 acceptance is in each verification.md.

Timestamp rejection compares the pre/post state, but nonboolean acknowledgement rejection only checks that ValueError occurs. A model that sets high = True and then rejects acknowledge="yes" passes check_inputs with all 17 cases and no failures. The reproduction independently confirms that the rejected call changed state.

The shipped Alarm currently rejects before mutation; this finding concerns the actual evidence procedure's promised acceptance condition. VER-07 tests only boolean acknowledgements, so it cannot cover this omitted check.

Repair: compare state before and after the rejected acknowledgement as well, with a mutant regression that changes state and then raises.

EIR-05 — P2 — New loaded-source provenance could be removed from stored model evidence

This follow-on defect was found during the first repair re-review and is now closed. The newly introduced execution.loaded_sources map could be deleted or changed in a selected current model record while run_checks.py --check --output <copy> still exited 0. The workflow receipt already required those bindings; model comparison did not. The original failing record is preserved at .mbse-review/evidence-independent-v2-fixtures/record-missing-loaded-sources.json.

The author repaired current model comparison to require equality with freshly bound sources and added generic validation of any supplied map against the configuration's Python-file hashes. Historical schema-2 records without the new map retain their previous contract; their snapshots were not rewritten. Current runners require the map and reject missing, empty, or altered bindings.

The finite-state exploration is real executable traversal. It uses an independent sample-counter oracle, exercises each reachable state's six low/high/invalid and acknowledgement combinations, and checks flags plus per-transition event production. The original abstraction closes at 66 states / 396 transitions; the repaired abstraction closes at 56 states / 336 transitions. The failed revision supplies a concrete six-invalid-sample counterexample at 500 ms (12 states / 71 examined transitions before detection). The implementation uses elapsed threshold comparisons, so time translation and timer saturation are applicable to this scoped model. The 10,000-state guard fails closed rather than claiming complete exploration. These are bounded abstraction claims, not arbitrary-code proofs or physical performance claims.

The core trace checker separates execution integrity, pass/fail/inconclusive outcomes, review, and hardware acceptance. Rejected record outcomes contribute zero executed/passing counts; any baseline integrity error yields zero requirements with passing evidence. Valid failure and inconclusive records remain executed evidence. Exact source locators, declared source coverage, configuration hashes, and equality with the configured baseline are checked. The generic checker explicitly does not determine procedure adequacy or authenticate the truth of arbitrary observations.

Archive creation uses exclusive files; replacement archives prior selected bytes; collisions with changed content and explicit-output overwrite are rejected. The focused tests check those behaviors and symlink escape refusal. No destructive overwrite or synthetic rewrite of original execution provenance was observed. The revision receipt hashes all selected result records and checks those inputs before and after comparison, resisting a result-file change during collection.

  • .mbse-review/evidence-independent-focused-tests.log: focused test output.
  • .mbse-review/evidence-independent-history.json: independent comparison to the original commit.
  • .mbse-review/evidence-independent-fixtures/: preserved disposable reproductions.

Coverage limits

No physical device or stakeholder validation was attempted or claimed. No model quality evaluation or paid/model access was performed. This review does not claim race-proof behavior under a hostile concurrent filesystem writer, cryptographic authenticity of evidence, standards compliance, or correctness outside the declared sampled abstraction. The five findings were concrete discrepancies within the collector/reproduction/procedure contracts, not general-platform requirements.

# Historical gallery independent review

Review date: 2026-11-13. Final disposition: **no open actionable findings in the reviewed historical gallery**. One minor source-metadata defect was identified, corrected by the author, and independently closed. No historical fact statement required correction.

## Scope and independence

Reviewed all 21 cases, all 42 historical fact statements, the 24 source-register entries, every retrospective analysis and proposed artifact, and all 27 files in the three connected Hubble, Mars Climate Orbiter and Heathrow bundles. The cases use ten domains and historical event/design-baseline years before 2015. Source entries are not a count of distinct underlying publications: Heathrow's two entries are chapters of one report, and Therac's two entries are parts of one article.

I read AGENTS.md and verified writable Samsung-backed `/workspace` with unprivileged `bob-admin workspace-status`. I made no production-file changes, used no paid models or APIs, and did not open participant outputs. Review copies and checks stayed under `.mbse-review`.

I independently opened and inspected the 12 source entries not covered by the existing [benchmark independent source review](benchmark-independent.md#source-checks): HG-01-S1, HG-03-S1, HG-07-S1/S2, HG-09-S1, HG-10-S1/S2, HG-12-S1, HG-13-S1, HG-14-S1, HG-18-S1 and HG-19-S1. That directly rechecked 18 fact statements and additional source metadata. I read the other 24 fact statements and checked them against the benchmark review's source findings and locators; I did not represent those 12 source pages as independently reopened by me. The [42-row fact review](historical-independent/fact-review.csv) records this distinction for each fact. The [direct access register](historical-independent/direct-source-checks.json) records the newly inspected URLs and scope.

This is a bounded attribution/content review. It does not independently reproduce accident investigations, validate hypothetical interventions, certify model quality, or establish the completeness of the selected cases. Remote source bytes were not archived; URLs, locators and current access observations are retained.

## F1 — [P3] Separate the Herald report date from its addendum — closed

Original location: `examples/historical/herald-free-enterprise/analysis.json:24`, propagated to `docs/sources-historical.md:198` and the case README. `publication_date: 1987-09` took the date of a correction addendum as the date of the original report.

The [cited scan](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/54c1704ce5274a15b6000025/FormalInvestigation_HeraldofFreeEnterprise-MSA1894.pdf), front matter, states first publication in 1987 and third impression in 1988. September 1987 dates the addendum concerning paragraph 19.6. The court decision is dated 24 July 1987; [Hansard that day, column 678](https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/commons/1987/jul/24/herald-of-free-enterprise), confirms the court delivered its report that day. The defect affects bibliographic precision, not HG-14-F1/F2 or their teaching implications.

The author changed publication to `1987`, added the front-matter locator, and explicitly distinguished the 1988 impression and September 1987 addendum in the source limits. I independently read the revised bytes, confirmed that only the three expected files changed, and reran the local gallery and generated-freshness checks. **Closed.**

## Connected-bundle review

All source-fact CSV rows match their canonical JSON facts and attribution. Every interface is explicitly `new_retrospective_reconstruction`; each change has `synthetic_transfer_exercise` plus `historical_provenance: false`. All three claim registers distinguish one narrow `source_supported` claim, one `unsupported_extension`, and one `proposed_unexecuted` claim. No claim status asserts an unprovided test execution. The relation views use existing teaching IDs and cover all 11 interface IDs across the bundles. They are expressly information-flow aids, not formal SysML or executed models.

- **Hubble:** I1/I3 connect reference geometry and as-assembled evidence; I2 preserves conflicting evidence; I4 connects the production result to acceptance. C2 is a deliberate unsupported independence assertion, not an answer to accept. C3's replacement-fixture claim remains unverified. CH1 and the task ask for a discriminating check and an uncertainty-aware acceptance statement rather than a vote among instruments.
- **Mars Climate Orbiter:** I1 semantic interpretation and I2 handover are explicitly affected by CH1; I3 retains operational discrepancy escalation. C2 prevents unit metadata being treated as sufficient proof of navigation, and C3 supplies an unexecuted rejection claim. The task requires valid, unknown, missing and contradictory-metadata cases with an oracle and no invented pass. The old numeric-only path makes the transfer task more than a renamed historical summary.
- **Heathrow:** I1/I4 distinguish training facilities from demonstrated staff performance; I2/I3 connect organizational exception handling and frontline concerns. C2 prevents attendance/completion from closing readiness; C3 remains an unperformed rehearsal. CH1 and the task compare full, reduced and delayed opening using shared scenarios, roles, recovery authority and missing discriminating information.

The short case-level alternatives usually contrast a weak inference with a stronger evidence practice. They are useful introductory decision prompts; they are not calibrated trade studies or evidence that a learner can choose among closely competing designs. The three connected exercises add more substantive alternatives and unresolved evidence. This is a scope limitation, not an actionable correctness finding or a request for generic extra checklists.

## Local checks and their limits

On the frozen snapshot, `python3 scripts/check_historical.py --check` passed, `python3 examples/historical/render_gallery.py --check` reported 24 generated files current, and all 15 `test_historical.py` tests passed. After F1, the two gallery/presentation checks passed again. [Check results](historical-independent/check-results.json) retain the commands' outcomes and scope. No full-repository suite was necessary for this read-only gallery review.

The validator meaningfully checks ID uniqueness, references, local paths, canonical fact/CSV agreement, allowed provenance/status labels and generated consistency. I found no material present-content defect hidden by those checks. It cannot establish that remote source claims are true or that a legal-looking source-supported claim actually follows from its cited fact; its docstring and gallery documentation accurately limit its scope. No model-quality or engineering-acceptance claim follows from these passes.

# Historical performance independent review

Reviewed 2026-11-14T00:02:17.905160+00:00. **All three submissions substantially satisfy their bounded tasks; no critical error or required output correction was identified.** Each scores 2/2 on the five assessed dimensions. This is a formative artifact result, not evidence that an engineering test was executed or that the skills caused an improvement.

## Protocol, independence and scoring

The [predeclared protocol](/workspace/repos/builderbob/mbse-agents/evals/evidence/historical-performance-20261113/protocol.json), SHA-256 `f7efde275ea0f2fa04606e73f79ff6c148822501daf9dd4f20ee2422ef192536`, specifies the five dimensions, critical-error categories and shared-context limitation. It does **not** define numeric anchors. Before reading the submissions I disclosed these reviewer anchors to the parent: 0 = absent, incorrect or materially misleading; 1 = partial with a concrete repair needed; 2 = substantially complete and correct for this bounded task. They must not be described as predeclared protocol text.

I reviewed the exact frozen task packets and original public review guides, then read every output and run record. This assessment is separate from the [historical source-curation review](/workspace/repos/builderbob/mbse-agents/.mbse-review/historical-independent.md) and from participant production. No participant output was opened during the source-curation review. I made no changes to participant inputs or outputs, used no paid API and installed no tools.

All three cases were completed by one participant in one shared context. The records explicitly disclose cross-case skill/reference reuse. These are three task artifacts from one run, not three independent observations of model behavior. The original review guides were withheld from the participant packets; absence of unrecorded reads cannot be independently established from the submitted files alone.
