Domain-model source checks

Checked 2026-11-13. These checks support methods and narrow corrections. They do not validate the twenty designs, their parameter values or their complete standards bases. Each example's source-review.md and review-status.json retain individual candidate requirement sources and their unresolved applicability.

Source Edition and inspected locator Supported use and limit
NASA Fault Tree Handbook with Aerospace Applications Version 1.1, August 2002; Chapter 7, printed pp. 81–84; Appendix A, pp. 158–161 Boolean minimal cuts and quantitative interpretation. The supplied examples use exhaustive disjoint-state sums; no NASA parameter values are transplanted into the gallery. The handbook does not establish these authored events or independence assumptions.
FAA AC 25.1309-1B August 30, 2024; §§7.4 and 7.6, printed pp. 7-2 and 7-5–7-6; purpose on cover The assessment considers common causes and exposure/flight context. A product of several per-hour rates is not itself a valid average probability per flight hour. The AC describes an acceptable means and does not by itself approve an aircraft design or make synthetic demand probabilities equivalent to a flight-hour objective.

The MIL-STD-882E copy on the US Army site returned 502; the DAU risk-management brief returned 403 on direct retrieval. Their search snippets were insufficient for a current clause-level authority determination. The GCS now leaves authority, delegation and numerical risk allocation tied to the actual program basis; it does not assert the former unverified DASD(SE) chain or a universal 1e-6/FH target.

Licensed SAE, ISO, IEC and ARINC text was not supplied. Existing clause references remain candidate citations in claim-level registers. Retained design targets, including the steering example's 50 ms switchover, are proposed project values until their source and applicability are established. They are not discarded to make verification easier. New executable models test explicitly authored logic and parameter hypotheses; physical and program evidence remains to be obtained.

HG-21: San Bruno: preserve the provenance of configuration data

Historical year: 2010. Case.

HG-21-S1 — NTSB Pipeline Accident Report PAR-11/01

  • Publication: 2011-08-30.

Reuse and maintenance

Paraphrases are compact; no long excerpts or publisher illustrations are copied. The authored analyses, artifacts, and hypothetical variants are new teaching material. They are not original requirements, approved changes, calibrated models, or evidence that a counterfactual intervention would succeed.

When a link changes, preserve its source identity and locator, record the new access observation, and review the affected claims before replacing the URL. Do not silently substitute a secondary narrative for an unavailable original.

Historical exploratory domain questions

Use the systems engineering judgment benchmark for current practice, performance cases and recorded assessment.

These prompts came from the previous collection. Their former "correct answer" prose was not validated and has been removed. Use them as exploratory questions, not an answer oracle, score, or demonstration of expert experience. Verify exact claims against the applicable primary source and adopted edition. Current public exercise inputs and reviewer criteria are separated under evals; see evaluation.

AQ-1: ARP4761 vs ARP4761A CMA Treatment Differences

Our safety team is updating from ARP4761 to ARP4761A. How does the treatment of Common Mode Analysis change, and what new method does 4761A introduce that 4761 did not explicitly include?

AQ-2: DO-331 Model-Based Development Supplement Applicability Rules

We are using Simulink models for both requirements capture and auto-code generation. Does DO-331 apply to both uses, and at what point does DO-178C alone become insufficient?

AQ-3: SOI #1 Through #4 Progression and Baselining

We just passed SOI #2. Our DER is asking whether the Software Requirements are now formally baselined or whether that happened at SOI #1. Which is correct, and what specifically gets baselined at each SOI?

AQ-4: DAL Allocation Reduction via Architectural Mitigation (ARP4754A Section 5.2.4)

Our FHA assigned a function as DAL A. The lead architect says we can reduce the implementation to DAL C on each side if we use a dissimilar dual-channel architecture. Is this correct, and what constraints apply?

AQ-5: DO-330 Tool Qualification vs DO-178C Tool Qualification Overlap

We have a requirements management tool and a code coverage tool. Our QA team says both need DO-330 qualification. Is that correct, and how does DO-330 tool qualification differ from what DO-178C Section 12.2 already requires?

DQ-1: DoDAF 2.02 Data Model vs Viewpoint Presentation (AV-2 vs Ad Hoc Glossaries)

Our program manager wants an AV-2 that lists all acronyms and definitions. Is that what AV-2 is for, and what actually belongs in AV-2 under DoDAF 2.02?

DQ-2: SV-5a Completeness Checking for Unallocated Requirements

We have completed our SV-5a (Operational Activity to Systems Function Traceability Matrix). How do we use it to verify completeness, and what does an empty row or column indicate?

DQ-3: JCIDS Disestablishment (2025) and Transition to MEIA/JROC Prioritization

We are writing a requirements document and referencing JCIDS as our requirements framework. Our government lead says JCIDS has been disestablished. What replaced it, and how does this affect our ICD/CDD/CPD document hierarchy?

DQ-4: DI-SESS-81495 (SEMP) vs DI-SESS-81748 (SDD) Scope Boundaries

Our program requires both a Systems Engineering Management Plan (DI-SESS-81495) and a System/Subsystem Design Description (DI-SESS-81748). The new engineer thinks the SDD should describe the engineering process. Where does the SEMP end and the SDD begin?

DQ-5: MIL-STD-882E Severity vs Probability Matrix for Software-Intensive Systems

Our safety engineer built a 5x5 risk matrix per MIL-STD-882E with probability levels A through E on one axis and severity categories I through IV on the other. For a purely software function, how do we assign the probability level, and what is the common mistake teams make?

UQ-1: ASIL Decomposition (Part 9) vs ASIL Tailoring -- When Each Applies

Our system architect wants to reduce the ASIL on a software component from ASIL D to ASIL B by "tailoring." Our functional safety manager says we need to use ASIL decomposition instead. Who is correct, and what is the difference?

UQ-2: Freedom from Interference Arguments for Mixed-ASIL Partitions

We have an ASIL D function and an ASIL QM function sharing the same microcontroller. What do we need to demonstrate, and what is the most commonly overlooked failure mode in freedom-from-interference arguments?

UQ-3: ISO 21448 SOTIF Boundary with ISO 26262 -- Sensor Perception Failures

Our ADAS camera system sometimes fails to detect pedestrians in low-light conditions. Is this an ISO 26262 functional safety issue or an ISO 21448 SOTIF issue? Where exactly is the boundary?

UQ-4: AUTOSAR Classic vs Adaptive Platform Selection for ASIL D

We are designing an ASIL D autonomous driving platform. Should we use AUTOSAR Classic or AUTOSAR Adaptive, and what is the safety argument difference between them?

UQ-5: ISO 26262 Part 6 vs Part 8 Software Development -- When You Need Both

Our project is developing safety-related software. We are following ISO 26262 Part 6. Our assessor says we also need to comply with Part 8. What does Part 8 add that Part 6 does not cover?

MQ-1: IEC 62304 Software Safety Class vs SIL Concept Differences

Our regulatory specialist keeps referring to our IEC 62304 Software Safety Class C as "SIL 3." Are these equivalent, and what is the fundamental difference?

MQ-2: FDA QMSR Alignment to ISO 13485:2016 vs Legacy 21 CFR 820 QSR

Our quality team is still working to the legacy 21 CFR 820 QSR structure. When does the transition to QMSR take effect, and what are the key structural differences they need to prepare for?

MQ-3: Basic vs Enhanced Software Documentation Levels Replacing Level of Concern

Our predicate device used the "Level of Concern" (Minor, Moderate, Major) framework for FDA software documentation. Our new 510(k) submission needs to follow the current guidance. What replaced Level of Concern, and how does it change our documentation package?

MQ-4: EU MDR 2017/745 Annex II Technical Documentation vs FDA DHF Structure

We are pursuing both FDA clearance and EU MDR CE marking for the same device. Our regulatory team says the FDA Design History File and the EU MDR Technical Documentation (Annex II) serve the same purpose. Is that accurate, and where do they diverge?

MQ-5: SOUP Management Under IEC 62304 vs FDA Expectations

We are using an open-source RTOS and a third-party image processing library in our Class C medical device software. IEC 62304 calls these SOUP. What does the standard require for SOUP management, and where do FDA expectations go beyond the standard?

Source: docs/workflows.md

Work through a systems engineering question

Start with the question, the system, and the decision the user needs to make. The result may be an explanation, a better question, a diagnosis, a comparison, or an engineering baseline. Use mbse-systems-engineering for an open problem or connected work that needs reasoning across tasks and disciplines. Use a focused task directly when its purpose is already clear. Add a domain skill when its operating context or assurance basis changes the analysis.

For an older prompt-based installation, use the migration guide to select current packages and preserve existing project instructions.

User goal Task skill Useful input Reviewable result
Understand a system or reason through a connected problem mbse-systems-engineering Question, observations, context, available sources Explained system understanding, synthesis, recommendation, or consequential next question
Explore a system idea mbse-system-concept Problem, desired outcome, constraints Alternatives, boundaries, feasibility tests, recommendation
Explain how a system will be used mbse-conops Stakeholders, environment, mission Operations concept, responsibilities, lifecycle, open decisions
Walk through an operation mbse-operational-scenarios Actors, trigger, context Normal and exception flows, modes, exchanges, evaluation conditions
Establish a requirement baseline mbse-requirements Needs, scenarios, constraints Identified requirements, rationale, source links, acceptance conditions
Allocate behavior to an architecture mbse-architecture Requirements, functions, interfaces Alternatives, allocations, contracts, trade decisions, unresolved risks
Plan verification and evidence mbse-verification-evidence Baseline, risks, available methods Procedures, criteria, configuration, trace, evidence gaps
Challenge a baseline or change mbse-baseline-review Artifacts and review decision Located findings, impact, repair options, disposition

Choose the work by its purpose

A concept asks which way of delivering the outcome is worth pursuing. A ConOps asks how people and systems will operate together. A scenario follows a specific trigger, sequence, exception, and outcome. They can inform each other, but a request to explain one outage does not require all three documents.

Architecture work develops or explains how the system is organized and why its interactions should produce the required behavior. Baseline review challenges an existing argument or change. Verification/evidence work asks what an observation can establish and what remains untested. An unclear requirement may first need discussion of stakeholder intent before a polished replacement.

Domain choice follows applicability. Aerospace separates aircraft and space program bases; defense includes mission, organizational, acquisition, and sustainment constraints; automotive includes driver, vehicle, and field context; medical-device work begins with intended use and clinical workflow; electronics addresses the detailed physical and HW/SW assumptions. For a medical-device FPGA, combine the device context with electronics when both affect the question. Do not load every domain because a system contains software or a sensor.

Connect sustained work

For a full workflow, carry the same IDs and assumptions from needs through requirements, functions, components, interfaces, verification, and evidence. Establish authoritative input paths/revisions and one shared baseline before combining results. Reconcile specialist terminology, units, timing references, operating conditions, and responsibilities. A domain contribution refines that baseline; it does not create a separate version of the same requirements. Feed architecture-derived requirements and test failures back into the earlier artifacts. A diagram cannot close a verification gap. Verification asks whether the specified requirements are met; validation asks whether the system serves stakeholder needs in the intended use context.

For a small task, produce the relevant artifact directly. For sustained work, maintain a brief decision and assumption log so a later session can continue from the actual baseline. Ask about missing facts that could change the answer; make labeled provisional assumptions for independent work. Scale artifact depth to the decision, system risk, and user's chosen process.

Record splits, merges, replacements, and retirements without recycling IDs or silently inheriting evidence. A useful handoff identifies the source revision, changed artifacts, decisive rationale, affected IDs, checks actually performed, and unresolved decisions with owners. For optional record shapes and an illustrative connected thread, see the core skill's engineering records and connected work.

Example requests

Use $mbse-systems-engineering to explain why our proposed staffing and recovery concept conflicts with the architecture team's assumptions. Identify the decisions that need to change and give a recommendation grounded in the supplied operating notes. Keep the answer useful to both teams.

Use $mbse-requirements and $mbse-architecture on our cold-storage alarm brief. Carry source IDs into measurable requirements and component allocations. Continue through verification planning and run the local reference-model checks. Deliver a linked baseline, executed evidence with its configuration, and open hardware validation work. Save reviewable artifacts in the project workspace.

See the worked example and model setup. This repository supplies instructions and offline maintenance tools. It does not supply an MBSE engine or certification authority.

Source: evals/benchmark/README.md

Systems engineering judgment exercises

Start with the benchmark guide for practice, isolated agent packets, independent explanation review and comparisons.

items.json contains public questions, reasoning dimensions, split assignments, selected skills and primary-source locators. keys.json contains proposed selections, explanations and reviewer criteria. Keep the latter out of producer packets and installed skill references. Its public availability means a prepared packet is input separation, not a secure held-out test.

The initial bank contains authored engineering situations and historical transfer questions. Supplied facts in an authored vignette are exercise assumptions. Historical sources support the supplied historical facts; they do not establish that the proposed modern intervention is effective. Question selections and review criteria require independent adjudication.

The adjacent performance bank covers artifact work and open engineering reasoning. Its criteria remain separately maintained. Historical HO-01 evidence is retained unchanged; its unknown model/settings do not become known because a new benchmark exists.

Use python3 scripts/benchmark.py validate from the repository root to check bank structure, source references and key consistency. Tests use synthetic response records to qualify scoring behavior. Neither check is an agent score.

Version 0.2.0 replaces the original choices with competing engineering judgments, repairs ambiguous lifecycle and command-authorization stems, clarifies a selected system boundary and rebalances option labels within each split. All splits were available during this revision. The original bank and scorer and failed three-arm diagnostic remain unchanged. Do not score old responses against the revised labels.

python3 scripts/benchmark.py diagnose reports measured answer-length shortcuts, ties and position distributions. It is a construction diagnostic, not a content validity test. Packets, responses and optional reviews now use schema 2 binding; the archived schema 1 runs are historical records, not retroactively validated.

Source: evals/evidence/README.md

Observed skill-use evidence

The revised quiz runs scored 24/24 selections and 94/96 independently reviewed reasoning points in each arm. They expose a ceiling and common reasoning gaps, with no observed advantage from adding the skills.

The engineering task runs include 19 active cases covering all 13 skills and five no-package comparisons. The connected historical exercises exercise three multi-file projects. A real outcome-rule ambiguity led to targeted guidance tuning and a fresh transfer check. Their independent agent assessments retain failures and comparison limits.

The initial quiz diagnostic preserves three 24-question runs. All arms reached 24/24; an independent surface-cue probe invalidated the initial bank for comparative quality claims. Its failures and original source remain recorded while the benchmark is repaired.

HO-01 is a single fresh artifact-producing exercise using isolated requirements, architecture, and verification/evidence packages. The producer had the raw request and packaged references, without the worked answer or rubrics. Outputs and their original hashes are preserved.

A separate reviewer assessed the actual artifacts against the original facts and four proposed criteria, reproducing document checks and all 12 trace mappings. No material repair remained for the requested draft. Controller verification and stakeholder validation activities are planned, not executed.

Run metadata records unknown model identity/settings and no external model API use. This is not a controlled Sol/Astra comparison or a pass rate for the historical eight-case bank or the expanded current benchmark. Future behavioral claims need an authorized, recorded host/model and additional unseen cases under the evaluation protocol.

The judgment and performance benchmark now provides separate practice, development and reserved public evaluation questions plus expanded artifact cases. Curated questions, answer keys, prepared packets and synthetic scoring tests are evaluation infrastructure; they are not completed agent runs. Add new run and independent-assessment links here only after their artifacts and provenance exist.

Source: evals/evidence/historical-performance-20261113/README.md

Connected historical project exercises

A separate participant completed three existing multi-file teaching projects: Mars Climate Orbiter, Hubble optics, and Heathrow Terminal 5. Each output includes proposed registers, editable relation views, a decision and the observations that could change it. No physical or historical test was run.

The independent review rated each output 2 on all five assessed dimensions. It found no critical error or required artifact correction. The reviewer disclosed its numeric anchors: the frozen protocol named dimensions and critical errors but did not predeclare a numeric scale. All 80 preparer-manifest entries, 83 recorded input hashes, 25 output hashes and three record sidecars were checked.

Original register fields, IDs and evidence statuses remain preserved. The collection distinguishes participant input/output files from reader references and public review guides added only after production.

Three cases share one participant context. Source retrieval and skill use are self-reported and content-checked; native activation was not measured. These observations support bounded artifact quality, not an improvement estimate, historical counterfactual, original-project approval or engineering acceptance.

Reader references: Heathrow Terminal 5: opening a service is an integration test

This page was added after participant production to resolve reading links. It was not part of the participant packet. The original supplied source register remains in sources.json.

Sources and access

  • HG-10-S1: House of Commons Transport Committee: The opening of Heathrow Terminal 5. Chapter 2, paragraphs 8–14 Publication: 2008-11-03. Committee conclusions and witness accounts are distinguishable; trial participation alone does not establish trial representativeness.
  • HG-10-S2: The opening of Heathrow Terminal 5: communication and lessons. Chapter 3, paragraphs 15–19 Publication: 2008-11-03. The committee explicitly avoided certainty that better cooperation would have prevented every problem.

Complete historical case. The adjacent public review guide was also supplied to readers after production.

Source: evals/evidence/historical-performance-20261113/heathrow-terminal-5/outputs/decision-brief.md

HG-10-CH1 — joint readiness note

Recommendation: reject separate departmental briefings as a replacement for the joint exception-handling rehearsal. Hold opening of the affected baggage-dependent service until an integrated trial and its unresolved issues have been reviewed. A fixed public date is a planning constraint, not evidence of readiness. A demonstrably separable reduced service may be proposed for that date, but its staffing, route, capacity, passenger arrangements and fallback must be bounded and exercised first. None of those conditions is established by this packet.

This is a synthetic readiness decision, not a retrospective approval or a claim about what Heathrow should have done on a particular date. HG-10-F1–F2 are attributed historical findings; the interfaces and claims are teaching reconstructions. No trial has been run here, and no public passengers, systems, or operations have been affected. Proposed decision roles below are role names, not appointments already made.

The inspected Transport Committee report, chapter 2, paragraphs 8–14 supports the narrow training/familiarisation finding. Committee conclusions are distinguishable from witness accounts about training and bag diversity. The inspected chapter 3, paragraphs 15–19 records communication concerns and joint-working arrangements, but does not establish with certainty that earlier cooperation would have prevented all problems. These sources motivate scenario coverage; they supply no capacity target for the fictional opening.

Claims and evidence boundary

Existing claim and status Disposition
HG-10-C1 — source_supported Retain the scoped historical finding. Relevant committee paragraphs were inspected; complete training records and trial data are not supplied.
HG-10-C2 — unsupported_extension Keep explicitly unsupported. Attendance and subsystem completion alone cannot establish end-to-end service or joint recovery performance.
HG-10-C3 — proposed_unexecuted Keep open. There is no synthetic joint rehearsal record, observed performance, issue disposition or authorized acceptance.

A briefing can support a claim that identified staff received a specified procedure revision if delivery and attendance are recorded. A separately observed knowledge check could support a narrower claim that those staff can identify their own action, contact and escalation rule. A list of departmental questions can expose open concerns. Neither briefing proposal nor attendance proves those outcomes, and no such records are supplied.

Only an integrated observation can show that airline and operator staff exchange the right information, acknowledge custody and authority, recognize disruption, coordinate passenger/bag decisions, and resume without losing status. Representative physical work is also needed to show staff can find and operate the actual spaces and equipment under HG-10-I1 and HG-10-I4. A tabletop rehearsal can expose authority gaps but cannot establish physical route performance, equipment handling, staffing adequacy or throughput.

Proposed trial and decision roles

Run the three scenarios in scenarios.md as a joint control-room/tabletop exercise now, using controlled simulated bag/passenger identities and actual planned communication channels where available. Record every simulation and substitution. The airline duty manager and terminal duty manager must participate with representative front-line staff, baggage/handling roles and an observer from each organization. No live service action is authorized by this plan.

Once an isolated, safely available route representative of the proposed opening scope exists, repeat the scenarios as a physical end-to-end exercise using the actual relevant configuration, work positions, interfaces and test bags. Facility delivery must document which spaces, equipment, staffing conditions and bag characteristics are represented. If only a reduced route is available, the result can apply only to that route and those conditions. If no representative route is available before opening, do not replace that missing evidence with a tabletop success: delay the dependent service. Trial feasibility and facility availability are themselves unresolved.

Before either stage, the proposed joint readiness chair agrees the procedure, scope, acceptance conditions, stop rules, recorders and review time with both duty managers. Qualitative conditions include completed acknowledged handovers, consistent bag/passenger status, a named owner for every exception, correct restriction of new acceptance during disruption, and coordinated restart after reconciliation. Demand, service limits, response times, workload and capacity criteria remain to be supplied before the physical trial can substantiate capacity or timeliness. A bounded exercise is not exhaustive readiness validation.

Options for the opening decision

Option Service effect and possible advantage Evidence that discriminates it
Full scope on the public date Keeps the planned service offer but exposes the whole affected journey to unresolved coordination and familiarisation gaps. Representative full-scope nominal and exception trial; demand and bag mix; staffing competence/coverage; physical route readiness; integrated capacity and recovery evidence. Unsupported now.
Reduced initial scope Limits flights, routes, hours or service types to an explicitly chosen demonstrable subset. May require rebooking, rerouting, longer waits, or withholding some checked-bag services. No specific reduction is selected without data. Proof the subset is physically and operationally separable; demand and capacity for it and any receiving service; roster and fallback resources; trial of its normal/recovery journeys; passenger communications; defined expansion gate. An untested manual workaround is not a fallback.
Delay affected service Preserves time for integrated familiarisation and correction, while imposing service disruption, possible rebooking and resource/scheduling costs. A delay does not itself fix the issues. Earliest representative-area availability; corrective-work and trial duration; availability/capacity of alternatives; passenger commitments; operational and commercial consequences. Recommended default while the acceptance gaps remain.

No weights, throughput numbers, historical airport metrics or invented financial estimates are used. The airline operations lead must supply demand, passenger commitments and alternate-service feasibility; the terminal operations lead must supply facility/capacity and route dependencies; staffing leads must supply competency and roster coverage; the joint chair must establish the decision deadline and permitted service envelope.

Open issues and ownership

Issue and affected IDs Proposed owner Service consequence and required next evidence
HG-10-O01: training area not representative or available; I1, I4, C2 Facility delivery lead and both training leads Physical performance remains unestablished. Produce a readiness/representativeness map and available trial window.
HG-10-O02: cross-organization stop, escalation and restart rules; I2, C3 Airline duty manager and terminal duty manager jointly Ambiguous authority may leave bags accepted into an unavailable service or restart with unreconciled status. Agree roles and observe SC02/SC03.
HG-10-O03: front-line concerns lack owned disposition; I3 Joint readiness chair with front-line representatives Unresolved issues may be bypassed at opening. Keep a concern/issue record with response, owner and review decision; repeat affected scenarios after correction.
HG-10-O04: service envelope and fallback capacity absent; C2 Airline operations lead and terminal operations lead Reduced scope or diversion could overload another service. Supply demand, resource and alternate-route evidence before choosing a subset.
HG-10-O05: no joint execution record; C3, I4 Joint trial lead and observers from both organizations No claim of rehearsal or demonstrated readiness can close. Retain configuration, actions, observations, deviations and results from all three scenarios.

Joint readiness message: The airline and terminal operator should retain a readiness hold for the affected baggage service; separate briefings cannot close HG-10-C2 or HG-10-C3. The two duty managers own the integrated recovery procedure, facility delivery owns availability/representativeness, and the joint readiness chair owns the opening-scope decision. Reopen at the earlier of a material scope/configuration change or delivery of the representative trial record, issue dispositions, and a viable fallback/service envelope, and in all cases before the communicated go/no-go deadline. If those artifacts remain unavailable at that deadline, delay the affected service or retain only a separately evidenced subset; do not silently carry the open claims into full opening.

Source: evals/evidence/historical-performance-20261113/heathrow-terminal-5/outputs/scenarios.md

HG-10 proposed integrated trial scenarios

All three scenarios are planned and unexecuted. The sequences are synthetic proposals for review, not actual historical events or adopted airport procedures. The complete operational and security procedures are not supplied. All physical steps require a controlled test configuration and site authorization; a simulated step must be labeled as such in the evidence record and excluded from physical-performance claims.

Common trial contract

Roles: airline check-in/front-line agent, airline baggage/reconciliation lead and duty manager; terminal operator baggage controller, facility/handling representative and duty manager; passenger representative; observer/recorder from each organization; joint trial lead; joint readiness chair. Confirm local role allocation before the exercise: contractual custody boundaries and the organization providing handling personnel are not specified in the packet.

Use the same scoped service configuration, staff access, communications, bag-status records and operating procedures proposed for opening. Identify test passengers and bags without using real customer data. Define the acceptance point, custody acknowledgements, operating restrictions, disruption cues, escalation time limits, permitted holding locations, and recovery criteria before execution. The packet supplies no numerical timing, load or capacity thresholds; owners must establish them from the actual service envelope. Do not declare capacity or timeliness on the strength of these qualitative scenarios alone.

Stage A can be run jointly as a tabletop with clearly labeled simulated equipment/status events. Stage B repeats the selected journey physically on a representative available route with actual interfaces, trained roles and identified test articles. An unavailable area is an explicit coverage exclusion. Separate briefings remain preparation for the exercise, not its replacement.

HG-10-SC01 — nominal passenger and baggage journey

Purpose and trace: test normal airline/operator handovers and staff performance under HG-10-I1, I2 and I4; challenge HG-10-C2. Initial state: the selected route is available, staff are in their assigned positions, systems and communication channels are in the declared mode, and the controlled passenger/bag identity and service destination are known. Start only when the trial lead has recorded which states are real and which are simulated.

Trigger: the passenger representative requests the in-scope journey with a test bag. The airline agent confirms eligibility under the trial rules, creates the bag/passenger association and destination, and submits the bag plus acceptance information to the operator's defined interface. The operator acknowledges the identifier, destination and custody/status, routes the test bag through the agreed facility steps, and reports completion or exception. Required screening steps follow the site-approved test procedure; simulated screening provides no evidence of screening performance.

The designated handling role acknowledges the next custody transfer. The airline reconciliation lead matches the bag and passenger/service records before a simulated or controlled dispatch decision. The airline communicates the passenger's service status. The observers trace the same bag identity across each boundary rather than inferring completion from one subsystem's success indicator.

Observable result: every handover has matched identifiers, sender, receiver, time and acknowledgement; no unowned bag or inconsistent passenger/bag status remains; the passenger reaches the agreed endpoint and the bag reaches its assigned controlled disposition. Completion alone does not establish performance under opening load.

Recovery authority: either front-line party may raise an anomaly and stop the local test step. The operator duty manager controls facility restrictions; the airline duty manager controls new airline acceptance and passenger/service disposition. The trial lead pauses the exercise if the declared route or configuration ceases to hold; restart uses the applicable exception scenario.

Retain: configuration/procedure versions; facility map and exclusions; staff roles and familiarity; test identities and characteristics; ordered handover log; actual/simulated steps; screen or status observations; observer findings; elapsed observations without an invented target; deviations and unresolved issues; separate review disposition.

HG-10-SC02 — baggage route unavailable after acceptance

Purpose and trace: challenge HG-10-I2 and HG-10-C3 by requiring joint service restriction and recovery. Initial state: SC01 has reached airline acceptance with a traceable set of test bags in the route; the designated holding/recovery arrangements and escalation contacts are known. Use a controlled failure injection or a clearly simulated interruption, never an unapproved live fault.

Trigger: the trial controller declares the selected downstream route unavailable after bag acceptance. The operator controller detects/receives the interruption, identifies the affected route and bag set, notifies the airline, and requests acknowledgement of the service restriction. The airline duty manager stops additional acceptance into the affected route and directs passenger messaging and any permitted rebooking/alternative service. The operator controls affected equipment and secure holding under the trial procedure; neither party silently routes bags into an unverified manual workaround.

Both sides reconcile which bags were accepted, transferred, held or remain unlocated. The airline owns passenger/service decisions; the operator duty manager owns facility isolation and technical restoration. Any fallback must be pre-agreed, accessible, staffed and compatible with capacity limits. If these conditions are absent, hold the affected service and exercise the delay/return/rebooking decision rather than inventing spare capacity.

Observable result: an acknowledged restriction reaches the airline acceptance point; the test records show no further acceptance into the blocked route after that restriction takes effect under the agreed timing rule; every affected bag and passenger has an owned status and disposition. A restored equipment indication does not alone trigger resumption.

Recovery authority and end state: the operator duty manager confirms route availability and bag/status reconciliation; the airline duty manager confirms staffing and service readiness; both record joint permission to resume within the approved envelope. The joint trial lead restarts the controlled scenario from an identified state. If reconciliation, capacity or authority is unresolved, the defined final state is affected-service hold with passenger/bag dispositions recorded, not nominal completion.

Retain: failure-injection identity and timing; initial bag set; alarm/notification/acknowledgement chronology; acceptance-stop observation; holding/custody and passenger decision logs; fallback evidence or explicit absence; restoration checks; joint restart/hold decision; issues and owners.

HG-10-SC03 — missing handover acknowledgement and inconsistent status

Purpose and trace: expose an organization/communication failure through HG-10-I2 and I3, while challenging HG-10-C3. Initial state: one test bag is at a controlled airline/operator boundary; both sides have the same initial identity and know the approved acknowledgement/escalation rule. Declare how acknowledgement timeout will be represented; no time value is supplied by this packet.

Trigger: suppress the agreed acknowledgement in the test channel and introduce a controlled disagreement: the airline record shows transfer attempted, while the operator record does not establish receipt. The airline front-line agent identifies the missing acknowledgement, records the concern under I3, and contacts the operator through the approved alternative channel. The operator checks its physical/test custody and record before asserting receipt. Neither side fabricates an acknowledgement or duplicates the bag merely to clear a queue.

The two duty managers establish one reconciled record of the bag's actual controlled location and status. They identify other transfers potentially affected by the channel failure and restrict further use of that handover until a safe defined method exists. The airline directs passenger/service information; the operator directs facility/custody actions. If no alternative communication or custody proof is available, place the affected transfer/service on hold and escalate to the joint readiness chair through the recorded issue process.

Observable result: front-line concern is acknowledged and assigned; a consistent bag/passenger disposition is agreed or explicitly marked unresolved; the record preserves original conflicting statuses, communication attempts and correction lineage. No lost ownership or duplicate transfer is hidden by overwriting a record.

Recovery authority and end state: communication restoration is followed by reconciliation of all potentially affected transactions, resolution of duplicate/stale statuses, and a controlled acknowledgement check. Both duty managers authorize service resumption; the trial lead resumes the test. An unlocated bag or unreconciled transaction ends in a documented hold, with an owner and next action. The readiness chair decides whether the unresolved issue prevents opening the selected scope.

Retain: injected failure and initial state; both unaltered status records; channel and acknowledgement logs; concern/issue ID; physical/test custody evidence; reconciliation and correction history; passenger/service disposition; named-role decisions and restart observation; residual gaps.

Review and coverage boundary

The joint trial lead assembles the configuration-specific record; observers from both organizations identify disagreements rather than averaging them. Each issue has an owner, corrective action, due/review trigger and affected scenario. Changed procedures, equipment, route, staff allocation or interface semantics require a justified applicability decision and rerun of affected scenarios. Record expected and observed behavior, actual deviations and the result only after execution. Acceptance remains a separate joint readiness decision.

These scenarios cover one nominal journey, route interruption and a failed organizational handover. They do not establish opening throughput, all bag classes, every staffing shift, security compliance or every failure combination. Select additional coverage using the real service envelope and observed issues rather than declaring this set exhaustive.

HG-10 review guide

This guide evaluates reasoning in the new exercise, not historical blame or a claim that a different decision would certainly have succeeded.

  • Preserve the distinction between completion of a briefing and demonstrated performance under representative conditions.
  • HG-10-C2 is unsupported because departmental readiness can coexist with missing handover and recovery capability.
  • HG-10-C3 cannot be promoted from proposed to executed merely by creating a rehearsal plan.
  • A useful fallback includes available resources, activation authority, customer consequences, and recovery criteria.
  • The original report supplies context; it does not prove that one proposed opening strategy would have prevented the historical disruption.

HG-03-CH1 — fixture acceptance review

Recommendation: do not close acceptance of HG-03-CH1. Preserve the auxiliary discrepancy and obtain an independent dimensional check of the replacement fixture as assembled. The two computers share one generated geometry file. Their agreement therefore cannot establish that this common input represents the physical fixture correctly. Replacement alone does not eliminate an error carried through the retained calibration chain.

This is a retrospective metrology teaching exercise. HG-03-F1–F2 are attributed historical findings; the interfaces and claims are teaching reconstructions; the replacement fixture, computers, and disputed result belong to the synthetic change. No numerical uncertainty budget, raw result, released geometry, executed check, or approval is supplied. Proposed role assignments below require confirmation by the laboratory.

The inspected NASA optical systems failure report, executive summary, PDF pages 4–6, supports the finding of an incorrectly assembled reference and the lack of an independent dimensional verification after assembly. It also records auxiliary indications being discounted. That historical evidence motivates the review; it does not diagnose the fictional replacement fixture or prove that its auxiliary instrument is correct.

Claims and interfaces

Existing claim and status Current disposition
HG-03-C1 — source_supported Retain the report-scoped historical statement. The report was inspected; no historical raw optical data are available in the packet.
HG-03-C2 — unsupported_extension Keep explicitly unsupported. Different computers do not remove the shared geometry-file dependency. Common source data, algorithms, configuration and calibration may create further dependence, but their details are unknown.
HG-03-C3 — proposed_unexecuted Keep open. The replacement fixture's as-assembled dimensions have not been measured in the supplied evidence. Agreement between computer results cannot substitute for that measurement.

HG-03-I1 connects physical assembly to the primary measurement; HG-03-I3 must connect the actual assembly to its calibration record and released definition. Those are two separate correspondences. HG-03-I4 must carry primary results with their reference and processing lineage, rather than an unexplained agreement statement. HG-03-I2 must preserve the auxiliary result and its unresolved disposition in the same acceptance record.

The proposed registers retain every original field. Added fields specify the evidence and ownership needed without treating a proposal as historical fact. dependencies.proposed.mmd retains the supplied relations and adds the two computers, common geometry file, physical references, unknown upstream dependencies, and proposed dimensional check. Solid arrows describe supplied/reconstructed relationships; dotted arrows denote unknown lineage or planned evidence, as labeled.

Why agreement is weak accuracy evidence

If the geometry generator encodes an erroneous reference, both computers can calculate consistent answers from the same erroneous input. Their agreement then demonstrates consistency for that input, not accuracy against the assembled fixture. A correct calibration certificate also does not prove that the measured hardware, serial identity, assembly state, alignment, or environmental conditions match the certificate. Shared optical raw data, analysis code or transforms are additional possible dependencies requiring inspection, not established facts about this laboratory.

The auxiliary instrument's independence is also unestablished. Preserve its disagreement while recovering its reference, calibration, source data, processing and environmental history. The present evidence supports neither declaring the auxiliary instrument correct nor dismissing it as unreliable. Do not average inconsistent measurements or expand tolerances merely to make them agree.

Select the discriminating check

Perform HG-03-V01, an independent dimensional survey of the as-assembled replacement fixture, before repeating the preferred instrument. Freeze and identify the assembly and current computer inputs first; recover the released definition, then measure relevant reference separations, orientations and alignment with a separately justified calibration and analysis path. Determine the required resolution and uncertainty from the applicable dimensional tolerances and optical sensitivity; neither is supplied. A metrology lead independent of the original geometry-file generation should review the method and data. Independence of people alone does not eliminate shared technical references.

check-options.csv compares this with a repeated measurement and a new physical measurement principle. The chosen check targets the missing physical-to-definition link directly. A repeat is useful for random variability or reproducibility but could reproduce the same systematic reference error. A different physical principle can later challenge the primary optical model if its reference, data and analysis chains are sufficiently distinct and its sensitivity is adequate.

Before execution, agree the measurands, configuration, environmental conditions, calibrated instruments, uncertainty model, decision rule, and reviewers. For a two-sided dimensional tolerance, a proposed conservative rule is that the relevant expanded measurement interval must lie within the specified tolerance interval. The coverage basis and treatment of correlated errors require review; overlapping a limit is inconclusive, not automatically acceptable. No numerical tolerance or confidence value is invented here.

A dimensional discrepancy that is resolved beyond the agreed uncertainty would support retaining the acceptance hold and correcting the assembly or reference chain. Dimensional consistency with adequate sensitivity would reduce concern about HG-03-C3 and shift the next investigation toward optical data, processing, and the auxiliary chain; it would not by itself explain the contradiction or close overall acceptance. An inconclusive or insufficiently sensitive result leaves C3 open. Closure could be reconsidered only after configuration-specific dimensional evidence, dependency review, and a defensible disposition of the auxiliary discrepancy are available.

Acceptance statement and next review

HG-03-CH1 is not accepted on the supplied evidence. HG-03-C2 remains an unsupported independence assertion and HG-03-C3 remains unexecuted. The auxiliary disagreement remains an open evidence item under HG-03-I2. No physical measurement or acceptance test was conducted in this review.

The proposed metrology lead owns HG-03-V01 and its uncertainty basis; the fixture configuration custodian owns the released definition and as-assembled identity; the analysis owner owns geometry/source/software lineage for both computers; the auxiliary measurement owner owns the raw result and calibration history. The acceptance review chair owns the discrepancy disposition and final scope. Reopen when the frozen configuration, dimensional results and uncertainty, dependency inventory, and preserved primary/auxiliary data are available together. A new fixture, another matching computation, or the passage of a schedule milestone is not that trigger.

Source: evals/evidence/historical-performance-20261113/hubble-optics/outputs/evidence-plan.md

HG-03 evidence plan and discrepancy record

This plan is proposed and unexecuted. New V/D identifiers identify output proposals and do not replace supplied teaching IDs.

HG-03-V01 addresses HG-03-C3 through HG-03-I1 and HG-03-I3. Configuration: replacement fixture as assembled, released definition, calibration chain, geometry generator version and source inputs, geometry-file hash, both computers' software/configuration and raw-input hashes, primary instrument identity, and auxiliary instrument identity. Unknown entries must be explicitly recorded before interpreting comparisons. Preserve the original state before adjustment; an adjustment creates a new identified configuration and requires applicability review of old evidence.

Preconditions: available released dimensional requirements and tolerances; defined reference datums, relevant measurands and environmental limits; an independently reviewed metrology procedure with sufficient resolution; controlled measuring equipment with appropriate calibration and uncertainty; a decision rule agreed before reading the new result. If these are unavailable, V01 is not ready to support acceptance. Do not invent them from the desired outcome.

Observation: record raw measurements and derived dimensions, uncertainty contributions and correlations, reference conditions, deviations, and the mapping from each result to the applicable tolerance. Independently reconcile the result with the physical fixture, released definition and generated geometry, without taking the generated file as an oracle. Where optical relevance depends on a sensitivity model, identify that model and its assumptions separately.

Expected decision outcomes: outside the agreed acceptance region means keep the hold and investigate/correct; wholly within it may support the scoped dimensional claim after review; overlap or inadequate sensitivity means inconclusive. A scoped V01 result is not a complete fixture or optical-system acceptance.

HG-03-D01 — unresolved auxiliary disagreement. Provenance: reported in synthetic HG-03-CH1; actual numbers and files are not supplied. Evidence state: reported discrepancy, raw evidence unavailable, no documented cause for the unreliable label. Preserve both the adverse result and the label as historical entries in this synthetic record; do not adopt the label as a finding.

Acquire and retain primary and auxiliary raw readings, acquisition conditions, instrument and fixture identifiers, calibration histories, processing versions, reference geometry, timestamps, operator observations, and all prior handling or adjustment. Preserve original bytes and hashes alongside any corrected reductions. The analysis owner and auxiliary measurement owner jointly prepare a comparison on the same measurand/configuration with uncertainty and correlation considered. The metrology lead reviews whether a real conflict remains.

A defensible disposition must identify the causal explanation, its supporting evidence, affected results and configurations, and what the corrected or additional measurement demonstrates. An explanation that the auxiliary instrument disagrees is circular. If a defect in that instrument is found, retain its original data, the defect evidence, correction history, and the limited scope of invalidated results. If the primary chain is at fault, re-evaluate both computer outputs. If the result remains unexplained, keep acceptance open.

Evidence ownership and retention: the fixture custodian keeps configuration and change history; the analysis owner keeps file/software lineage; the metrology lead keeps V01 procedure, raw observations, uncertainty and review; the auxiliary owner keeps D01 evidence; the acceptance chair records claim-by-claim disposition and authorized scope separately from measurement outcomes. These roles are proposed and no role-holder approvals are asserted.

HG-03 review guide

This guide evaluates reasoning in the new exercise, not historical blame or a claim that a different decision would certainly have succeeded.

  • Distinguish repeated measurement, independent computation, and an independent physical reference. They address different failure mechanisms.
  • HG-03-C2 is an unsupported independence claim even if both computers are functioning correctly.
  • HG-03-C3 remains unverified until the replacement fixture itself is checked; a drawing or calibration certificate for another configuration is insufficient.
  • Treat the auxiliary discrepancy as a question to resolve, not automatic proof that either instrument is correct.
  • A strong response chooses a check based on discriminating power and uncertainty, not the prestige or number of agreeing instruments.

Source: evals/evidence/historical-performance-20261113/mars-climate-orbiter/outputs/decision-brief.md

HG-05-CH1 — decision brief

Recommendation: reject HG-05-CH1 as submitted for the planned integration exercise. Adding a unit field is useful, but continued acceptance of numeric-only files without recovered provenance retains the ambiguity the change is meant to remove. Resubmit the controlled interface proposal in interface-contract.md; use a quarantined test environment while its conditions are evaluated. This is an engineering recommendation, not an approval, flight decision, or executed integration result.

HG-05-F1 and HG-05-F2 are attributed historical findings. HG-05-I1–I3 and HG-05-C1–C3 are teaching reconstructions; HG-05-CH1 is synthetic. The supplier's assertion that export tests pass is part of the fictional change narrative. No export report, software build, sample file, raw measurement, or consumer execution is supplied.

The inspected Phase I investigation report, executive summary pp. 6–8 and sections 4–5, supports the unit mismatch and wider transition, communication, staffing, training, and verification issues. It does not establish that this proposed format or legacy adapter works. This review introduces no mission or certification standard.

Claim disposition

Existing ID and status Assessment and acceptance boundary
HG-05-C1 — source_supported Retain the narrow historical finding; the relevant report content was inspected. The complete historical interface specification is not supplied.
HG-05-C2 — unsupported_extension Retain as an explicitly unsupported assertion. A label can be recognized while the number is wrong, converted twice, assigned to the wrong event, or used incorrectly downstream. A producer-only test cannot establish consumer or navigation behavior.
HG-05-C3 — proposed_unexecuted Keep open. Rejection must be observed at the ingestion boundary and in downstream accepted state, including mixed batches, parser failure, and recovery. A rejection message alone is insufficient.

claim-evidence.proposed.csv preserves every original field and adds the proposed review and ownership fields. It does not silently rewrite C2 into a weaker true claim or promote C3 to passed.

Conditions for a revised proposal

Condition Minimum evidence Proposed accountable role
HG-05-P01: remove ambiguous ingress Reviewed version/unit contract, exact parser and adapter configuration, and an explicit list of permitted paths. No fall-through from a failed new-format parse to legacy parsing. Consumer integration owner, with producer interface owner
HG-05-P02: recover legacy provenance Byte-identifiable files, producing configuration, source quantity/units, derivation history, and a reviewer-supported mapping. Files without that evidence stay quarantined. Producer data custodian; consumer owner decides admissibility
HG-05-P03: establish an independent oracle A controlled paired sample linking a known impulse quantity to source values, expected serialized values, and expected consumer results, with units, frame, event/time definition, derivation, and tolerance basis. Navigation verification lead; supplier contributes source information but does not solely approve its own oracle
HG-05-P04: exercise both successful and rejected paths The acceptance matrix, executed later against identified producer/consumer builds; input/output hashes, expected/observed comparison, rejection reasons, accepted-state comparison, logs, and deviations. Consumer integration test owner; navigation verification lead reviews
HG-05-P05: transfer operating responsibility Agreed quarantine/replay procedure, legacy inventory disposition, anomaly contact, configuration owner, and demonstrated development-to-operations handover. Operations lead and development lead through HG-05-I2

Proposed roles have not been assigned to named people in the supplied packet. The integration lead must confirm role holders before scheduling the review. The next review is triggered by delivery of P01–P03 plus a runnable, versioned ingestion path; final exercise acceptance additionally needs P04–P05 and disposition of anomalies.

What can be reused

Available or asserted material Permitted use and limitation
source-facts.csv and sources.json Establish rationale and historical source scope; they are not test vectors.
interfaces.csv, claim-evidence.csv, change.json, relations.mmd Identify interfaces, claims, and coverage to turn into a procedure. The graph is an information-flow aid, not an executable model.
request.md, review-task.md, packet-manifest.json, supplied skills Define the task, provenance boundary, file integrity, and engineering guidance. Hash agreement is not verification of an engineering claim.
Supplier export tests Reported only in the synthetic change. Recover actual procedure, inputs, expected results, execution logs, producer release and configuration before claiming any reuse. Even then, they cover only their demonstrated scope.
Existing legacy data files None are supplied. Recover identities, units, generating releases and transformations before use as semantic acceptance data. Unknown files may later be used as clearly labeled negative rejection fixtures; they cannot become a valid oracle by assertion.
Producer, adapter, consumer implementation and released interface Not supplied; obtain the actual versions for integration execution. No fabricated sample in these outputs is historical flight data.

The proposed matrix has no passed rows and contains no executed result. sample-plan.json supplies a concrete analytical fixture: an ideal 2 N force for 3 s gives a 6 Ns impulse; the disagreement fixture carries 7 Ns. These are invented, labeled software-test inputs with an independently derivable mathematical answer, not physical calibration or historical data. The navigation verification lead must review them, agree the comparison rule, and obtain the provenance-supported physical sample still needed for broader meaning. Structural validity and physical correctness remain different claims.

Message to the integration lead

Reject HG-05-CH1 as submitted: the uncontrolled legacy path leaves unit meaning unresolved. The gap is a provenance-bound interface and an independently established producer-to-consumer acceptance sample. The consumer integration owner owns the revised ingress contract; the producer data custodian owns legacy recovery; the navigation verification lead owns the oracle. Reopen when those artifacts and a runnable configuration are available, then require the recorded ingestion results and operations handover before accepting the exercise.

Source: evals/evidence/historical-performance-20261113/mars-climate-orbiter/outputs/interface-contract.md

Proposed revision to HG-05-I1

Status: proposed, unexecuted, and unapproved. The original ID, producer, consumer, meaning, basis, and reconstruction status remain in interfaces.proposed.csv; this text is a proposed revision, not a historical specification.

Exchanged item: impulse quantity records from Ground-data producer to Navigation consumer. The contract must define scalar or vector components, sign/frame, event identity, time basis and integration interval, precision, and validity limits. These details are absent and remain release blockers where they affect the sample or downstream interpretation. No timing or accuracy target is invented here.

Version recognition: propose an explicit envelope identifier and exact schema version new-v1. Only versions listed in the released consumer registry are recognized. Validate schema before interpretation; reject unknown, missing, duplicate, or contradictory version identifiers. A filename, numeric magnitude, parse success, or supplier name does not identify a version. Never retry rejected new-format data through a permissive legacy parser.

Unit semantics: initially allow only the exact proposed token N*s, meaning newton-seconds of impulse, bound to the quantity and its frame/time definition. Other strings, empty/null/missing units, mixed metadata, or quantity/unit mismatches are rejected. These tokens are design proposals to be agreed, not existing standard schemas. Supporting another known unit requires a separately reviewed mapping and independent conversion samples; this review does not enable it implicitly.

Legacy path: numeric-only records cannot authenticate their own units. Disable direct numeric-only ingestion. A separate controlled legacy-v0 adapter may be proposed only when a reviewed manifest binds each file's SHA256, producing release, original units, quantity definition, and derivation history. The adapter produces the same validated canonical representation and preserves the original bytes and conversion lineage. Unknown or unrecoverable provenance means quarantine, even if the values look plausible. Verified provenance is an eligibility condition, not proof of correct numerical processing.

Acceptance and failure: stage each file, validate the entire file and its envelope, and commit atomically only after applicable checks. Any unknown or contradictory item quarantines the whole file; do not partially add accepted records. Preserve bytes, hash, schema identifier, rejection code, and diagnostic context. Accepted-state identifiers and values must be unchanged after rejection. Recovery requires a new controlled input/revision and owner disposition, not an operator unit guess or relabeling the same bytes to silence an error.

Semantic check: the acceptance sample must compare the actual consumer interpretation against a quantity established independently of the exporter and its metadata. A recognized N*s label cannot reveal every incorrect number. The future test harness must detect the seeded metadata/quantity disagreement; general live detection needs an available independent observation or residual check and remains unestablished here. Unexplained residuals follow HG-05-I3; a parser acceptance cannot close HG-05-C2.

Ownership: the Navigation verification lead owns and controls the paired acceptance sample and its expected answers, with independent review of the derivation. The producer interface owner supplies originating quantity provenance and export configuration. The consumer integration owner implements and tests dispatch, validation, isolation, and state transitions. The development and operations leads jointly own handover under HG-05-I2. The integration lead confirms owners, acceptance scope, and review triggers. These are proposed responsibilities, not recorded appointments.

Evidence record: preserve input/output hashes, source-quantity provenance, expected intermediate and final quantities, unit transformations, frame/time interpretation, tolerance rationale, producer/adapter/consumer versions, procedure revision, pre/post accepted state, warnings, rejection/quarantine log, observed outcomes, deviations, reviewer decision and acceptance decision separately. No such execution record exists in this bundle.

HG-05 review guide

This guide evaluates reasoning in the new exercise, not historical blame or a claim that a different decision would certainly have succeeded.

  • Preserve HG-05-C1 as a narrow attributed historical finding.
  • HG-05-C2 remains unsupported: new metadata cannot establish physical meaning or mission correctness by itself.
  • HG-05-C3 remains planned until an identified implementation is exercised and outputs are inspected. A plausible rejection policy is not a test result.
  • A credible disposition considers compatibility, explicit unknown states, quarantining disputed inputs, shared producer/consumer review, and the consequences of changing the format.
  • Do not claim that this exercise proves how the original mission would have behaved after the change.

HG-05 connected review task

All IDs in this bundle are newly assigned teaching IDs. The source facts are attributed historical findings; the interfaces and claims are teaching reconstructions. The change request is synthetic and was never proposed to the original program. No test in this bundle has been executed.

Read source facts, interfaces, claim/evidence register, and change request together. Use the case sources and locators to challenge an assertion. The relation view is an editable information-flow aid, not a formal SysML model.

Decision to produce

Write a disposition of HG-05-CH1 with a claim-by-claim evidence status. Revise HG-05-I1 to state how version and unit semantics are recognized, what happens to unknown inputs, and who owns the acceptance sample. Identify which existing files can support testing and which require provenance recovery.

Produce an acceptance matrix with at least a valid sample, an unrecognized unit, a missing unit, and a disagreement between metadata and an independently known quantity. State the oracle, expected disposition, and evidence still needed. Do not mark any row passed.

End with a short status message to an integration lead: decision, reason, remaining gap, owner, and the next review trigger.

Review your result using the review guide. The guide is public formative material; this task is not a hidden performance benchmark.
