Source: evals/evidence/ho01/independent-assessment.md

HO-01 independent smoke-exercise assessment

Assessed 2026-10-12 against the isolated packet's request.md and the four HO-01 criteria in mbse-agents-modernization/evals/rubrics.json. All six files in mbse-evaluation-packet-ho01/outputs were read. The parent reports that the producer did not receive the rubrics or worked answer; this reviewer read the HO-01 criteria only after production finished. Outputs were not edited.

Result: the requested reviewable draft is completed and all four criteria are met at draft maturity. No material finding requiring artifact repair was identified. This is one skill-use smoke exercise, not an overall model-performance judgment or Sol/Astra comparison.

HO-01 criterion Assessment and located evidence
Preserve N-01 through N-04 and linked allocations Met. 00-review-guide.md, Input and provenance, retains both source paragraphs verbatim. 01-requirements.md maps opening at/above 32 °C for 30 s, brief-dip reset, closing strictly below 28 °C after 60 s, local override/explicit resume, 5 s missing-data stop/fault/no automatic restart, and remote intent/network-failure local stop into RQ-01 through RQ-10. DR-01/DR-02 are explicitly proposed derived requirements. 04-trace-and-decisions.md, source disposition and allocation tables, preserve N-01–N-04 across functions, components, interfaces and planned activities.
Define timer/sample freshness and stop/resume semantics Met for a draft with open contracts. 02-architecture.md, mode/transition contract and I-01 through I-08, separate data eligibility, thermal qualification, motion arbitration, direct local inhibit and authorization latches. Nominal 1 s sampling is not treated as a bound. Acquisition versus receipt time, age/gap limits, invalid/stale packets and clock mapping remain explicit D-01/D-05/D-10 decisions. Simultaneous stop/fault reasons persist, return of data cannot authorize motion, and release of stop is distinct from deliberate enable. Proposed startup/timer-reset behavior is labeled as a design choice.
Keep 50 ms, weather and safe-state decisions unconfirmed Met. 04-trace-and-decisions.md, D-04/D-09 and RK-04/RK-07, rejects the manager's universal 50 ms as an adopted deadline. 02-architecture.md, timing budgets, separates event-to-inhibit from physical arrest/coast/holding. Wind/rain, safe position and operator response remain unresolved; neither automatic opening nor closing is asserted universally safe. Proposed accountable roles are distinguished from agreed assignments or approval authority.
Supply usable interface/verification conditions without executed-evidence claims Met. Interface contracts identify directions, exchanged data/signals, units, validity, ownership, error handling and specific unresolved terms. 03-verification-plan.md, VA-01–VA-14 and SV-01–SV-04, supplies normal/boundary/fault/recovery stimuli, observations, acceptance dependencies, configuration, environment, roles and proposed evidence names. VA-04/VA-06/VA-10 observe physical motion as well as electrical inhibit; VA-14 addresses actual path bounds and uncertainty. Every activity remains Planned and the stated requirement totals are 0 verified/accepted.

The architecture makes useful decisions rather than treating the candidate list as sufficient: it compares network-only, MCU-mediated and direct local driver-inhibit options; proposes a local fault indicator because the dashboard shares the failed network; and retains the one-MCU/one-driver/common-power/mechanical dependencies. It does not claim general fault tolerance or established reliability. Closing-reset semantics, remote command scope and detailed motion policy are recorded for decision rather than silently invented. These unresolved terms appropriately block a final design while permitting the requested draft.

Independently reproduced document checks

Using Python 3.12 in the supplied Windows workspace, without running controller tests or changing outputs, this reviewer reproduced:

  • 2/2 raw input paragraphs present verbatim and N-01–N-04 present in all five core drafts.
  • Input SHA-256 and all five core-artifact SHA-256 hashes match 05-artifact-checks.md.
  • 15/15 local Markdown links resolve; table field counts are consistent across all six artifacts.
  • Unique definition counts match the report: RQ 10, DR 2, F 7, C 7, I 8, AD 4, VA 14, SV 4, D 12 and RK 8; no undefined local artifact-ID reference was found.
  • All 12 requirement records' planned VA sets match their trace rows, and each linked VA explicitly names the corresponding requirement.

05-artifact-checks.md consistently describes these as document checks, explicitly excludes them from verified-requirement totals, and records proposed future evidence paths as nonexistent results. Its reported checks are reproducible; the review does not independently authenticate the producer's historical execution timestamps. No unsupported controller-test, simulation, proof, certification or acceptance claim was found.

Limits and next work

The producer's actual model identity and settings are unknown/inherited. This single task, four proposed criteria and one independent assessment do not establish comparative model quality, variability, reliability or cost. No primary-source/regulatory assertion needed external verification for this source-only greenhouse draft. The proposed direct inhibit, wiring, sensor/driver properties, environmental envelope, physical stop and stakeholder agreement remain untested. D-01–D-12 and the missing hardware/supplier/evidence contracts must be resolved before execution or final acceptance; these are documented design gaps, not a failure to complete the requested draft.

Source: evals/evidence/ho01/outputs/00-review-guide.md

Greenhouse vent controller — review guide

Revision: GH-DRAFT-01. Prepared: 2026-10-12. Status: review draft; no requirement, architecture, result, or design decision is approved by this packet.

Deliverables

  • Requirements: source-grounded obligations, provisional derived requirements, acceptance gaps and allocations.
  • Architecture: boundary, functions, components, modes, interfaces, alternatives and timing dependencies.
  • Verification and validation plan: planned activities, acceptance conditions, configuration and evidence records.
  • Traceability and decisions: bidirectional source coverage, dependencies, risks and decisions needed for a final design.
  • Artifact checks: actual local document checks and their limited scope.

These are textual proposals. No live model was changed, no controller was implemented, and no operational test, simulation, proof, reliability study or certification was executed. There are no supplied test results or supplier reliability data. Proposed future evidence locations in the plan do not denote existing results.

Input and provenance

Only ../request.md and the three packet skills and their referenced contracts were used. Raw source IDs are retained below and throughout the deliverables. The unlabeled candidate-design paragraph and manager proposal are cited by locator, not given invented raw source IDs. Artifact IDs such as RQ-01, F-01 and D-01 are local draft identifiers.

Raw stakeholder input

Source locator: ../request.md, paragraph beginning N-01 Owner:. The following wording is retained verbatim:

N-01 Owner: Open the vent when a valid inside-temperature reading stays at or above 32 deg C for 30 s. A brief dip below 32 resets the interval. Close below 28 deg C after 60 s. N-02 Technician: A local manual stop overrides motion; resuming automatic mode requires an explicit action. N-03 Maintenance: If data is missing for 5 s, stop motion and show a fault; do not automatically resume motion after data returns. N-04 Owner: We want remote access, but the local stop must work during network failure.

Raw candidate and uncertainty input

Source locator: ../request.md, paragraph beginning Candidate design:. The following wording is retained verbatim:

Candidate design: temperature samples nominally every 1 s over a shared network, one MCU, one motor driver, end switches, dashboard. Unknown: sample jitter, motor travel time, stale-data detection, operator response, wind/rain constraints and safe position. A manager proposes a universal 50 ms stop deadline without a source. There are no test results or supplier reliability data.

The candidate component list is a design input, not an approved requirement baseline. Nominal 1 s sampling is not a maximum interval or an end-to-end latency bound. The unsupported 50 ms proposal is not used as a deadline or acceptance limit.

Review disposition

The requirement register contains 10 source-grounded draft records and 2 provisional derived records. All 12 have planned verification links; this is planning coverage only. The plan contains 14 verification activities and 4 stakeholder-validation activities, all planned, with execution, review and acceptance absent. The decision register contains D-01 through D-12. It locates incomplete acceptance criteria instead of supplying unsupported limits.

Immediate review priorities are D-01/D-02 (temperature qualification), D-03/D-04 (restart and local stop), D-05/D-06 (data loss and fault indication), and D-08/D-09 (movement and weather hazards). Remote scope and timing/reliability evidence also need resolution. The work can proceed as a draft; approval, firmware completion and physical acceptance require those decisions and measured evidence.

Execution environment: inherited Windows/PowerShell workspace. Host identity beyond the supplied environment, actual model identity, and actual model settings were unavailable to this exercise and are recorded as unknown. No model identity was inferred from tool documentation. No network, model API, credential, publication or live application mutation was used.

Source: evals/evidence/ho01/outputs/01-requirements.md

Requirements register

Baseline: GH-DRAFT-01. Source wording and locators are preserved in 00-review-guide.md. Every record is unapproved. “Shall” expresses proposed requirement wording, not approval or proof of feasibility.

Interpretation and measurement rules

  • System boundary: controller, temperature acquisition interface, local stop interface, motor driver, vent actuator/end switches, fault indication and dashboard interface. The shared network, operator and weather are interacting external entities. Exact sensor, vent and power arrangements await D-11.
  • T is an accepted inside-temperature reading in degrees Celsius. Whether a reading is valid, fresh and attributable to the inside sensor awaits D-01/D-05. A nominal 1 s stream does not establish uninterrupted physical temperature between samples.
  • Opening uses T >= 32 deg C and resets on every accepted T < 32 deg C, including one brief dip. No smoothing or debounce may hide a valid dip under N-01.
  • Closing uses the strict threshold T < 28 deg C and 60 s from N-01. Whether the interval must be uninterrupted, and how a rise or an invalid sample affects it, await D-02. No opening-reset rule is silently extended to closing.
  • Timer start, sensor-time versus reception-time semantics, maximum sample gap, quantization, accuracy and acceptance tolerance await D-01/D-02/D-05/D-10. Architecture suggestions are provisional until these decisions are resolved.
  • “Stop motion” is a required outcome. Disabling the driver is a mechanism; it does not prove physical arrest. D-04 separates local demand-to-inhibit latency from inhibit-to-physical-stop time. D-05 resolves missing-data timing. Neither threshold provides a supported universal 50 ms bound.

Source-grounded draft requirements

ID Proposed statement and conditions Source, rationale and relation Acceptance condition / unresolved part Accountable owner; proposed allocation; verification
RQ-01 The controller shall issue an opening demand when a valid inside-temperature reading has satisfied T >= 32 deg C for 30 s in enabled automatic mode, subject to stop/fault inhibition. N-01, request stakeholder paragraph; N-02/N-03 constrain permission to move. Preserves the high threshold and delay. Boundary stimuli at exactly 32 and just below it; no early demand; demand at expiry under an agreed timer/tolerance contract. Meaning of “stays,” timer origin and reaction tolerance: D-01/D-10. Actual vent opening completion: D-08/D-11. Owner with controls engineer; F-02/F-03 → C-02/C-03/C-04; VA-01, VA-13, VA-14.
RQ-02 The controller shall reset the opening qualification interval upon every valid inside-temperature reading below 32 deg C before that interval expires. N-01, request stakeholder paragraph; decomposition of RQ-01. A brief valid dip must not be filtered away. A valid dip immediately before expiry prevents that opening demand and a new 30 s interval is required. Equality at 32 does not reset. Missing/invalid samples and unseen dips: D-01/D-05. Owner with controls engineer; F-01/F-02 → C-02; VA-02, VA-11, VA-14.
RQ-03 The controller shall issue a closing demand below 28 deg C after the specified 60 s qualification in enabled automatic mode, subject to stop/fault inhibition. N-01, request stakeholder paragraph; N-02/N-03 constrain permission. Preserves the strict low threshold and duration. T = 28 deg C does not qualify; qualified T < 28 deg C produces no early closing demand and a demand at expiry. Continuity, reset policy, timer origin and tolerance: D-02/D-10; movement completion: D-08/D-11. Owner with controls engineer; F-02/F-03 → C-02/C-03/C-04; VA-03, VA-13, VA-14.
RQ-04 The controller shall make the local manual stop override every motion demand, including automatic and any remote demand. N-02, request stakeholder paragraph; N-04 establishes network-failure condition. Local stop asserted in each supported mode/direction prevents further commanded motion and stops current motion. Stop event, residual travel, physical stopping time and operating loads must be defined in D-04/D-09/D-11. Technician with hardware/controls engineers; F-03/F-04/F-05 → C-01/C-02/C-03/C-04; VA-04, VA-10, VA-13, VA-14.
RQ-05 After a local manual stop, the controller shall require an explicit operator action before automatic mode is resumed. N-02, request stakeholder paragraph. Stop release or data restoration alone must not re-enable automatic motion. Release the stop and exercise temperature thresholds; automatic mode remains disabled until the defined explicit action is accepted. Action, location, prerequisites and interaction with fault reset: D-03/D-04/D-07. Technician; F-03/F-05 → C-01/C-02/C-05; VA-05, VA-13.
RQ-06 If required temperature data has been missing for 5 s, the controller shall stop motion and inhibit motion while the condition persists. N-03, request stakeholder paragraph. Inhibition is the derived consequence of stopping with no usable feedback. Test both idle and moving cases around 5 s. At the defined expiry, stop is required; command-to-inhibit and physical stopping acceptance remain open. Last receipt/last valid sample origin, invalid/stale data treatment and scheduler allowance: D-05/D-10; physical stop: D-04/D-09. Maintenance with controls/hardware engineers; F-01/F-03/F-04 → C-02/C-03/C-04; VA-06, VA-11, VA-13, VA-14.
RQ-07 The controller shall indicate a missing-temperature-data fault when the 5 s missing-data condition occurs. N-03, request stakeholder paragraph; N-04 is relevant when the network also carries the dashboard. Observe an unambiguous fault at the selected indication point on expiry and during failed network conditions. Indicator location, persistence, visibility and indication latency: D-06/D-10. A remote dashboard alone is not established as available during network failure. Maintenance; F-06 → C-02/C-05 and proposed C-06; VA-07, VA-13, VA-14.
RQ-08 The controller shall not automatically resume motion after temperature data returns following a missing-data fault. N-03, request stakeholder paragraph. Return of telemetry is not authorization to move. Restore valid data while an opening/closing threshold qualifies; motion remains inhibited without the approved recovery action. Fault clearance versus automatic authorization and permissible human actions: D-03. Maintenance with technician; F-03/F-05 → C-02/C-01/C-05; VA-08, VA-13.
RQ-09 The system shall provide remote access within an owner-approved scope. N-04, request stakeholder paragraph; stakeholder intent requiring elaboration. The dashboard is a candidate mechanism, not a specified remote-control feature set. Scope, permissions, read versus command capability, authorization/security and availability acceptance are absent: D-07. This record cannot yet be baselined as measurable. Owner; F-07 → C-05/C-02/network; VA-09, SV-04.
RQ-10 The local manual stop shall remain effective during failure of the shared network. N-04, request stakeholder paragraph; N-02 defines stop behavior. With the temperature/dashboard network disconnected, stalled, congested or returning unusable data, local stop satisfies the approved RQ-04 acceptance. No network response is required on its actuation path. Full electrical/processor-fault independence is not claimed. Owner and technician with hardware engineer; F-04/F-05 → C-01/C-03/C-04; VA-10, VA-13, VA-14.

Provisional derived requirements

These requirements need engineering and stakeholder review. They do not introduce new stakeholder thresholds or standards obligations.

ID Proposed requirement Source/parent and rationale Acceptance gap and owner Proposed allocation and verification
DR-01 The controller shall accept data for automatic qualification and data-availability monitoring only under an explicit validity/freshness contract, and shall prevent duplicate, out-of-order or stale data from extending freshness or creating false qualification. RQ-01/RQ-02/RQ-03/RQ-06/RQ-08; N-01/N-03; candidate shared-network samples. Needed to prevent replayed or old readings from masking loss. Treating all invalid data as missing is a proposed conservative interpretation, not verbatim source wording. D-01/D-05 must set identity, accuracy, age/gap limits, timestamp/sequence rules, clock assumptions and invalid-data policy. Controls engineer owns definition; owner/maintenance confirm semantics. F-01/F-02 → C-02/network/sensor interface; VA-11, VA-06, VA-14.
DR-02 The controller and driver interface shall issue mutually exclusive open/close commands and apply stop/fault inhibition ahead of directional motion commands. RQ-04/RQ-06/RQ-10; N-02/N-03/N-04; candidate one motor driver. Engineering decomposition to avoid a conflicting command defeating stop. D-08 must define cancellation/reversal/deadtime and end-switch behavior; D-04 must define inhibit semantics. Demonstrate no simultaneous direction enables and no effective direction drive during asserted inhibit. Hardware/controls engineer owns contract. F-03/F-04 → C-02/C-03; VA-12, VA-04, VA-13, VA-14.

Baseline review findings

No source obligation has been dropped. N-01 decomposes into three records without weakening the brief-dip opening reset; N-02 yields override and explicit resumption; N-03 yields stopping, fault indication and no automatic recovery; N-04 yields remote intent and network-independent local stop. RQ-09 remains non-measurable until scope is agreed. Timing tolerances, physical stop limits, sampling interpretation and weather envelope remain approval blockers. Candidate end switches and other proposed mechanisms are architecture choices, not retroactively attributed to the owner. There is no supported reliability target, regulatory obligation, hazard class or 50 ms deadline in this input.

Source: evals/evidence/ho01/outputs/02-architecture.md

Architecture proposal

Configuration: GH-DRAFT-01 textual proposal. No modeling-tool project or deployed design was changed. Source IDs and requirement contracts are in 01-requirements.md; unresolved decisions are in 04-trace-and-decisions.md.

Boundary and proposed physical structure

The shared network carries nominally 1 s temperature samples and dashboard traffic. One MCU accepts eligible temperature readings, qualifies thresholds, arbitrates requests and manages mode/fault authorization. One motor driver commands the vent mechanism. End switches report direction-specific limits. The operator acts through a local stop and an explicit automatic-enable/recovery interface.

The candidate lacks a specified local stop actuation path. The preferred review option adds a local maintained/latching inhibit path to the driver's motion-enable circuit and an MCU observation input. Its direct inhibit does not require network or MCU message processing. A local fault indicator is also proposed because a dashboard on the failed network may be unreachable. Both are additions for review, with electrical compatibility, power-loss behavior and fault detection unproved.

flowchart LR
  S[Inside temperature source] -->|I-01 samples via shared network| M[C-02 single MCU]
  D[C-05 dashboard] <-->|I-05 remote interface via shared network| M
  L[C-01 local stop and explicit action interface] -->|I-02 stop status and action| M
  L -->|I-03 proposed direct latched inhibit| R[C-03 single motor driver]
  M -->|I-04 direction and enable| R
  R -->|I-07 motor power| V[C-04 vent motor and mechanism]
  E[C-07 end switches] -->|I-06 limits| M
  M -->|I-08 proposed local fault indication| A[C-06 local indicator]

All arrows are directional interface proposals. The diagram does not establish redundancy, independence from common power, electrical fail-safe behavior or sufficient motor stopping performance.

Functional decomposition and allocation

Function Transformation, input and output Applicable modes Requirements and raw sources Proposed components
F-01 Qualify data availability Temperature packets/time/identity → accepted reading or invalid/unavailable status and missing-data expiry All; motion authorization only when enabled RQ-06/RQ-08/DR-01; N-01/N-03 C-02, temperature interface/shared network
F-02 Qualify thermal demand Eligible readings/time → high interval, reset event, low interval and opening/closing demand AUTO_ENABLED; restart timer policy provisional RQ-01/RQ-02/RQ-03/DR-01; N-01 C-02
F-03 Arbitrate permission and direction Qualified/manual/remote requests, stop, fault, limits → inhibit or one eligible directional command All RQ-01/RQ-03/RQ-04/RQ-05/RQ-06/RQ-08/DR-02; N-01/N-02/N-03 C-02; C-03 final inhibit gate
F-04 Control and halt motion Enable/direction/local inhibit → motor energization/removal and vent movement OPENING, CLOSING, IDLE under orthogonal authorization flags RQ-04/RQ-06/RQ-10/DR-02; N-02/N-03/N-04 C-01/C-03/C-04; C-07 limits
F-05 Manage explicit authorization Local stop/release, recovery action, current data/fault → latched inhibition and deliberate automatic-enable state All RQ-05/RQ-08/RQ-10; N-02/N-03/N-04 C-01/C-02; C-05 only within D-07 scope
F-06 Indicate fault/status Data-loss fault and mode → observable fault/status All RQ-07; N-03 C-02/C-05; proposed C-06
F-07 Provide remote access Remote request/status exchange → owner-approved information/control operation D-07 scope; subordinate to stop/fault RQ-09/RQ-10; N-04 C-05/C-02/shared network

Component responsibilities and failure dependencies

Component Responsibility and interfaces Resource constraints / failure behavior to resolve
C-01 Local stop and action interface, proposed Assert direct inhibit (I-03), report stop state and deliberate operator action (I-02). Maintained/latching mechanism, wiring faults, release/reset semantics and contact behavior: D-03/D-04. Must not require network. An explicit auto-enable interface must be supplied; remote reset is not assumed.
C-02 One MCU, candidate F-01/F-02/F-03/F-05/F-06/F-07; I-01/I-02/I-04/I-05/I-06/I-08. Scheduler/clock accuracy, memory, CPU, resets, firmware, power and startup defaults unknown. Shared processor means thermal control and missing-data fault logic can fail together. Proposed output-default inhibit requires electrical validation.
C-03 One motor driver, candidate Translate exclusive commands and inhibit into motor power, I-03/I-04/I-07. Disable polarity, priority, propagation delay, braking/coasting, load/current/thermal limits and default state unknown. A shorted/stuck driver can defeat a logic-disable path; no fault tolerance is claimed.
C-04 Motor, vent and mechanical load Produce movement and physical halt, I-07. Travel time, inertia, gear behavior, holding capability, force, weather load and safe position unknown: D-08/D-09/D-11. Drive removal may permit coast or wind-driven movement.
C-05 Dashboard, candidate Remote access and status, I-05. Network failure makes availability uncertain. Scope, security, reconnection/replay and remote movement privileges await D-07. Must not own local stop enforcement.
C-06 Local fault indicator, proposed Show fault through I-08 when dashboard network fails. Type, power, visibility, latching and indication deadline await D-06. Common power can remove indication.
C-07 End switches, candidate Signal opening/closing limits through I-06. Switch count/location, polarity, wiring diagnostics, bounce, contradictory limits and direct driver interruption unknown. They do not establish mid-travel position or stop distance.

Dependencies to review: shared supply/ground, reset and clock; one MCU and common firmware/configuration; one driver; network used for both sensing and remote access; shared enclosure/environment; stop wiring and maintenance; operator availability. A direct stop path reduces network dependence but retains driver, power and mechanical common causes. No failure probability, availability or independence claim is supportable without D-12 evidence.

Mode and transition contract

Use orthogonal authorization flags and motion state rather than one mode that loses simultaneous stop/fault information. Suggested flags are auto_authorized, local_stop_latched and data_fault_latched; data eligibility and end limits are additional guards. Motion state is IDLE/OPENING/CLOSING. These are proposed logical names, not code.

Event / condition Proposed state/output response Basis and unresolved decision
Startup/reset Driver commanded inhibited; auto_authorized=false; collect qualified data before any deliberate enable. Conservative proposal, D-03/D-11; N-02/N-03 do not specify power-cycle recovery.
Local stop asserted in any state Direct local inhibit asserts; latch stop, clear auto authorization, cancel pending demands, request stop; preserve any fault latch. RQ-04/RQ-05/RQ-10; N-02/N-04; D-04 sets physical outcome.
Local stop released Do not automatically clear authorization inhibition or restart. RQ-05; N-02. Whether physical latch release and explicit enable can be a single action: D-03/D-04.
Missing-data expiry Set data fault latch; clear auto authorization; inhibit/stop; show fault. Stop has priority over demand qualification at the same processing instant. RQ-06/RQ-07/RQ-08/DR-02; N-03; event origin and latency D-05/D-10.
Data returns Update current data eligibility; retain fault latch and disabled automatic authorization. RQ-08; N-03. No motion just because high/low readings return.
Explicit recovery/enable action Proposed guard: no active local stop, qualified fresh data and resolved active fault. Acknowledge fault and enable only under D-03's approved action protocol. Reset thermal timers before new qualification, proposed. RQ-05/RQ-08; N-02/N-03; timer reset on recovery is a design choice, D-01/D-03.
High/low qualification completes with permission Submit one directional demand through arbitration. Motion continuation/cancellation/reversal policy remains undefined. RQ-01/RQ-03/DR-02; N-01; D-08 must decide persistence of a qualified demand during travel.
Direction-specific end limit Proposed: inhibit further drive in that direction. Contradictory limits or failed switch behavior must be specified before implementation. Candidate end switches; D-08/D-11; no added source obligation is asserted.
Concurrent stop, data loss and remote/thermal demand Retain both inhibition reasons; no effective directional drive; clearing one reason leaves the other effective. RQ-04/RQ-05/RQ-06/RQ-08/RQ-10/DR-02; N-02/N-03/N-04.

Interface contracts

Interface Source → target; exchanged item and units/format Timing and validity responsibility Error handling / missing agreement
I-01 Inside source via shared network → C-02; temperature in deg C, source identity, proposed sequence/timestamp/quality fields Nominal 1 s is input fact. Maximum gap/jitter/latency and field schema unspecified. Sensor owns measurement; MCU owns acceptance/availability. D-01/D-05 set stale/invalid rules and clock relationship. Duplicate/reordered data must not renew freshness under DR-01. Lost network can make temperature unavailable.
I-02 C-01 → C-02; asserted stop state and explicit operator action, digital semantics TBD Local electrical path; no network dependency. MCU owns latches/guards; event debounce/detection latency TBD. D-03/D-04 set active polarity, failed wiring response and distinction between stop release, fault acknowledgment and enable. Debounce must not silently postpone stop.
I-03 C-01 → C-03; proposed hardwired maintained/latching motion inhibit Stop circuit and driver own final disable; polarity, edge reference and delay TBD. D-04/D-11 confirm direct inhibit overrides I-04. No supported claim for stuck-driver failure. Reset cannot bypass an active stop.
I-04 C-02 → C-03; OPEN/CLOSE/ENABLE or equivalent digital contract Exclusive commands; inhibit wins. MCU owns command consistency; driver owns interpretation and electrical response. D-04/D-08 define default inhibit, reversal sequence/deadtime and fault behavior. Interface delay budget unknown.
I-05 C-05 ↔ C-02 through shared network; status and approved remote operations Rates, delivery semantics, freshness, authentication and permissions TBD under D-07. Network failure cannot disable I-03. Reject stale/queued movement commands after reconnection under a proposed D-07 protocol. Local stop reset by remote command is unresolved, not permitted by this draft.
I-06 C-07 → C-02; direction-specific reached-limit digital indications Switch and MCU own electrical/read/debounce contract; latency TBD. D-08/D-11 address absent/stuck/contradictory switches; travel timeout value requires measured travel evidence.
I-07 C-03 → C-04; motor electrical power, polarity/current/voltage TBD Driver/mechanical owner supplies load, inertia, response and holding data. Disable may brake or coast; actual physical stop/holding behavior must be measured across D-09 envelope.
I-08 C-02 → proposed C-06, and status via I-05; missing-data fault/mode indication Indicator availability, timing, content and persistence await D-06/D-10. Local indicator avoids network transport dependence; supply loss remains common cause. Fault reset display behavior follows D-03.

Timing, resources and trade records

Proposed data-loss origin is controller monotonic receipt time of the last accepted fresh reading. Eligibility may also need sensor acquisition age; unsynchronized sensor time cannot be subtracted without an agreed clock mapping. At the 5 s expiry, a missing-data event must take precedence. Whether invalid packets count as missing and whether sensor acquisition time instead governs expiry remain D-05 decisions. A 1 s nominal period yields no proven worst-case sampling or freshness margin.

Path / budget Contributions requiring evidence Supported value / gap
Physical threshold crossing → eligible reading Sensor accuracy/response + acquisition gap/jitter + network delay + validation/scheduling All maximums unknown. Under a sample-based D-01 contract, 30/60 s start from the defined eligible sample; these intervals do not establish physical crossing-to-motion latency.
Eligible thermal interval → command → vent at limit 30 s opening or 60 s closing qualification + scheduler + arbitration + driver response + travel Qualification durations from N-01. All other terms and reaction tolerance unknown.
Local stop event → physical arrest Contact/input response + direct inhibit circuit/driver delay + mechanical deceleration/coast Sum unknown. Proposed I-03 excludes network and MCU scheduler from direct actuation; 50 ms is unsupported. Event origin and residual movement require D-04.
Last eligible datum → missing-data physical stop Defined 5 s absence interval + expiry evaluation delay + arbitration/output delay + driver delay + mechanical stop 5 s from N-03; remaining terms and deadline interpretation unresolved D-05/D-10. Cannot claim physical halt at exactly 5 s.
Missing-data expiry → observable fault Detection + display update + display response; network transport if remote display Deadline unknown; local proposed indicator removes network transport term.

No CPU, memory, electrical current, thermal or communication budget can be closed from the inputs. Owners must measure worst-case paths and allocate limits/margins once justified; no numerical margins are invented.

Decision record Alternatives and review recommendation Evidence, consequence and revisit trigger
AD-01 Local stop allocation (A) network/dashboard stop; (B) local MCU input commanding disable; (C) direct local maintained/latching driver inhibit plus MCU status. Recommend C for review. A conflicts with N-04. B removes network from the button but remains MCU/scheduling dependent. C best supports N-02/N-04 with the single-MCU candidate; adds wiring/latch integration, retains common driver/power/mechanics. No electrical tests exist. Revisit on D-04/D-11 or driver incompatibility.
AD-02 Data validity and time Receipt-only presence; sensor age only; combined eligibility using identity/sequence and age with a controller monotonic timeout. Recommend combined eligibility for review. N-01/N-03 plus shared network motivate stale/replay handling. Additional metadata/clock contract may be needed. No age/gap bound selected. Revisit on D-01/D-05 and actual sensor protocol.
AD-03 Fault display Dashboard only; local indication plus dashboard status. Recommend local indication plus dashboard. N-03 demands visible fault; N-04/shared network exposes dashboard availability risk. Adds proposed C-06 and supply/visibility questions. Revisit on D-06.
AD-04 Recovery protocol Auto-restart on packet return; deliberate guarded recovery/automatic-enable action. Recommend deliberate guarded action. Auto-restart conflicts with N-03; deliberate auto resumption also supports N-02. Exact number/location of actions unapproved D-03/D-07. Revisit on operator validation.

Architecture closure requires agreed interval/validity semantics, interface electrical data, motion policy, environment and measured timing. This proposal supports review, not a claim that the candidate design is already adequate.

Source: evals/evidence/ho01/outputs/03-verification-plan.md

Verification and stakeholder-validation plan

Plan baseline: GH-DRAFT-01. Every activity is planned. None has been executed, passed, failed, reviewed or accepted. No supplier reliability data or test evidence was supplied. Artifact consistency checks in 05-artifact-checks.md do not verify controller requirements.

Configuration and acceptance controls

Before an activity is executable, record its approved requirement/design revision; decision dispositions; hardware wiring/sensor/driver/motor/vent/end-switch/indicator identifiers and revisions; firmware, build and configuration hashes; network topology/settings; temperature packet schema; timer/clock assumptions; load/weather envelope; instrument identity/calibration/uncertainty; fixture and procedure version; operator roles; observation channels; and deviations. A software-only setup must be labeled with its model scope and must not be used to claim hardware stopping behavior.

Observe both command/inhibit signals and physical vent movement where stopping or opening/closing is claimed. Timestamp sensor acquisition when available, receipt/acceptance, timer events, stop actuation, driver electrical response, physical motion and fault visibility. Use a defined common measurement time reference and uncertainty budget; do not assume unsynchronized clocks are comparable. Temperature boundary offsets and measurement tolerances must be selected from the resolved sensor contract, not arbitrary constants.

For each activity below, “acceptance” is the intended criterion. A D-ID indicates missing approval/input. These cases remain planned and acceptance-blocked until the decision and numeric/electrical contract are resolved; they cannot produce an unconditional pass in their present form. Proposed future evidence names are templates, not existing artifacts.

Requirement verification activities

ID; requirements and raw sources Method, preconditions and procedure / stimulus Expected observation and acceptance Environment, limitations, owner/reviewer; planned evidence
VA-01; RQ-01; N-01 with N-02/N-03 guards Test + timer-contract analysis. Start enabled, fresh eligible data, no inhibition, vent able to open. Inject exactly 32 deg C, values above, and just-below controls with agreed timestamps. Inspect immediately before/at/after 30 s. No early opening demand; demand at the agreed 30 s expiry; physical opening observable in hardware under the approved movement contract. Below-threshold controls do not qualify. D-01/D-08/D-10/D-11 block final timing/physical acceptance. Deterministic packet bench for timing logic, actual motor/vent for movement. Controls engineer executes; owner-designated reviewer. Proposed future-evidence/VA-01-result.md plus raw synchronized trace.
VA-02; RQ-02; N-01 Test. While high qualification is active, inject one valid sub-32 sample immediately before expiry and resume high samples. Repeat at several phase offsets and at equality 32. No filtering may suppress an accepted dip. Sub-32 resets elapsed opening qualification to its defined origin; no old-interval demand; renewed high stream must qualify for a full new 30 s. Equality 32 retains qualification. Undetected between-sample dips cannot be proven absent by this test; D-01/D-05/D-10. Packet bench and firmware trace; controls engineer; owner reviews interpretation. Proposed future-evidence/VA-02-result.md.
VA-03; RQ-03; N-01 Test + analysis. Enabled, valid data, vent able to close. Apply below-28, exactly-28 and above-28 readings; check 60 s boundaries. Apply interruption/rise/invalid cases according to D-02's selected rule. No qualification from equality 28; no early closing demand; demand after approved 60 s interval and hardware closing behavior. Interruption behavior matches D-02 rather than an assumed opening-reset rule. D-02/D-08/D-10/D-11. Packet bench plus hardware travel case; controls engineer; owner reviewer. Proposed future-evidence/VA-03-result.md.
VA-04; RQ-04/DR-02; N-02/N-03/N-04 Inspection + hardware test. Inspect direct inhibit wiring/priority. Actuate local stop during opening, closing, idle, threshold expiry and each enabled remote mode; hold conflicting demands active. Measure local event → inhibit → physical stop. Local stop dominates; no new effective drive while stop asserted; current movement halts within the justified D-04 limit and residual-travel constraint. Release does not erase latch authorization. No 50 ms criterion is used. D-04/D-07/D-09/D-11. Guarded actual driver/motor/vent fixture across approved load envelope; hardware/controls engineer; technician and owner reviewer. Proposed future-evidence/VA-04-result.md, wiring inspection and scope/motion traces.
VA-05; RQ-05; N-02 Test + demonstration. Enter local stop from enabled mode, release it, maintain qualifying hot/cold data, vary dashboard/network reconnection. Attempt the defined explicit action with and without required guards. Release and reconnection alone cannot enable automatic motion. Only the agreed deliberate action under valid guards permits new automatic qualification. D-03/D-04/D-07; startup behavior recorded separately. Controller/UI bench; technician executes usability demonstration; controls engineer reviews logic. Proposed future-evidence/VA-05-result.md.
VA-06; RQ-06/DR-01; N-03/N-01 Test + worst-case timing analysis. Start idle and moving, stop required data at known last eligible origin. Exercise just before/at/after 5 s, variable jitter, loss, invalid/replayed/reordered packets and MCU scheduling load. Defined absence expiry triggers inhibit/stop; no packet deemed ineligible renews freshness; motion remains inhibited during loss. Measure detection and physical stop separately. Deadline origin, permitted scheduling delay, invalid-data policy and physical halt criteria await D-04/D-05/D-09/D-10. Packet fault-injection bench and hardware halt case; controls engineer; maintenance/hardware reviewer. Proposed future-evidence/VA-06-result.md and latency analysis.
VA-07; RQ-07; N-03 Test + demonstration. Trigger 5 s missing-data fault with network present and disconnected; observe the selected display from the intended operator position and exercise persistence/reset. Unambiguous missing-data fault appears at the approved indication point by the approved deadline and has the agreed persistence. Dashboard availability must be checked rather than assumed. D-06/D-10. Actual indicator/dashboard, representative visibility conditions from D-06; maintenance executes, owner reviews visibility. Proposed future-evidence/VA-07-result.md.
VA-08; RQ-08; N-03 Test. After data-loss stop, restore eligible high data and then low data, including already qualifying-looking packets; attempt no action, stop release, acknowledgment alone and the approved enable protocol. Restoration alone never resumes movement. Any movement after recovery requires the defined deliberate permission; retained simultaneous stop/fault remains effective. D-03/D-05/D-07. Controller/UI bench; controls engineer; maintenance/technician reviewer. Proposed future-evidence/VA-08-result.md.
VA-09; RQ-09; N-04 Inspection + test/demonstration after remote scope is approved. Exercise each permitted read/control operation and rejected operation; failure, reconnection, stale commands and permissions. Approved remote features operate to D-07 criteria; operations outside scope and prohibited reset/bypass fail. No measurable remote criterion exists yet; activity definition is blocked on D-07. Actual dashboard/network/controller configuration; responsible software engineer; owner reviewer. Proposed future-evidence/VA-09-result.md and scope checklist.
VA-10; RQ-10/RQ-04; N-04/N-02 Inspection + hardware fault injection. Disconnect temperature/dashboard network, stall/congest it and supply unusable packets. Actuate the local stop before, during and after the 5 s data-fault transition while moving in each direction. Local stop satisfies RQ-04 without a network response; loss of network does not inhibit local stop actuation. Separate measurement of manual path and automatic data-loss path. D-04/D-05/D-09/D-11. Actual local stop/driver/vent fixture; hardware engineer; technician/owner reviewer. This checks network independence only, not all common failures. Proposed future-evidence/VA-10-result.md.
VA-11; DR-01/RQ-02/RQ-06; N-01/N-03 Schema inspection + tests. Apply wrong sensor identity, duplicate/older sequence, stale acquisition age, invalid quality, absent timestamp, unsynchronized clock, implausible/non-numeric values and bursts with nominal/variable spacing according to approved I-01 contract. Each case has a defined accept/reject outcome; invalid/stale data do not falsely complete thermal qualification or mask absence. Temperature acceptance range, age limit, clock mapping and invalid policy remain D-01/D-05 decisions. Sensor-interface packet harness; controls/sensor engineer; owner/maintenance reviewer. Proposed future-evidence/VA-11-result.md with case matrix.
VA-12; DR-02; N-02/N-03/N-04 Inspection + signal-level tests/analysis. Submit simultaneous open/close, a reversal, stop concurrent with direction, expiry concurrent with remote command, and end-limit changes. Capture all driver inputs/output states. Never assert effective open and close concurrently; inhibit wins against all direction requests; reversal/default outputs comply with D-04/D-08 electrical and deadtime contract. A trace proves only exercised sequences, not all schedules. Driver interface fixture and actual firmware; controls/hardware engineer; independent reviewer only if program later requires it. Proposed future-evidence/VA-12-result.md.
VA-13; RQ-01/RQ-03/RQ-04/RQ-05/RQ-06/RQ-07/RQ-08/RQ-10/DR-02; N-01/N-02/N-03/N-04 State-transition analysis + scenario tests. Cover startup, MCU reset, held stop, data loss, overlapping stop/fault, data return, release of only one inhibit, threshold expiry concurrent with inhibit, explicit recovery and network reconnection. All source guard conditions preserved; no implicit authorization on release/return/reconnection; overlapping latches retained; prioritized inhibition works. Startup, timer reset and recovery policies require D-01/D-03/D-04/D-05/D-08/D-11. Proposed state-table review first, then exact firmware/hardware revision. Controls engineer; technician/maintenance reviewers. Proposed future-evidence/VA-13-result.md and transition-coverage matrix.
VA-14; RQ-01/RQ-02/RQ-03/RQ-04/RQ-06/RQ-07/RQ-10/DR-01/DR-02; N-01/N-02/N-03/N-04 Analysis + targeted worst-case measurement. Close budgets from sensor acquisition through transport, scheduler, arbitration, driver, movement and display. Quantify uncertainty/clock drift; include overload/jitter and approved load/weather cases. All allocated path bounds and margins meet approved criteria and retain threshold/duration semantics. Nominal 1 s rate and unsupported 50 ms are insufficient. Missing component maxima, limits and measurement tolerances block closure: D-01/D-04/D-05/D-06/D-09/D-10/D-11. Versioned budget and actual instrumentation traces; hardware/controls engineer; owner reviewer. Proposed future-evidence/VA-14-result.md plus budget workbook or Markdown.

Stakeholder validation activities

These validate intended use and decision adequacy. They do not substitute for requirement verification.

ID Participants, scenario and question Intended acceptance / output State
SV-01; N-01, D-01/D-02 Owner and controls engineer review sequences at 32/28, sampled versus continuous qualification, brief dips, gaps and timer origins. Owner confirms the operational interpretation and rationale for 30/60 s and threshold behavior; record an agreed source amendment if intent changes. Planned; no stakeholder decision supplied.

Include delayed/absent human response. Confirm controls are understandable and cannot accidentally restart; agree location/action protocol and indication. Operator response is characterized, never assumed to meet a safety deadline. Planned.
SV-03; N-01/N-03/N-04, D-08/D-09/D-11 Owner, technician and mechanical/safety engineer assess mid-travel stop, wind/rain, unattended operation and power/network loss. Agree operating envelope, hazards, permissible residual motion, holding behavior and safe-position strategy. Explicitly reconcile any weather-driven repositioning with N-02/N-03 stop inhibition. Planned; no safe position inferred.

Evidence lifecycle and reporting

Use an executed-result record only after actual execution. Each record must contain evidence ID; VA/SV ID; result pass/fail/inconclusive; observed values and uncertainty; actual existing raw-artifact paths; exact requirement/design/input revisions or hashes; tool/instrument and version; execution time; operator; deviations; unresolved failures; and scope (logic bench, simulation or physical hardware). Keep separate review records with reviewer, disposition and date, and separate acceptance records with authorized owner and disposition. A result may be executed but unreviewed or unaccepted.

No independent-review, tool-qualification or certification requirement is present in the source. If one is introduced, establish its program basis and update the plan; do not infer compliance from a test name. Any later formal proof must identify encoded properties, assumptions, time bounds, fairness/vacuity checks and the mapping to implementation. No proof is proposed as already performed.

Current coverage: 12/12 requirement records have planned verification links; 0/12 are verified, reviewed or accepted. There are 14 planned VA activities and 4 planned SV activities; 0 executed results. Failed/inconclusive result records: none, because there has been no execution. Stale evidence: none supplied to assess. Missing evidence and unresolved acceptance definitions remain gaps, not passes. Final claims must be reconciled to exact configuration and changes must invalidate or rejustify affected evidence.

Decisions required for a final design

All entries are open. Owners below are proposed accountable roles, not evidence of agreement or assigned personnel. A final disposition should record decision, source amendment if any, rationale, date/approver, changed artifact IDs and affected verification activities.

ID Decision / missing acceptance definition Supported proposal or options, with consequence Proposed owner; affected records
D-01 What constitutes a valid inside reading and “stays at/above” in a sampled stream? Define accuracy, sensor identity, first qualifying event, timestamp origin, maximum gap/jitter and invalid/gap reset behavior. Propose qualification over eligible samples on controller monotonic time, reset high timer on every eligible sub-32 sample and on invalidity/gap per approved rule. This cannot establish all between-sample physical dips. Continuous physical-temperature intent would need additional sampling/sensing justification. No numerical gap/age/accuracy bound is selected. Owner + sensor/controls engineer; RQ-01/RQ-02/DR-01, I-01, VA-01/VA-02/VA-11/VA-14, SV-01.
D-02 Does the 60 s closing interval require uninterrupted <28? What resets it; what happens at 28, gaps and recovery? Propose uninterrupted eligible below-28 samples and reset at >=28, with new qualification after inhibition, but this is unapproved. Source only explicitly states a reset for opening. Owner + controls engineer; RQ-03, F-02, VA-03/SV-01.
D-03 What explicit actions clear manual-stop authorization and data-fault inhibition? Can acknowledgment and automatic enable be combined? Define startup/power-cycle state and response if operator never acts. Propose deliberate guarded enable only with stop released and fresh data; preserve fault/stop reasons separately. Propose inhibited startup and restarted thermal timers. N-03 forbids automatic movement on return but does not prescribe the specific reset protocol. Operator response time is unknown and cannot be credited as protection. Technician + maintenance + owner; RQ-05/RQ-08, F-05, VA-05/VA-08/VA-13, SV-02.
D-04 Define local stop event reference, physical stopping criterion, allowable residual travel/force, load envelope, latency and release/reset wiring. Resolve manager's 50 ms proposal. Propose AD-01 direct local latching inhibit; distinguish contact-to-driver and driver-to-physical-halt times. Derive justified limits from hazards and mechanical/driver data, then measure. No source supports a universal 50 ms bound; neither acceptance nor feasibility is established. Technician/owner + hardware/mechanical/safety engineer; RQ-04/RQ-05/RQ-10/DR-02, I-02/I-03/I-04/I-07, VA-04/VA-10/VA-14.
D-05 Does “missing for 5 s” start at last packet receipt, last accepted fresh receipt or sample acquisition? How do stale/duplicate/invalid packets, clock mapping and scheduler latency affect detection? Propose last accepted fresh receipt on MCU monotonic clock, with separate acquisition-age eligibility and rejected packets not refreshing it. Treat invalid/stale as unavailable only if approved. Define the event at the 5 s threshold and separate detection/output/physical stop response. Do not replace source 5 s with an invented timeout. Maintenance + controls/sensor engineer; RQ-06/RQ-08/DR-01, I-01, VA-06/VA-08/VA-11/VA-14.
D-06 Where is the missing-data fault observable during network loss? Define indicator content, visibility, timing, persistence and clearing. Propose C-06 local fault indication plus dashboard status. Dashboard-only depends on the same failed network. Local power-loss display availability still needs assessment. Maintenance + owner; RQ-07, AD-03, I-08, VA-07/SV-02.
D-07 Define remote access: monitor/control, authorized roles, security, availability, stale-command treatment and whether remote recovery is allowed. Dashboard is candidate only. Propose stop/fault override all remote commands and no remote clearance of a local stop until expressly approved. Scope and measurable acceptance remain absent. Owner + software/security/controls engineer; RQ-09/RQ-05/RQ-10, I-05, VA-09/VA-05/VA-10, SV-04.
D-08 How does a qualified demand persist during travel? Define cancellation/reversal, simultaneous demands, end-limit handling, switch failure and travel timeout. Source does not specify completion time or motion policy. Propose exclusive directions and end-limit inhibit. Reversal deadtime and timeout must follow actual driver/travel evidence; no values selected. Owner + mechanical/hardware/controls engineer; RQ-01/RQ-03/DR-02, C-03/C-04/C-07, I-04/I-06/I-07, VA-01/VA-03/VA-12/VA-13.
D-09 Define wind/rain/temperature/load envelope, hazards, safe position and holding behavior after stop or power/data loss. Neither open nor closed is justified as universally safe. N-02/N-03 require stopping; automatic weather repositioning could conflict and needs an explicit source decision. Mid-travel stop can leave exposure or allow wind-driven movement. Owner + mechanical/safety engineer; RQ-04/RQ-06/RQ-10, C-04, VA-04/VA-06/VA-10/VA-14/SV-03.

Preserve 30/60/5 s source values; define their event semantics and justified tolerance. Unknown scheduling and network maxima prevent closed budgets. Nominal 1 s sampling is not a bound. Controls/hardware engineer + owner/maintenance; RQ-01/RQ-02/RQ-03/RQ-04/RQ-06/RQ-07/RQ-10, VA-14 and affected boundary tests.
D-11 Select actual sensor, MCU, driver, motor/vent, switches, power/defaults, wiring and indicator interfaces. Obtain mechanical travel/holding and electrical disable data. Retain single MCU/driver as candidate. Validate direct inhibit and default states; do not assume disable brakes, end switches are diagnostic or power restoration cannot move. Hardware/mechanical engineer; all physical allocations, I-01 through I-08, VA-04/VA-10/VA-12/VA-13/VA-14.

There are no test results or supplier reliability data.

Engineering performance observations

These runs exercised all 13 shipped skills across 19 active cases, including a full-catalog typo task, and five matched no-package baseline tasks. Participants worked from frozen packets; the supplied requests, selected skill bytes, actual outputs, run records and collection hashes are retained in this directory. The protocol and original case/rubric snapshots precede production.

Independent agent review found 23 of the 24 outputs met every case criterion. The task-plus-domain HO-13 response had one consequential ambiguity: its timing plan classified an above-limit point estimate as failed while also classifying an overlapping uncertainty interval as inconclusive, without precedence. Its original output remains unchanged; the targeted tuning record records the subsequent instruction change and fresh exercise.

Design, reasoning and comparison review assesses 15 outputs. Domain and operational review assesses the other nine. Their adjacent JSON records retain individual criteria, located evidence, hashes and limitations. Four of five matched tasks tied at the rubric ceiling; the baseline HO-13 avoided the ambiguity found in the skill arm. This sample does not establish an advantage from the skills.

Start with the actual skill-assisted revision, baseline revision, director explanation, or negative-routing result. The last contains only the requested corrected word; its record reports no skill file read.

All input bytes were checked. Three early design-case run records received a final metadata pass after their per-case completion notice; the response bodies and their hash maps did not change. The independent review retains old/new record hashes and the producer's clarification. Earlier authoring-end timestamps were overwritten, so those records cannot support precise production-time comparisons.

These are instruction-restricted smoke exercises on a shared host. Each producer handled several cases in one context; exact served model/settings and costs were unavailable. Skill reads are participant-reported, not native activation telemetry. Reviewers are separate agents, not an independent professional acceptance board. Criterion coverage is not statistical performance, hardware verification or a claim of market leadership. Publisher PDFs retrieved during inspection remain at the original workspace locations; URLs and retrieval hashes are preserved.

Source: evals/evidence/performance-20261113/none/HO-09/outputs/output.md

The outcome is reliable drinking-water service through seasonal demand changes and treatment maintenance. A lower unit production cost is useful only within a concept that delivers that service. Plant size is a means, not the outcome.

The stated staffing limit is two locations; confirm whether this means two continuously staffed sites, two sites in total, or a limit on the available operator roster before treating unattended units as feasible. Storm road closures are an operating condition that constrains replenishment, repair and access. Seasonal demand is a design condition requiring an actual demand profile. The sponsor's preference for the largest plant and its reported unit-cost advantage are preferences, not a requirement to select it. No interruption tolerance, storage volume, outage duration, capital budget or alternative cost is supplied.

Useful concept What it could contribute What must be established
Larger central plant with the same single production path Production capacity and the stated unit-cost advantage Whether it can keep producing during maintenance. Extra capacity alone does not remove the interruption mechanism.
Central treatment with independently maintainable treatment trains Continued production at one staffed location while a train is isolated Remaining capacity during maintenance, isolation arrangements, and shared vulnerabilities in intake, power, controls and distribution. This is a design option, not a supplied capability.
Distributed treatment within the staffing limit An alternative production source and potentially shorter delivery paths Which sites require attendance; ability to operate and maintain them when roads close; potable-water assurance; and whether shared source, power or distribution failures defeat the independence. More than two attended locations is infeasible under the stated limit. Remote or unattended operation is unproven.
Additional clean-water storage A finite bridge across production outages and possibly seasonal peaks Deliverable usable volume, water quality during storage, demand during outages, pumping/distribution availability, and sufficient production time and capacity to refill. Nominal tank volume is not guaranteed delivered supply.
Treatment resilience plus storage Coverage of both short interruptions and longer maintenance or access delays The smallest combination meeting the agreed service objective and staffing constraint; its whole-service costs remain unknown.

I would first reconstruct a few representative maintenance and storm scenarios using plant outage records, repair/access delays, seasonal demand and the distribution layout. Agree how much interruption, if any, the sponsor will accept and whether that applies to all demand or an explicitly agreed essential-service level. Check the full path from source to customer: independent treatment or a full tank will not help if the same failed pump or main prevents delivery.

The question most likely to change the recommendation is: Can usable, potable and deliverable storage cover the demand deficit throughout the longest outage the district agrees it must withstand, including storm-delayed repair, and refill before another such outage? Compare usable volume with the time-integrated deficit between required delivery and available production, including an explicitly justified reserve. The necessary values are not supplied.

If that bridge is feasible and the delivery path remains available, investigate storage with maintainability improvements to the existing plant first. If it is infeasible, investigate independent treatment capacity that can be maintained within the two-location staffing limit, with storage for transition periods. Compare the largest central proposal on the same service scenarios, whole-service cost and maintenance coverage before selecting it. No option is established as cheapest or compliant from the given facts.

Source: evals/evidence/performance-20261113/none/HO-09/request.md

An isolated district needs reliable drinking-water service. Current service is interrupted when the one treatment plant needs maintenance. Candidate proposals are a larger central plant, smaller distributed treatment units, or additional clean-water storage. Demand varies seasonally. Operators can staff only two locations; access roads close during storms. The sponsor prefers the largest plant because its unit production cost is lowest. Compare useful concepts and explain what you would investigate first. Preserve the sponsor's outcome, distinguish hard constraints from preferences, and identify the question most likely to change your recommendation. Do not make up performance, cost or staffing data.

Source: evals/evidence/performance-20261113/none/HO-12/outputs/output.md

The city improved one step for applicants: submission fell from 40 to 10 minutes. The unresolved problem is the time and uncertainty between requesting permission and receiving a decision that allows urgent work to proceed. Approval still takes 30 days, and the shared engineering, land-record and inspection services constrain that flow. A chatbot may help people submit complete information, but the facts do not establish that questions at intake are what keeps cases waiting.

Use an end-to-end service boundary from an applicant's first attempt to apply through a communicated approval, refusal or other explicit disposition. Track applicant work and resubmission as well as the city's work. Engineering review, land records and any inspections needed before a decision belong within the analysis even when another organization controls them. Distinguish that analysis boundary from the director's authority to change staffing, priorities or outside commitments. Track permission to start urgent work as an outcome; construction execution and later inspections can remain outside the initial improvement scope unless they actually gate that permission.

Measure What it resolves
Calendar time from initial submission to decision, with median, upper-tail and oldest unresolved age, separated by urgent/routine and case complexity Whether service is improving for applicants, including people still waiting. Confirm what the reported 30 days means.
Time at each handoff: ready and waiting, active review, blocked for information, and awaiting an outside response Where delay accumulates and who can change it; account for parallel activities without adding overlapping times twice.
Arrival and completion rates, work in progress and backlog age by stage and priority Whether queues are growing and whether moving work merely shifts the delay.
First-submission completeness, rework and repeated contacts Whether intake assistance, including a chatbot, addresses a material cause of delay.
Urgent cases meeting an agreed need-by date and reasons for misses Whether the service supports time-critical work; define urgency and escalation ownership explicitly.
Decision accuracy, required-review completion, avoidable reversals and applicant access across channels Whether faster processing preserves sound decisions and access to the service.

The next decision should authorize a bounded examination of actual cases and a small flow-improvement pilot, with a named service owner and participation from the three shared services. Reconstruct event timelines for recent routine, urgent and still-open cases; establish whether each bottleneck is waiting for scarce capacity, missing information, scheduling or a dependency. Agree baseline measures, pilot scope and review date before changing the process. No numeric improvement target is justified yet.

If complete cases spend most of their time waiting for engineering or inspections, pilot coordinated scheduling, a visible shared queue and an explicit urgent-case route with agreed capacity. Preserve required checks, monitor effects on routine cases and prevent indefinite starvation. If records requests or incomplete submissions dominate, first address access, information exchange or application guidance. A chatbot merits a bounded trial only if evidence shows that the questions it can answer contribute materially to rework or delay; compare its impact on complete submissions and total decision time, including the human support it requires.

Three facts would most sharpen the decision: where urgent cases spend their 30 days; who can approve urgency and allocate shared capacity; and whether engineering, records and inspections can proceed concurrently. The conditional recommendation is to improve the limiting stage and its handoffs first, then decide whether a chatbot is a useful part of that change.

Source: evals/evidence/performance-20261113/none/HO-12/request.md

A city digitized its flood-permit service. Online applications now take applicants 10 minutes instead of 40, but approval still takes 30 days and urgent work is delayed. Engineering review, land records and outside inspections are shared bottlenecks. The director asks for an AI chatbot. Stage Maximum
COMP-1 interface processing 150 ms

Controller architecture, proposed revision B

This is a proposed reconciliation and implementation work plan. No implementation option has been selected or measured for revision B.

COMP-1 input interface forwards the sensor input to COMP-2 detector. COMP-2 sends the alarm command to COMP-3 local annunciator over IFC-2. IFC-1 is the sensor-to-detector interface. IFC-3 carries operator stop/resume intent to COMP-2.

The current allocations are retained below as an unresolved design baseline, not a feasible revision-B budget. They assume serial, nonoverlapping stages.

Stage Current maximum allocation
COMP-1 interface processing 150 ms
COMP-2 detection 80 ms
COMP-3 warning assertion 30 ms
Sum 260 ms

The sum exceeds the 200 ms REQ-7 criterion by 60 ms. This allocation cannot guarantee the new requirement. It is not a measurement proving every implementation run takes 260 ms. Establish whether sampling phase, scheduling, queuing, IFC-2 transfer and annunciator response are already included; any uncovered delay must also be budgeted from the unchanged input trigger through actual local warning assertion. The historical 460 ms observation cannot be explained by the supplied 260 ms allocation alone; its configuration and detailed timing records are insufficient to reconcile that gap.

Engineering options for selection, not approved changes:

  • Reduce COMP-1 processing latency through a measured and justified implementation change. With the other two allocations unchanged, 90 ms for COMP-1 would merely reach 200 ms and leave no allowance for uncovered delay or uncertainty. A robust allocation must include those contributions and justified margin.
  • Reduce latency across COMP-1, COMP-2 and COMP-3 and explicitly allocate any interface or scheduling delay. Demonstrate a complete worst-case path bound rather than moving delay into an uncounted stage.
  • Consider architectural concurrency or a shorter alarm path only if causal dependencies, input validity, detection correctness and interface behavior remain satisfied. Replace the serial sum with a justified critical-path analysis if stages genuinely overlap.

Select an option after investigating the path and the 260/460 ms discrepancy. Do not change the pressure threshold, move the trigger downstream, terminate timing at command transmission, or weaken operating conditions to meet the criterion.

Proposed motion-inhibit transitions reconcile the recorded diagram with N-02 and unchanged REQ-8:

State and event Proposed next state and observable behavior
OPERATING; local stop asserted or required sensor data missing INHIBITED; motion inhibited and latch state recorded
INHIBITED; stop released, data restored, or network reconnected, without a new explicit local resume Remain INHIBITED; retain motion inhibit and the visible stop latch after reconnection
INHIBITED; resume requested while stop remains asserted or data remains invalid Remain INHIBITED; do not retain this request as permission for automatic later recovery
INHIBITED; new explicit local resume with stop released and required data valid Permit removal of this inhibit and transition to OPERATING, subject to existing independent interlocks; this does not itself command motion
Any state; stop assertion coincident with resume Stop takes precedence; remain or enter INHIBITED

The fresh-resume and precedence details are proposed design resolutions for review, not new approvals. Stop release and data restoration must never themselves authorize motion. Preserve the stop-latch indication through network recovery and shift change, consistent with the operator note. A generic fault indicator is not evidence that the stop latch remains visible.

These state labels concern motion permission. They must not redefine REQ-7's existing “during operation” condition or introduce a new exception to warning behavior. Resolve the exact operating-mode and interface observation definitions using the existing project contracts before implementation and verification.

VER-7: establish the actual implementation configuration, controlled threshold and validity contract, and operating modes before execution. Retain the trigger “after the valid pressure input first meets the high-pressure condition during operation” and end event “assert the local high-pressure warning.” Identify an observable input-contract boundary and the actual local annunciator assertion. Document stimulus accuracy, sensor/input observation, annunciator observation, timestamp alignment, instrument calibration, resolution and uncertainty. Before running, agree the conformance decision rule; a proposed conservative rule is that measured latency plus stated timing uncertainty must not exceed 200 ms. Values near the limit with unresolved uncertainty do not establish conformance.

VER-8: verify motion inhibition and stop-latch indication with observable motion or a justified motion-permission measurement, not the fault indicator alone. Prepare the following sequences and expected results:

  1. Assert local stop while operating. Observe motion inhibition and the stop-latch indication. Keep stop asserted and attempt resume; inhibition must remain.
  2. Release stop without resume. Inhibition must remain. A new explicit local resume with required conditions satisfied may remove this inhibit; it must not bypass independent interlocks or itself be treated as a motion command.
  3. Assert stop, lose communication/sensor data, release stop and restore data/network without resume. Verify retained inhibition and visible stop latch after restoration. Repeat with restoration before stop release.
  4. Lose required data without a local stop. Restore it without resume and verify no automatic authorization of motion, consistent with N-02 and the proposed state machine.
  5. Attempt resume before required data is valid or before stop is released; restore the conditions afterward without a new resume. Verify inhibition remains. Check simultaneous stop/resume with stop precedence.
  6. Change operator shifts during the outage. Confirm the incoming operator can see the retained stop latch after reconnect and that neither handover nor reconnection counts as local resume.

Record event ordering, the actual stop/data/resume inputs, motion or permission observations, display observations and the tested configuration. Verify warning behavior in every mode covered by the unchanged operating-condition contract as well; resolving motion recovery must not silently suppress REQ-7.

Source: evals/evidence/performance-20261113/none/HO-15/outputs/output.md

The supplied RFC 793 (1981), section 2.6 fact supports a transport claim: receiving TCP has taken responsibility for the data. It does not establish delivery to an end user. Logging a transport ACK as “operator saw and accepted shutdown” skips several distinct claims. An unattended dashboard during shift change makes that gap concrete. The packet supplies the historical source fact; no independent source retrieval or system test was performed here.

Claim Minimum evidence it would need
Transport receipt The transport acknowledgment, bound to the relevant communication. It supports only the supplied transport meaning.
Application receipt The receiving application validates and records the specific instruction, its identity and target. Transport receipt alone does not establish this.
Display The application records presenting the correct instruction and version to a particular session. Rendering does not prove anyone looked at it.
Human acknowledgment or acceptance A deliberate response from an identified person, bound to the instruction and version, distinguishing acceptance from rejection or deferral. This is an attributable attestation, not independent proof of comprehension.
Authority Confirmation that the issuer and responding actor have the required authority for that target and action, under the current duty assignment. Presence at the dashboard does not confer authority.
Performed action Feedback or observation establishing the required shutdown state of the intended equipment. An accepted instruction or issued command does not establish completion.

A minimal proposed contract would give each instruction a unique identifier, version, target, requested end state, issuer, designated responsible role, validity period and response deadline. Set those deadlines and the fallback policy from operational needs; none is supplied. Record application receipt, presentation, deliberate human response, authorization, action request and confirmed outcome as separate events with attributable actors and correlated times. A rejection or deferral remains explicit and leaves the work unresolved. Acceptance must not silently act as an execution command unless that behavior has been expressly designed and authorized.

Keep each pending instruction assigned to a responsible on-duty role. A shift handover must transfer the pending instruction and obtain explicit acceptance of responsibility by the incoming operator; a reconnect or a new session must not clear it or count as acceptance. If acknowledgment, ownership transfer or completion is missing by the agreed deadline, retain an unresolved state and escalate through an agreed staffed route. Do not mark success or invent an automatic shutdown policy. Enforce the applicable authorization and equipment interlocks when requesting action. Identify duplicates so retransmission cannot repeat an action, and reject expired or superseded instructions unless deliberately reissued with current authority.

A useful verification scenario starts with an instruction sent just before shift change. Arrange transport ACK and application receipt while the dashboard is unattended. Verify that the log records only the events actually observed, retains a pending human response, and triggers the agreed escalation when its deadline passes. Transfer duty and confirm the incoming authorized operator sees the pending instruction and must respond explicitly. Verify that an unauthorized response cannot authorize action. Following an authorized response and action request, withhold equipment-state confirmation: the system must remain “completion unconfirmed.” Then supply correlated confirmation of the required state and check that completion is recorded separately. Replay a duplicate and an expired instruction and verify no additional or stale action occurs. Capture event logs, identities, handover records and equipment observations against predefined expected states. This is a proposed scenario; it has not been executed.

To interpret the observation, obtain the prototype version and configuration, workload and request mix, concurrency timing, trial duration, network conditions, completion/error counts and logs. The next useful check is a controlled network-loss and restoration exercise using the identified configuration and a representative eight-request workload. First reproduce and document normal-network behavior. Then interrupt the relevant connection while requests are in flight, observe the behavior throughout the outage, restore connectivity and trace each request to its final outcome. Before execution, specify the loss duration and location, expected behavior for pending and new requests, permitted retries, and recovery criteria using project constraints. Check for lost, duplicate, stale or corrupted results and ambiguous completion, as applicable to the request semantics; record response outcomes, errors and time to recovery. Retain synchronized logs and the exact configuration so the result can support a bounded claim.

The experiment is proposed, not performed. Network-loss behavior remains unresolved until those conditions, expectations and observations are available. A successful run would support only its tested conditions; broader approval would require the project's remaining evidence and authorized decision.
