Fault Tree: HZ-001 — explicit dependency model

The same sensor under-reading event is reused in initiation and monitoring; multiplying it twice would understate the probability. A watchdog observes processor liveness, so BE6 is intentionally unused for running-but-wrong output. Clamp free-flow protection, actual flow dynamics, clinical risk, and physical independence require separate tests.

The machine-readable failure model is authoritative for this authored abstraction. Executed results and interpretation provide complete minimal cuts, scenario calculations, proof obligations and retained counterexamples. Event IDs from the earlier model retain their stated failure meaning; new shared-dependency events are explicit. Probabilities are synthetic per-demand inputs under the declared mutual-independence hypothesis after shared events are represented. No flight-hour rate, ASIL/SIL achievement, physical effectiveness or risk acceptance follows from these results.

Risk-Benefit Analysis

This draft identifies candidate benefits and the comparative evidence needed to evaluate them. No residual-risk or benefit conclusion is established. The executed models test selected control logic; they do not estimate clinical benefit or harm.

Intended medical benefits: - Accurate, controlled intravenous fluid and medication delivery replacing manual gravity infusion - DERS is intended to reduce out-of-range programming errors. The former 70-80% ECRI claim had no identifiable source and has been removed; effectiveness requires device-specific evidence. - Automated volume tracking and KVO transition reduce the risk of air embolism from empty containers - EHR integration reduces medication transcription errors - Alarm management provides early warning of occlusion, air, and other hazardous conditions

Residual risk summary:

HZ ID Residual Risk Level Benefit Justification
HZ-001 Unassessed (control proposal) Hypothesis: closed-loop control and rate limiting reduce over-infusion; compare measured delivery, failure coverage and use conditions against the selected alternative
HZ-002 Unassessed (control proposal) Hypothesis: DERS hard limits reject covered bolus-entry errors; test library validity, bypass paths and uncovered error types
HZ-003 Unassessed (control proposal) DERS with validated drug library provides protection not available with non-DERS pumps
HZ-004 Unassessed (control proposal) Air-in-line detection with automatic pause provides protection not available with gravity infusion
HZ-005 Unassessed (control proposal) Proposed spring-closed clamp aims to prevent free-flow; effectiveness and failure dependencies unverified
HZ-008 Unassessed (control proposal) Compare demonstrated EHR/alarm benefits with assessed cyber-induced harms; effectiveness and acceptability remain open

Assessment status: Individual residual risks remain unassessed; planned controls and suggested benefits do not establish their effectiveness or risk-benefit acceptability.

Overall Residual Risk Evaluation

Per ISO 14971 (exact locator to verify), this section evaluates the overall residual risk from all identified hazardous situations considered together.

Evaluation method: Review of the completeness of the hazard identification process, confirmation that all identified hazards have been addressed by risk controls, and assessment of whether the combination of individual residual risks creates a cumulative risk that is unacceptable.

Open assessment work:

  1. Check hazard-identification completeness against intended use, foreseeable misuse, implementation fault analysis, and actual adverse-event/predicate data. No MAUDE review artifact or completeness determination is supplied.
  2. The table proposes controls for the 12 listed hazardous situations. Coverage of that list does not establish completeness, effectiveness, or independence.
  3. Assess individual and combined residual risk with supported estimates, confirmed control effectiveness, benefit-risk evidence, and the adopted acceptability process.
  4. Define actual postmarket responsibilities, review cadence, and monitoring records. Proposed logging/network features do not establish an operating surveillance process.

Disposition: Overall residual-risk acceptability is unresolved. The proposed controls, individual estimates, combined risk, benefit-risk argument, usability, and postmarket arrangements require evidence and an authorized review. No acceptance is recorded by this teaching case.

Requirements

Proposed teaching baseline. Physical performance and risk acceptance remain open. Executed abstract-model evidence and its exact scope are in analysis/report.md. Source review identifies candidate citations and unresolved applicability; review status identifies the checked scope.

These proposed requirements retain their original IDs. Measurability, decomposition and source applicability are review obligations; versioning does not imply approval.

Requirement Record Schema

Field Description
ID Unique identifier (e.g., REQ-FUN-001)
Statement Atomic shall-statement
Rationale Why this requirement exists
Source Candidate basis requiring source review; hazard ID (HZ-), control ID (CTL-), regulatory clause, or stakeholder need
Parent Parent requirement ID (if derived)
Verification Method: test, analysis, inspection, demonstration
Allocation Target component ID(s) from architecture.md
Status Draft, baselined, verified, deferred

Functional Requirements

REQ-FUN-001

Field Value
Statement The pump shall deliver fluid at a programmable rate from 0.1 mL/hr to 999 mL/hr in increments of 0.1 mL/hr.
Rationale Clinical infusion protocols require a wide rate range with fine granularity for titrated medications.
Source Stakeholder need (clinician); IEC 60601-2-24 Clause 201.12.1
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01B, CMP-PMA-01A, CMP-PMA-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-002

Field Value
Statement The pump shall maintain flow rate accuracy within +/-5% of the programmed rate at rates >= 1 mL/hr and within +/-15% at rates < 1 mL/hr under standard test conditions per IEC 60601-2-24.
Rationale Flow accuracy requirements are mandated by the infusion pump particular standard.
Source IEC 60601-2-24 Clause 201.12.1.101; CTL-001
Parent REQ-FUN-001
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01B, CMP-PMA-01A, CMP-PMA-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-003

Field Value
Statement The pump shall use closed-loop flow control comparing commanded flow rate against measured flow rate from the flow sensor, with a control loop period of not more than 10 ms.
Rationale Closed-loop control compensates for tubing compliance, viscosity, and mechanical variation.
Source CTL-001; architecture decision AD-04
Parent REQ-FUN-002
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01B, CMP-PMA-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-004

Field Value
Statement The pump shall accumulate delivered volume with an accuracy of +/-5% of the actual volume delivered and shall compare accumulated volume against the programmed VTBI.
Rationale Volume tracking drives KVO transition and dose completion awareness.
Source Stakeholder need (clinician); IEC 60601-2-24
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-005

Field Value
Statement The pump shall transition to KVO mode (MODE-003) when the programmed VTBI has been delivered and shall annunciate the transition to the clinician via an audible and visual alarm.
Rationale Automated KVO transition maintains venous access while alerting the clinician that the primary infusion is complete.
Source Stakeholder need (clinician); CTL-008
Parent REQ-FUN-004
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01B, CMP-MCB-01D, CMP-UIM-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-006

Field Value
Statement The pump shall deliver clinician-initiated bolus volumes from 0.1 mL to 100 mL at rates from 1 mL/hr to 999 mL/hr with DERS hard limit checking applied before bolus delivery begins.
Rationale Bolus delivery must be bounded by drug library hard limits to prevent over-infusion.
Source Stakeholder need (clinician); CTL-003; HZ-002
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01B, CMP-MCB-01C, CMP-PMA-01A
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-007

Field Value
Statement The DERS shall check programmed drug, concentration, dose, and rate against the active drug library before infusion start and shall alert the clinician if any parameter exceeds a soft limit.
Rationale DERS is the primary defense against medication dosing errors.
Source CTL-003; HZ-003; FDA Infusion Pump Improvement Initiative
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01C
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-008

Field Value
Statement The DERS shall prevent infusion start if any programmed parameter exceeds a hard limit, and the hard limit shall not be overridable by the clinician.
Rationale Hard limits represent absolute safety boundaries that should never be exceeded.
Source CTL-003; HZ-003; FDA Infusion Pump Improvement Initiative
Parent REQ-FUN-007
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01C
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-009

Field Value
Statement The DERS shall log all soft limit alerts and clinician override decisions, including drug name, programmed parameters, limit values, and clinician response, to non-volatile memory.
Rationale Override logging supports pharmacovigilance and drug library tuning to reduce alert fatigue.
Source Stakeholder need (pharmacist); FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance (data integrity)
Parent REQ-FUN-007
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01C
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-010

Field Value
Statement The pump shall store a drug library containing a minimum of 2000 drug entries with per-drug soft and hard limits for concentration, dose, rate, and VTBI, organized by clinical care area.
Rationale Hospital drug libraries require large capacity with care-area-specific limit profiles.
Source Stakeholder need (pharmacist)
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01C
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-011

Field Value
Statement The pump shall validate the integrity of drug library files using CRC-32 and digital signature verification before activating a new drug library.
Rationale Corrupted or tampered drug libraries can defeat DERS protection.
Source CTL-009; HZ-009; FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance
Parent REQ-FUN-010
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01C, CMP-WCM-01C
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-012

Field Value
Statement The pump shall generate a high-priority alarm per IEC 60601-1-8 within 5 seconds of detecting an occlusion condition exceeding the configurable occlusion pressure threshold.
Rationale Prompt occlusion detection prevents under-infusion and upstream line rupture.
Source IEC 60601-2-24 Clause 201.12.4.101; CTL-005
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01D, CMP-PMA-01E, CMP-UIM-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-013

Field Value
Statement The pump shall generate a high-priority alarm per IEC 60601-1-8 within 2 seconds of detecting air-in-line volume exceeding 50 microliters and shall pause the infusion (MODE-004).
Rationale Air embolism prevention requires rapid detection and infusion stoppage.
Source IEC 60601-2-24 Clause 201.12.4.103; CTL-004; HZ-004
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01D, CMP-PMA-01D, CMP-UIM-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-014

Field Value
Statement The pump shall generate alarm signals conforming to IEC 60601-1-8 alarm priorities: high-priority (pulse pattern, >= 75 dBA), medium-priority (>= 65 dBA), and low-priority (>= 55 dBA), measured at 1 meter.
Rationale Standardized alarm characteristics ensure clinical audibility and recognition.
Source IEC 60601-1-8 Clause 6.3; IEC 60601-2-24
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01D, CMP-UIM-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-015

Field Value
Statement The pump shall continuously monitor the flow sensor output and shall generate a medium-priority alarm if the measured flow rate deviates from the commanded rate by more than 15% for more than 30 seconds.
Rationale Flow deviation detection catches partial occlusions and pump mechanism failures.
Source CTL-001; HZ-001
Parent REQ-FUN-003
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01D, CMP-PMA-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-016

Field Value
Statement The pump shall detect an upstream occlusion (container empty) when upstream pressure drops below the configurable threshold and shall generate a high-priority alarm within 5 seconds.
Rationale Upstream occlusion indicates fluid source exhaustion requiring clinician intervention.
Source IEC 60601-2-24 Clause 201.12.4.101; CTL-005
Parent REQ-FUN-012
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01D, CMP-PMA-01E
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-017

Field Value
Statement The pump shall detect the door-open condition via the door latch sensor and shall transition to MODE-004 (Alarm/Pause) within 500 ms of detection.
Rationale Door open during infusion requires immediate stoppage; anti-free-flow clamp engages mechanically.
Source CTL-006; HZ-005
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01D, CMP-PMA-01F
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-018

Field Value
Statement The pump shall detect loss of flow sensor input and shall transition to open-loop delivery with a medium-priority alarm within 5 seconds, using motor step counting as the backup flow estimation method.
Rationale Flow sensor failure should not halt infusion but requires clinician awareness of reduced accuracy.
Source CTL-010; IEC 60601-2-24
Parent REQ-FUN-003
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01B, CMP-MCB-01D
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-019

Field Value
Statement The pump shall monitor battery state of charge and shall generate a low-priority alarm when remaining battery runtime falls below 30 minutes and a high-priority alarm when runtime falls below 10 minutes.
Rationale Battery depletion warning gives clinician time to connect AC power before infusion is interrupted.
Source IEC 60601-1 Clause 11.8; stakeholder need (clinician)
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01K
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-020

Field Value
Statement The pump shall display the current infusion parameters (drug name, rate, VTBI, volume infused, time remaining) on the main screen with a refresh rate of not less than 2 Hz.
Rationale Clinician situational awareness requires continuously visible infusion status.
Source Stakeholder need (clinician); IEC 62366-1 (usability)
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-UIM-01A, CMP-UIM-01C
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-021

Field Value
Statement The pump shall respond to clinician touch inputs within 200 ms of contact and shall provide visual feedback on the display within 500 ms.
Rationale Responsive interface prevents data entry errors and clinician frustration.
Source IEC 62366-1 (usability); stakeholder need (clinician)
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-UIM-01A, CMP-UIM-01C
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-022

Field Value
Statement The pump infusion programming workflow shall require DERS limit checking to complete before the pump permits infusion start, and shall not provide a user interface path that bypasses DERS checking.
Rationale DERS bypass would defeat the dose error reduction safety function.
Source CTL-003; HZ-003; FDA Infusion Pump Improvement Initiative
Parent REQ-FUN-007
Verification Test, Inspection
Allocation CMP-UIM-01C, CMP-MCB-01C
Status Proposed

REQ-FUN-023

Field Value
Statement The pump shall execute a power-up self-test verifying processor, memory, flow sensor, pressure sensor, air detector, door sensor, display, alarm annunciator, and watchdog within 30 seconds of power application and shall not permit infusion start until self-test passes.
Rationale Pre-use self-test detects latent faults before they combine with active faults during infusion.
Source CTL-011; IEC 60601-1 Clause 15.4.4
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01, CMP-MCB-01J
Status Proposed

Safety Requirements

REQ-SAF-001

Field Value
Statement The proposed spring-closed anti-free-flow clamp shall occlude the IV tubing within 500 ms of door opening or loss of hold-open power, without requiring a processor/software command. Mechanical actuator/interlock fault coverage remains to be specified.
Rationale Free-flow is the highest-severity hazard; the closing mechanism is intended to avoid a processor-command dependency; independence needs evidence.
Source HZ-005; CTL-006; IEC 60601-2-24 Clause 201.12.4.104
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-PMA-01C
Status Proposed

REQ-SAF-002

Field Value
Statement The hardware watchdog timer shall reset the main processor within 200 ms if the processor fails to service the watchdog, and the reset shall place the pump in a safe state (infusion stopped, anti-free-flow engaged, alarm activated).
Rationale Processor lockup or software hang must result in a safe state, not continued uncontrolled delivery.
Source HZ-006; CTL-007
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01J, CMP-MCB-01A
Status Proposed

REQ-SAF-003

Field Value
Statement The pump shall limit the maximum deliverable flow rate to 999 mL/hr for software-commanded excessive motor speed within the specified drive envelope, enforced by a candidate hardware current limiter on the pump motor driver that prevents motor speed from exceeding the rate corresponding to 999 mL/hr.
Rationale Hardware rate limiting provides defense in depth against software faults that could command excessive pump speed.
Source HZ-001; CTL-002; IEC 60601-2-24
Parent —
Verification Test, Analysis
Allocation CMP-MCB-01H
Status Proposed

REQ-SAF-004

Field Value
Statement The pump shall detect a discrepancy between the commanded flow rate and the measured flow rate exceeding 25% of the commanded rate for more than 10 seconds and shall transition to MODE-004 (Alarm/Pause) with a high-priority alarm.
Rationale Gross flow discrepancy indicates pump mechanism failure, tubing displacement, or free-flow condition.
Source HZ-001; HZ-005; CTL-001
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01B, CMP-MCB-01D
Status Proposed

REQ-SAF-005

Field Value
Statement The RTOS memory protection unit shall enforce spatial isolation between the infusion control partition (P1) and the communication partition (P4) such that a fault in the communication task cannot modify infusion control memory.
Rationale Communication failures and network attacks must not propagate to safety-critical infusion control.
Source HZ-008; CTL-012; FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance
Parent —
Verification Test, Analysis
Allocation CMP-MCB-01E
Status Proposed

REQ-SAF-006

Field Value
Statement Upon detection of a non-recoverable software fault, the pump shall transition to a safe state within 1 second. The safe state shall consist of: infusion stopped, anti-free-flow clamp engaged, high-priority alarm activated, and fault code displayed.
Rationale Non-recoverable faults must result in a defined safe state that prevents patient harm and alerts the clinician.
Source HZ-006; CTL-007; IEC 60601-1 Clause 13.1
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01B, CMP-MCB-01D, CMP-PMA-01C, CMP-UIM-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-SAF-007

Field Value
Statement The pump shall maintain alarm annunciation capability (audible and visual) independent of the touchscreen display, such that alarm signals are generated even if the display application crashes or the touchscreen fails.
Rationale Alarm annunciation is the last line of defense; it must function when the display has failed.
Source HZ-007; CTL-008; IEC 60601-1-8
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01D, CMP-UIM-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-SAF-008

Field Value
Statement The pump shall provide battery backup sufficient to maintain infusion delivery and alarm capability for a minimum of 2 hours at a rate of 125 mL/hr.
Rationale AC power interruptions in hospital settings must not immediately halt treatment.
Source IEC 60601-1 Clause 11.8; stakeholder need (clinician)
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01K
Status Proposed

REQ-SAF-009

Field Value
Statement The DERS engine shall operate independently from the network communication functions such that a loss of Wi-Fi connectivity does not degrade DERS checking capability for infusions programmed using the locally stored drug library.
Rationale DERS protection must not depend on network availability.
Source HZ-008; CTL-012; FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance
Parent REQ-FUN-007
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01C
Status Proposed

REQ-SAF-010

Field Value
Statement The pump shall not accept drug library updates during an active infusion. Drug library activation shall require the pump to be in MODE-005 (Standby/Setup) with no active infusion.
Rationale Mid-infusion library changes could alter DERS limits for the active drug, creating an inconsistent safety state.
Source HZ-009; CTL-009
Parent REQ-FUN-011
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01C, CMP-WCM-01C
Status Proposed

Interface Requirements

REQ-IFC-001

Field Value
Statement The pump shall transmit infusion status data (drug, rate, volume infused, alarm state) to the EHR via IFC-EXT-001 using HL7 v2 or FHIR messaging within 30 seconds of a status change event.
Rationale Timely auto-documentation reduces manual charting burden and supports clinical decision-making.
Source Stakeholder need (clinician, hospital IT); IEC 80001-1
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-WCM-01B
Status Proposed

REQ-IFC-002

Field Value
Statement The pump shall receive drug orders from the EHR via IFC-EXT-002 and shall pre-populate infusion programming fields, requiring clinician confirmation before infusion start.
Rationale EHR-to-pump order transfer reduces transcription errors; clinician confirmation prevents automation complacency.
Source Stakeholder need (clinician); CTL-003
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-WCM-01B, CMP-MCB-01C
Status Proposed

REQ-IFC-003

Field Value
Statement The pump shall encrypt all network communications using TLS 1.2 or higher with certificate-based mutual authentication per the hospital PKI infrastructure.
Rationale Network encryption prevents eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks on infusion data and drug library transfers.
Source CTL-012; FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance; IEC 62443-4-1
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01G, CMP-WCM-01A
Status Proposed

REQ-IFC-004

Field Value
Statement The pump shall authenticate to the hospital Wi-Fi network using WPA2-Enterprise or WPA3 with 802.1X and shall not support open or WEP-encrypted networks.
Rationale Weak or absent Wi-Fi authentication exposes the pump to network-based attacks.
Source CTL-012; FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance
Parent REQ-IFC-003
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-WCM-01A
Status Proposed

REQ-IFC-005

Field Value
Statement The pump shall forward active alarm notifications to the central monitoring station via IFC-EXT-004 within 10 seconds of alarm activation, including alarm priority, alarm condition, and pump identifier.
Rationale Remote alarm notification enables centralized monitoring of pump fleets in large clinical areas.
Source Stakeholder need (clinician, hospital administration); IEC 60601-1-8
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-WCM-01B, CMP-MCB-01D
Status Proposed

REQ-IFC-006

Field Value
Statement The MCB shall validate all data received from the WCM via IFC-INT-009 against expected message format and value ranges before acting on the data, and shall reject malformed messages with an error log entry.
Rationale Input validation at the MCB-WCM boundary prevents network-originated data from corrupting safety-critical functions.
Source CTL-012; HZ-008; FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01B
Status Proposed

Performance Requirements

REQ-PRF-001

Field Value
Statement The pump shall achieve trumpet curve compliance per IEC 60601-2-24 Clause 201.12.1.103 for observation windows of 2, 5, 11, 19, and 31 minutes at the reference rate of 25 mL/hr.
Rationale Trumpet curve compliance demonstrates short-term and long-term flow uniformity.
Source IEC 60601-2-24 Clause 201.12.1.103
Parent REQ-FUN-002
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01B, CMP-PMA-01A
Status Proposed

REQ-PRF-002

Field Value
Statement The pump shall complete power-up self-test and be ready for infusion programming within 30 seconds of power application at ambient temperatures between 10C and 40C.
Rationale Rapid startup supports clinical workflow in emergency and routine settings.
Source Stakeholder need (clinician); IEC 60601-1
Parent REQ-FUN-023
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01, CMP-UIM-01, CMP-WCM-01
Status Proposed

REQ-PRF-003

Field Value
Statement The pump shall operate within a total power consumption of 25 watts on AC mains and shall consume not more than 15 watts from battery during infusion at 125 mL/hr.
Rationale Power budget constrains thermal design and battery runtime requirements.
Source IEC 60601-1 Clause 11; architecture constraint
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01K
Status Proposed

REQ-PRF-004

Field Value
Statement The pump shall resume infusion delivery within 5 seconds of AC power restoration following a power interruption of less than 5 seconds, without clinician intervention, and shall alarm if the interruption exceeds 5 seconds.
Rationale Brief power interruptions from outlet disconnects during patient transport should not halt treatment.
Source IEC 60601-1 Clause 11.8; stakeholder need (clinician)
Parent REQ-SAF-008
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-MCB-01K, CMP-MCB-01B
Status Proposed

Traceability

Proposed teaching baseline. Physical performance and risk acceptance remain open. Executed abstract-model evidence and its exact scope are in analysis/report.md. Source review identifies candidate citations and unresolved applicability; review status identifies the checked scope.

Trace Strategy

This traceability matrix establishes bidirectional linkage across all Smart Infusion Pump system engineering artifacts. Forward traces propose source, allocation, and verification relationships; they do not demonstrate that any test was executed or requirement verified. Reverse traces confirm that every component, hazard, and verification activity connects back to a requirement. Gaps are first-class entries with disposition, not omissions.

Traced entities: - Requirements (REQ-) to architecture components (CMP-) - Requirements (REQ-) to hazard/control sources (HZ-, CTL-) - Requirements (REQ-) to verification activities (VER-) - Verification activities (VER-) to evidence artifacts (EVD-) - Components (CMP-) back to requirements - Hazards (HZ-) through controls (CTL-) to requirements

Surgical Robot Platform

Proposed teaching baseline. Physical performance and risk acceptance remain open. Source review identifies candidate citations and unresolved applicability; review status identifies the checked scope.

Overview

The Surgical Robot Platform is a multi-arm teleoperated surgical system for minimally invasive procedures including general surgery, gynecology, and urology. The system uses a master-slave architecture in which a surgeon seated at an ergonomic console manipulates hand controllers and foot pedals that map to articulated instrument arms and an endoscopic camera at the patient-side cart. Haptic feedback provides force sensing from tissue interaction back to the surgeon's hands. A stereoscopic vision system delivers 3D high-definition imagery with instrument overlay and anatomical annotation. The system is classified FDA Class II via the De Novo pathway (no substantially equivalent predicate device) and EU MDR Class IIb. Embedded software is IEC 62304 Class C.

System Boundary

Inside the system boundary: - Surgeon console: master hand controllers, foot pedal array, stereoscopic display, haptic feedback actuators, console processor - Patient-side cart: four articulated instrument arms (three instrument + one camera), instrument drive mechanisms, joint encoders, force/torque sensors, cart processor - Vision tower: stereoscopic endoscope, image processor, video distribution, light source interface - System controller: motion scaling, tremor filtering, workspace mapping, safety supervisory software - Instrument interface: instrument recognition, usage tracking, sterile adapter engagement detection

Outside the system boundary: - Surgical instruments (disposable/reusable endeffectors, supplied separately) - Electrosurgical generator (external energy source connected via IFC-EXT-004) - Operating room table and positioning system - Anesthesia equipment and patient monitoring - Hospital network infrastructure - Sterile draping and accessories

Operational Environment

The system operates in hospital operating rooms under controlled environmental conditions: 18C to 26C ambient temperature, 30% to 60% relative humidity, and standard atmospheric pressure. The surgeon console may be located in the same OR or in an adjacent control room connected via a dedicated fiber-optic link. The system requires dedicated 30A electrical circuits for the patient-side cart and vision tower.

Operating Modes

Mode ID Name Description Active Functions Constraints
MODE-001 Teleoperation Full master-slave control with haptic feedback and vision active All FUN- functions active Surgeon authenticated; instruments engaged
MODE-002 Setup/Docking Patient-side cart positioning and instrument port alignment FUN-MOT-01 (limited), FUN-VIS-01, FUN-SAF-01 Reduced speed limits; no instrument actuation
MODE-003 Fault Hold All motion halted; instruments locked in place after detected fault FUN-SAF-01, FUN-SAF-02, FUN-VIS-01 No motion; surgeon must acknowledge before resume
MODE-004 Manual Override Surgeon or assistant manually repositions arms at the patient side FUN-SAF-01 (monitoring only), FUN-SAF-02 Motor drives disengaged; clutch brakes released

Key Technical Challenges

  1. Haptic feedback latency. The round-trip delay from force sensing at the instrument tip through the communication link to the haptic actuators at the surgeon console must remain below 10 ms to maintain transparent teleoperation. Exceeding this threshold degrades the surgeon's force perception and increases the risk of tissue damage from excessive applied force.

  2. Motion scaling fidelity and tremor filtering. The system scales surgeon hand movements (typically 3:1 to 5:1 reduction) while filtering physiological tremor (8-12 Hz). The scaling and filtering algorithms must preserve intentional fine movements (suturing, dissection) without introducing phase lag or spatial distortion that could cause instrument drift.

  3. Instrument arm collision avoidance. Four articulated arms operating in a shared surgical workspace must avoid collisions with each other, the patient, and the OR staff. The collision avoidance algorithm must operate in real time without impeding the surgeon's intended motion trajectory.

  4. De Novo regulatory pathway. No substantially equivalent predicate device exists for this configuration, requiring the De Novo classification process with a comprehensive risk-benefit analysis and special controls recommendation.

Stakeholders

Stakeholder Role
Surgeon Primary operator; controls instruments via console during procedures
OR nursing staff Assists with setup, docking, instrument exchange, and draping
Patient Subject of surgical procedure; subject to harm from device malfunction
Biomedical engineering Installs, maintains, and calibrates the robotic system
FDA (CDRH) Reviews De Novo classification request; defines special controls
EU Notified Body Assesses EU MDR conformity for Class IIb active therapeutic device

Standards Applicability

Standard Applicability
IEC 62304 Software lifecycle for Class C safety-classified embedded software (console, cart, vision)
ISO 14971 Risk management across full product lifecycle; surgical-specific hazard categories
IEC 60601-1 General safety and essential performance; Type B applied part (instrument contact)
IEC 80601-2-77 Particular requirements for robotically assisted surgical equipment
IEC 62443 Cybersecurity for networked surgical systems; defense-in-depth for console-cart link

Failure Containment / Partitioning

The system uses physical separation and independent processors to contain faults within subsystem boundaries.

Console-Cart isolation: The surgeon console and patient-side cart are physically separate units connected by a dedicated fiber-optic link. A communication fault triggers MODE-003 (Fault Hold) with instruments locked in place. The console cannot directly drive patient-side motors; all commands pass through the system controller safety supervision layer.

Safety supervision independence: The safety supervisory software (CMP-CTR-01B) runs as an independent task with higher priority than the motion control task on the system controller. It independently monitors joint envelopes and communication integrity. The emergency stop circuit (CMP-PCA-01F) is entirely hardwired, bypassing all software.

Vision isolation: Vision processing failure does not affect motion control or safety supervision. Loss of video triggers a surgeon notification but does not halt instrument arms, as the surgeon can request pause via the clutch pedal.

Architecture Decisions

AD-01: Dedicated Fiber-Optic Link over Hospital Network

Decision: Use a dedicated point-to-point fiber-optic link between the surgeon console and the system controller rather than routing over the hospital Ethernet network.

Rationale: The teleoperation control loop requires deterministic sub-2 ms round-trip latency and near-zero packet loss. Hospital networks cannot guarantee this quality of service. A dedicated link reduces exposure to shared routing; endpoints, maintenance interfaces, message authenticity, availability and recovery still require threat analysis and testing.

Trade-off: The surgeon console cannot be located in a geographically distant site. Accepted because the clinical use case is same-building teleoperation, not remote surgery.

AD-02: EtherCAT for Patient-Side Servo Communication

Decision: Use EtherCAT as the real-time fieldbus between the system controller and the patient-side cart joint servos.

Rationale: EtherCAT provides deterministic sub-microsecond jitter communication to multiple servo drives on a single network, supporting the 1 kHz servo loop rate required for stable joint control. The protocol's distributed clock synchronization ensures all joints receive commands within the same control cycle.

Trade-off: EtherCAT requires specialized interface hardware on each joint servo drive. Accepted because the servo loop timing requirements cannot be met with standard Ethernet protocols.

AD-03: Hardware Current Limiting Independent of Software

Decision: Implement per-joint hardware current limiters on each motor driver (CMP-PCA-01E) that are not configurable or overridable by software.

Rationale: The maximum force limit (25 N per arm) must hold even under complete software failure. A hardware current limiter provides a force ceiling that is physically enforced regardless of commanded torque values, providing defense in depth against motion control software faults.

Trade-off: A fixed force limit constrains manipulation. The retained 25 N value is an unvalidated design hypothesis; appropriateness depends on instrument, tissue, contact geometry, direction, duration and intended procedure. Establish task-specific limits with representative physical and clinical evidence before accepting the setting.

Functional Requirements

REQ-FUN-001

Field Value
Statement The system shall map surgeon hand controller movements to instrument tip movements with a configurable motion scaling ratio from 1:1 to 5:1, selectable by the surgeon during MODE-001.
Rationale Motion scaling enables fine manipulation beyond unaided human dexterity for microsurgical tasks.
Source Stakeholder need (surgeon); IEC 80601-2-77 Clause 201.12
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-CON-01B, CMP-CTR-01A
Status Draft

REQ-FUN-002

Field Value
Statement The system shall filter physiological hand tremor in the frequency range of 8 Hz to 12 Hz from the surgeon's hand controller input while preserving intentional movements below 4 Hz with less than 5% amplitude attenuation.
Rationale Tremor filtering improves instrument tip stability without degrading intentional surgical gestures.
Source Stakeholder need (surgeon); IEC 80601-2-77
Parent REQ-FUN-001
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-CTR-01A
Status Draft

REQ-FUN-003

Field Value
Statement The system shall provide haptic force feedback from the instrument tip to the surgeon's hand controllers with a round-trip latency of not more than 10 ms measured from force/torque sensor sampling to haptic actuator output.
Rationale Transparent haptic feedback below 10 ms preserves the surgeon's force perception and prevents tissue damage from excessive force.
Source IEC 80601-2-77; stakeholder need (surgeon)
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-PCA-01C, CMP-CON-01C, CMP-CTR-01A
Status Draft

REQ-FUN-004

Field Value
Statement The system shall render stereoscopic 3D video from the endoscopic camera to the surgeon console display at a minimum of 60 frames per second with a glass-to-glass latency of not more than 100 ms.
Rationale Low-latency high-frame-rate stereo video is essential for depth perception and hand-eye coordination during teleoperation.
Source Stakeholder need (surgeon); IEC 80601-2-77
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-VIS-01A, CMP-VIS-01B, CMP-CON-01D
Status Draft

REQ-FUN-005

Field Value
Statement The system shall detect the identity and usage count of each attached surgical instrument via the instrument recognition interface and shall prevent use of instruments that have exceeded their maximum usage cycle count.
Rationale Instrument tracking prevents use of worn instruments that may fail during a procedure.
Source Stakeholder need (biomedical engineering); IEC 80601-2-77
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-PCA-01D, CMP-CTR-01A

Safety Requirements

REQ-SAF-001

Field Value
Statement The system shall halt all instrument arm motion within 50 ms of detecting a joint position, velocity, or torque value outside the predefined safe operating envelope and shall transition to MODE-003 (Fault Hold).
Rationale Runaway arm motion is a critical hazard; immediate halt prevents patient injury.
Source IEC 80601-2-77 Clause 201.12.4; ISO 14971
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-CTR-01A, CMP-CTR-01B, CMP-PCA-01B
Status Draft

REQ-SAF-002

Field Value
Statement The system shall implement collision avoidance that prevents instrument arm-to-arm contact and arm-to-patient contact by enforcing minimum separation distances and reducing arm velocity as separation decreases, without requiring surgeon intervention.
Rationale Multi-arm collision is a foreseeable hazard unique to multi-arm robotic surgical systems.
Source IEC 80601-2-77; ISO 14971
Parent —
Verification Test, Analysis
Allocation CMP-CTR-01A, CMP-PCA-01B
Status Draft

REQ-SAF-003

Field Value
Statement Upon loss of the communication link between the surgeon console and the patient-side cart exceeding 100 ms, the system shall transition to MODE-003 (Fault Hold), halt all instrument motion, and annunciate an audible and visual alarm at both the console and the patient-side cart.
Rationale Uncontrolled instrument motion during communication loss can cause patient injury.
Source IEC 80601-2-77 Clause 201.12.4; ISO 14971
Parent —
Verification Test
Allocation CMP-CTR-01A, CMP-CON-01A, CMP-PCA-01A
Status Draft

REQ-SAF-004

Field Value
Statement The system shall limit the maximum force exertable by any instrument arm to 25 N, enforced by an independent hardware current limiter on each motor driver that is not software-overridable.
Rationale Hardware force limiting provides defense in depth against software faults that could command excessive arm force.
Source IEC 80601-2-77; ISO 14971
Parent —
Verification Test, Analysis
Allocation CMP-PCA-01E
Status Draft

REQ-SAF-005

Field Value
Statement The system shall provide a physical emergency stop button accessible from both the surgeon console and the patient-side cart that immediately removes power from all motor drives and engages joint brakes within 100 ms of activation.
Rationale Emergency stop is required as a last-resort safety measure independent of software control.
Source IEC 60601-1 Clause 9.2; IEC 80601-2-77
Parent —
Verification Test

A changed requirement, failed evidence, and a verified model repair

This executed walkthrough shortens REQ-02's invalid-reading qualification interval from 1 s to 500 ms, while preserving its identifier and the unchanged requirements. The deliberate teaching change is recorded as CR-01. Its value is an instructional choice; no real stakeholder approval is implied.

Configuration Requirement interval Implementation interval Actual execution
Prior snapshot 1000 ms 1000 ms Eight procedures pass; first sensor fault at 1000 ms.
Failed snapshot 500 ms 1000 ms VER-03, VER-06, VER-07 and VER-08 fail. The shortened deadline is missed.
Repaired model 500 ms 500 ms Eight procedures pass; first sensor fault at 500 ms.
Prior record reused against current baseline 500 ms Prior record Configuration/selection mismatch rejects the record; zero requirements receive passing evidence credit.

The failed execution is retained with its source configuration, observations, run ID and timestamps. It is valid evidence of a failed design. The repaired run supports the revised sampled behavior, with all original requirement, function, component, actor, interface and procedure IDs preserved. CR-01 is a new source; the original NEED-02 brief remains available rather than being rewritten.

python3 -B examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm-revision/compare_revisions.py --check
python3 -B scripts/check_trace.py examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm-revision/failed/baseline.json
python3 -B scripts/check_trace.py examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm-revision/baseline.json

The workflow receipt records actual reproduction of every stage and the attempt to reuse stale evidence. The failed snapshot's run_checks.py --check deliberately exits 1 after reproducing four failures; the comparison command expects exactly those failures. It does not mask an unrelated execution error as the expected failure.

The repaired model's finite-state exploration checks all reachable states under low/high/invalid readings and both acknowledgement values, comparing each output and event against the independent sample-counter oracle. The abstraction and its assumptions are defined in verification. These executions establish model behavior, evidence rejection and ID preservation. Sensor hardware, clock jitter, annunciation, persistence and operator effectiveness remain outside the executed scope.

To record another model execution, run run_checks.py in the relevant snapshot; its previous selection is archived before replacement. compare_revisions.py --record likewise archives the previous workflow receipt before selecting a new one. --record --output <new-path> creates an additional receipt and refuses to overwrite an existing file.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm-revision/architecture.md

Architecture and allocation

The logical design separates sensing, evaluation, local annunciation, and events. reference_model.py emulates evaluation/event behavior and returns output flags; it does not implement the sensor or sound/light actuator.

flowchart LR
  S[COMP-01 Sensor adapter] -->|IFC-01 time and temperature| E[COMP-02 Evaluator]
  U[ACTOR-01 Technician] -->|IFC-02 acknowledgement| E
  E -->|IFC-03 high OR fault| A[COMP-03 Annunciator]
  E -->|IFC-04 transition record| L[COMP-04 Event recorder]
Function Requirements Allocation Responsibility
FUN-01 Qualify temperature interval REQ-01 COMP-02 Reset pending timer on invalid/low input; latch after interval
FUN-02 Diagnose input availability REQ-02 COMP-01, COMP-02 Invalid input detection and valid recovery
FUN-03 Retain/acknowledge warning REQ-03 COMP-02, COMP-03 Preserve high latch and expose state
FUN-04 Record state changes REQ-04 COMP-02, COMP-04 Once per changed state pair

IFC-01: (time_ms, temperature_c) on contiguous 100 ms ticks. None, NaN, infinity, booleans, and nonnumeric values are invalid temperatures. The model rejects gaps, duplicate/out-of-order ticks, noninteger times, and nonboolean acknowledgement. IFC-02: ACTOR-01 technician acknowledgement at current tick. IFC-03: separate high/fault and their OR as local alarm. IFC-04: ordered time_ms, high, sensor_fault records in volatile memory.

AD-01: high latches, fault automatically clears on valid recovery to distinguish an excursion requiring acknowledgement from a current diagnostic condition. AD-02: discrete ticks make teaching checks reproducible; continuous timing and missing-tick handling remain open. AD-03: transitions are logged once; persistence is open.

HAZ-01: unnoticed excursion, CTL-01: warning plus operator action. HAZ-02: misleading healthy indication during sensor failure, CTL-02: invalid-input detection. Tests check modeled controls; noisy-lab effectiveness and reagent protection are unvalidated. Shared power is a common dependency, not redundancy.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm-revision/brief.md

Stakeholder brief

This fictional project monitors a laboratory cabinet holding temperature-sensitive research reagents. It is not claimed to be a medical device or validated storage system.

Source Need / teaching-project decision
NEED-01 Local warning after temperature has remained at or above 8 deg C for 2 s. This project threshold is not a sourced clinical/reagent limit.
NEED-02 Distinguishable sensor-unavailable indication after 1 s of invalid readings.
NEED-03 High warning remains visible until temperature is below 8 deg C and a technician acknowledges.
NEED-04 Timestamped alarm changes for investigation.

SCN-01: monitor storage, detect a sustained excursion, latch warning, observe recovery, acknowledge, retain event record. SCN-02: invalid/missing readings produce sensor fault; valid reading clears that fault; an existing high warning still needs valid recovery and acknowledgement.

Boundary: sensing interface, alarm logic, local annunciation, event record. Refrigeration control, networks, reagent disposition, and lab quality decisions are outside this demonstration.

Assumptions: samples every 100 ms; monotonic timestamps; power available; a valid reading represents cabinet temperature. Physical accuracy, sound/light perception, power loss, calibration, retention across reset, and staffing/response time require subsequent design and stakeholder validation.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm-revision/change-request.md

Teaching change request

This is a deliberate instructional baseline change, not a real stakeholder approval or a claim that 500 ms is a clinically appropriate limit.

Source Changed need Supersedes Reason
CR-01 Assert the sensor-unavailable indication within 100 ms after readings have remained invalid for 500 ms; clear on the next valid sample. NEED-02 1 s qualification interval Exercise a shorter detection interval and its evidence impact.

Keep REQ-02, FUN-02, COMP-01/COMP-02, IFC-01, and procedure IDs stable. The original brief remains preserved. REQ-01, REQ-03, and REQ-04 are unchanged. The 100 ms sampling interface remains unchanged, so 500 ms spans five elapsed ticks from the first invalid sample. No physical sensing or operator result is established by this choice.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm-revision/failed/requirements.md

Proposed requirement baseline

Values come from the brief, not regulation. Requirements apply to sampled reference behavior. Timer intervals begin at the first applicable sample, not a physical threshold crossing between samples.

ID Requirement Source Acceptance
REQ-01 The evaluator shall latch high within 100 ms after valid samples have been at or above 8 deg C continuously for 2 s, and not before that interval. NEED-01 First high 2000-2100 ms from first qualifying sample; below-threshold/invalid sample resets pending interval.
REQ-02 The evaluator shall assert sensor fault within 100 ms after readings have been invalid continuously for 500 ms; the next valid sample shall clear sensor fault. CR-01 First fault 500-600 ms; clearance on next valid sample. Nonfinite/nonnumeric readings are invalid.
REQ-03 The evaluator shall retain latched high until acknowledgement while the current sample is valid and below 8 deg C. NEED-03 Early acknowledgement, recovery alone, and sensor recovery cannot silently clear high.
REQ-04 The event recorder shall record each change of high/fault state once, with sample time and resulting states. NEED-04 Exact ordered transition records; no event for unchanged state.

Derived interface IFC-01 uses contiguous 100 ms ticks, supporting the model timing claims. Jitter, transport/actuator latency, and persistence need further requirements. No requirement is marked stakeholder approved.

CR-01 in the change request supersedes the NEED-02 timing choice in the preserved brief. Requirement IDs and unaffected requirements stay stable.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm-revision/failed/verification.md

Verification procedures

Run python3 examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm-revision/run_checks.py from repository root. The runner uses explicit inputs, saves observations, and hashes implementation, baseline, procedure, and design sources. No model API or physical equipment is used.

ID Requirement Procedure Acceptance
VER-01 REQ-01 Feed 8 deg C from t=0 through 2100 ms. No early high; first at 2000 ms.
VER-02 REQ-01 High, one 7.9 deg C sample at 1900 ms, then high through 3800 ms. Pending interval restarts; no high yet.
VER-03 REQ-02 Missing readings t=0 through 600 ms. First fault 500 ms.
VER-04 REQ-03 Latch high, acknowledge at 9 deg C, recover without acknowledgement, acknowledge at 7 deg C. Only final action clears high.
VER-05 REQ-04 Inspect VER-04 records, including unchanged ticks. Exactly assertion at 2000 and clearance at 2300, correct states.
VER-06 REQ-02, REQ-04 NaN through 500 ms, then valid 7 deg C. Fault and recovery with exactly their two records.
VER-07 REQ-01–REQ-04 Traverse every reachable finite abstract state against an independent sample-counter oracle, using low/high/invalid temperature and both acknowledgement inputs. No output or event mismatch in any reachable transition.
VER-08 REQ-02 Exercise eight invalid-temperature classes, eight invalid next timestamps, and nonboolean acknowledgement. Invalid readings produce fault at the specified interval; invalid call contracts are rejected without changing state.

VER-07 quotients absolute time by translation and saturates elapsed timers once their decision threshold is reached. The implementation uses only those timer threshold comparisons for control decisions. The oracle counts samples instead of reading the implementation's timestamps. Every transition checks flags, local-alarm output, and exact event production. This establishes equivalence for that finite sampled abstraction and its six input combinations per state; it does not establish real clock, scheduler, sensor, actuator, or persistence behavior.

Architecture and allocation

The logical design separates sensing, evaluation, local annunciation, and events. reference_model.py emulates evaluation/event behavior and returns output flags; it does not implement the sensor or sound/light actuator.

flowchart LR
  S[COMP-01 Sensor adapter] -->|IFC-01 time and temperature| E[COMP-02 Evaluator]
  U[ACTOR-01 Technician] -->|IFC-02 acknowledgement| E
  E -->|IFC-03 high OR fault| A[COMP-03 Annunciator]
  E -->|IFC-04 transition record| L[COMP-04 Event recorder]
Function Requirements Allocation Responsibility
FUN-01 Qualify temperature interval REQ-01 COMP-02 Reset pending timer on invalid/low input; latch after interval
FUN-02 Diagnose input availability REQ-02 COMP-01, COMP-02 Invalid input detection and valid recovery
FUN-03 Retain/acknowledge warning REQ-03 COMP-02, COMP-03 Preserve high latch and expose state
FUN-04 Record state changes REQ-04 COMP-02, COMP-04 Once per changed state pair

IFC-01: (time_ms, temperature_c) on contiguous 100 ms ticks. None, NaN, infinity, booleans, and nonnumeric values are invalid temperatures. The model rejects gaps, duplicate/out-of-order ticks, noninteger times, and nonboolean acknowledgement. IFC-02: ACTOR-01 technician acknowledgement at current tick. IFC-03: separate high/fault and their OR as local alarm. IFC-04: ordered time_ms, high, sensor_fault records in volatile memory.

AD-01: high latches, fault automatically clears on valid recovery to distinguish an excursion requiring acknowledgement from a current diagnostic condition. AD-02: discrete ticks make teaching checks reproducible; continuous timing and missing-tick handling remain open. AD-03: transitions are logged once; persistence is open.

HAZ-01: unnoticed excursion, CTL-01: warning plus operator action. HAZ-02: misleading healthy indication during sensor failure, CTL-02: invalid-input detection. Tests check modeled controls; noisy-lab effectiveness and reagent protection are unvalidated. Shared power is a common dependency, not redundancy.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm-revision/reference_model.py

reference_model.py

"""Illustrative sampled alarm model; not deployed firmware or physical validation."""
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
import math
import sys

_LOADED_MODULE_CODE = sys._getframe().f_code


@dataclass
class Alarm:
    high: bool = False
    sensor_fault: bool = False
    high_since: int | None = None
    invalid_since: int | None = None
    last_ms: int | None = None
    events: list = field(default_factory=list)

    def step(self, time_ms, temperature_c, acknowledge=False):
        if type(time_ms) is not int or time_ms < 0 or time_ms % 100:
            raise ValueError("Model uses nonnegative integer 100 ms ticks")
        if self.last_ms is not None and time_ms - self.last_ms != 100:
            raise ValueError("Model requires contiguous 100 ms ticks")
        if type(acknowledge) is not bool:
            raise ValueError("Acknowledge must be boolean")
        previous = (self.high, self.sensor_fault)
        valid = type(temperature_c) is int or (type(temperature_c) is float and math.isfinite(temperature_c))
        if valid:
            self.invalid_since = None
            self.sensor_fault = False
            if temperature_c >= 8:
                if self.high_since is None:
                    self.high_since = time_ms
                if time_ms - self.high_since >= 2000:
                    self.high = True
            else:
                self.high_since = None
                if acknowledge:
                    self.high = False
        else:
            self.high_since = None
            if self.invalid_since is None:
                self.invalid_since = time_ms
            self.sensor_fault = time_ms - self.invalid_since >= 500
        self.last_ms = time_ms
        if previous != (self.high, self.sensor_fault):
            self.events.append({"time_ms": time_ms, "high": self.high, "sensor_fault": self.sensor_fault})
        return {"high": self.high, "sensor_fault": self.sensor_fault,
                "local_alarm": self.high or self.sensor_fault}

Requirements to architecture to executed evidence

This fictional walkthrough demonstrates the skills' artifact contracts. It is hand-authored and executed locally, not a controlled Sol/Astra evaluation output.

  1. Brief: needs, scenarios, boundary, teaching assumptions.
  2. Requirements: sources, conditions, time reference, units, acceptance.
  3. Architecture: allocations, interfaces, decisions, hazards/controls.
  4. Verification: eight reproducible procedures, including finite-state exploration and invalid-input checks.
  5. Baseline: connected sources, allocations, verification, evidence. Executed record: configuration hashes and measured results.

The original v1 snapshot retains all supplied artifacts and results byte-for-byte; its six original procedures still reproduce. The current schema adds exact source locators, the ACTOR-01/IFC-02 acknowledgement interface, execution provenance, and separate integrity/outcome/acceptance reporting. Run history is append-only under evidence/runs/; the selected result can change only after its previous bytes have been archived. Each --check executes a fresh reproduction and leaves the historical record's date and host untouched.

Checked reference-model evidence contract

The version 2 baseline identifies sources, requirements, functions, components, external actors, interfaces, verification activities, and evidence. Every ID is unique within the baseline. A source locator is exact text that occurs once in its artifact. IFC-02 connects ACTOR-01 to COMP-02, so operator acknowledgement appears in the checked trace as well as the architecture diagram.

The source files and the baseline itself must be included in configuration coverage. An executed record hashes exactly the baseline's declared configuration files. The input baseline must equal its configured artifact. Changing the requirement text, model, procedure, evidence-writing code, or baseline invalidates old evidence until a new execution and applicability assessment are performed.

Current runners bind each loaded Python module to its source bytes at import. The binding compares the actual module code object with compilation of those bytes, which also catches a stale bytecode cache or a source edit during import. Execution rejects any later change to the model, procedures, explorer or writer, and records those loaded-source hashes. The workflow comparison applies the same binding to its comparison code, writer and trace checker. Historical snapshots retain their original collection mechanism and provenance.

Field Meaning
status: planned Proposed work; no artifact or execution credit is claimed.
status: drafted A named artifact exists; no execution credit is claimed.
status: executed A version 2 execution record supplies run ID, timestamps, command, Python/platform, hashes, outcomes and observations.
result: pass/fail/inconclusive The procedure's observed outcome, independent of whether its record is structurally valid.
review: pending/reviewed Review is separate from execution; Reviewed requires a reviewer and a hashed review artifact.
acceptance: not_accepted_for_hardware This reference-model contract provides no hardware or stakeholder acceptance.

The checker rejects unsupported record versions, inconsistent scopes, missing provenance, stale or incomplete hashes, duplicate/missing outcomes, unstructured or nonfinite observations, and contradictory acceptance claims. Outcomes from a rejected record contribute zero executed or passing procedure counts. A baseline with any integrity error receives zero requirements with passing evidence credit. A valid record containing a failure still counts as an executed procedure; a requirement receives passing credit only if all its linked procedures pass.

The summary therefore separates reported procedure count, valid execution records, rejected records, pass/fail/inconclusive outcomes, and requirement coverage. Those checks establish consistency and applicability of the supplied record. They do not authenticate a producer, prove that an arbitrary recorded observation is truthful, or establish that a procedure adequately tests its claim. run_checks.py --check separately reruns this example's actual procedures and compares observations. The finite-state procedure's precise abstraction is in verification.

The runner and trace checker use the same review-reference validation, including reviewer identity, contained artifact path and artifact hash. Workflow receipts also require complete execution provenance; reproducing observations does not repair missing timestamps, commands, run identity or loaded-source bindings. Current model reproduction requires the saved loaded-source map to match the actual bound modules. The generic checker validates any supplied map against Python configuration hashes; immutable historical records without that later field retain their original, more limited provenance contract.

Execution files under evidence/runs/ are created exclusively. Selecting a new result archives prior selected bytes before atomic replacement. A run ID collision with different content fails. Explicit output paths never overwrite. Historical v1 files remain in the original snapshot; their recorded Python version is preserved and their missing execution timestamp is not retroactively invented.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/history/legacy-v1/README.md

Requirements to architecture to executed evidence

This fictional walkthrough demonstrates the skills' artifact contracts. It is hand-authored and executed locally, not a controlled Sol/Astra evaluation output.

  1. Brief: needs, scenarios, boundary, teaching assumptions.
  2. Requirements: sources, conditions, time reference, units, acceptance.
  3. Architecture: allocations, interfaces, decisions, hazards/controls.
  4. Verification: six reproducible procedures and observations.
  5. Baseline: connected sources, allocations, verification, evidence. Executed record: configuration hashes and measured results.
python examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/run_checks.py
python examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/run_checks.py --check
python scripts/check_trace.py examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/baseline.json

In an authorized host, provide the brief and invoke $mbse-requirements, then $mbse-architecture and $mbse-verification-evidence. Preserve IDs and request artifacts through local execution. Withhold this worked answer when evaluating behavior.

Results establish sampled reference behavior only. Physical sensing/annunciation, power loss, jitter, calibration, persistence, environmental qualification, and operator response remain open. No real device, risk acceptance, or stakeholder validation is claimed.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/history/legacy-v1/architecture.md

Architecture and allocation

The logical design separates sensing, evaluation, local annunciation, and events. reference_model.py emulates evaluation/event behavior and returns output flags; it does not implement the sensor or sound/light actuator.

flowchart LR
  S[COMP-01 Sensor adapter] -->|IFC-01 time and temperature| E[COMP-02 Evaluator]
  U[Technician] -->|IFC-02 acknowledgement| E
  E -->|IFC-03 high OR fault| A[COMP-03 Annunciator]
  E -->|IFC-04 transition record| L[COMP-04 Event recorder]
Function Requirements Allocation Responsibility
FUN-01 Qualify temperature interval REQ-01 COMP-02 Reset pending timer on invalid/low input; latch after interval
FUN-02 Diagnose input availability REQ-02 COMP-01, COMP-02 Invalid input detection and valid recovery
FUN-03 Retain/acknowledge warning REQ-03 COMP-02, COMP-03 Preserve high latch and expose state
FUN-04 Record state changes REQ-04 COMP-02, COMP-04 Once per changed state pair

IFC-01: (time_ms, temperature_c) on contiguous 100 ms ticks. None, NaN, infinity, booleans, and nonnumeric values are invalid temperatures. The model rejects gaps, duplicate/out-of-order ticks, noninteger times, and nonboolean acknowledgement. IFC-02: acknowledgement at current tick. IFC-03: separate high/fault and their OR as local alarm. IFC-04: ordered time_ms, high, sensor_fault records in volatile memory.

AD-01: high latches, fault automatically clears on valid recovery to distinguish an excursion requiring acknowledgement from a current diagnostic condition. AD-02: discrete ticks make teaching checks reproducible; continuous timing and missing-tick handling remain open. AD-03: transitions are logged once; persistence is open.

HAZ-01: unnoticed excursion, CTL-01: warning plus operator action. HAZ-02: misleading healthy indication during sensor failure, CTL-02: invalid-input detection. Tests check modeled controls; noisy-lab effectiveness and reagent protection are unvalidated. Shared power is a common dependency, not redundancy.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/history/legacy-v1/brief.md

Stakeholder brief

This fictional project monitors a laboratory cabinet holding temperature-sensitive research reagents. It is not claimed to be a medical device or validated storage system.

Source Need / teaching-project decision
NEED-01 Local warning after temperature has remained at or above 8 deg C for 2 s. This project threshold is not a sourced clinical/reagent limit.
NEED-02 Distinguishable sensor-unavailable indication after 1 s of invalid readings.
NEED-03 High warning remains visible until temperature is below 8 deg C and a technician acknowledges.
NEED-04 Timestamped alarm changes for investigation.

SCN-01: monitor storage, detect a sustained excursion, latch warning, observe recovery, acknowledge, retain event record. SCN-02: invalid/missing readings produce sensor fault; valid reading clears that fault; an existing high warning still needs valid recovery and acknowledgement.

Boundary: sensing interface, alarm logic, local annunciation, event record. Refrigeration control, networks, reagent disposition, and lab quality decisions are outside this demonstration.

Assumptions: samples every 100 ms; monotonic timestamps; power available; a valid reading represents cabinet temperature. Physical accuracy, sound/light perception, power loss, calibration, retention across reset, and staffing/response time require subsequent design and stakeholder validation.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/history/legacy-v1/requirements.md

Proposed requirement baseline

Values come from the brief, not regulation. Requirements apply to sampled reference behavior. Timer intervals begin at the first applicable sample, not a physical threshold crossing between samples.

ID Requirement Source Acceptance
REQ-01 The evaluator shall latch high within 100 ms after valid samples have been at or above 8 deg C continuously for 2 s, and not before that interval. NEED-01 First high 2000-2100 ms from first qualifying sample; below-threshold/invalid sample resets pending interval.
REQ-02 The evaluator shall assert sensor fault within 100 ms after readings have been invalid continuously for 1 s; the next valid sample shall clear sensor fault. NEED-02 First fault 1000-1100 ms; clearance on next valid sample. Nonfinite/nonnumeric readings are invalid.
REQ-03 The evaluator shall retain latched high until acknowledgement while the current sample is valid and below 8 deg C. NEED-03 Early acknowledgement, recovery alone, and sensor recovery cannot silently clear high.
REQ-04 The event recorder shall record each change of high/fault state once, with sample time and resulting states. NEED-04 Exact ordered transition records; no event for unchanged state.

Derived interface IFC-01 uses contiguous 100 ms ticks, supporting the model timing claims. Jitter, transport/actuator latency, and persistence need further requirements. No requirement is marked stakeholder approved.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/history/legacy-v1/verification.md

Verification procedures

Run python examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/run_checks.py from repository root. The runner uses explicit inputs, saves observations, and hashes implementation, baseline, procedure, and design sources. No model API or physical equipment is used.

ID Requirement Procedure Acceptance
VER-01 REQ-01 Feed 8 deg C from t=0 through 2100 ms. No early high; first at 2000 ms.
VER-02 REQ-01 High, one 7.9 deg C sample at 1900 ms, then high through 3800 ms. Pending interval restarts; no high yet.
VER-03 REQ-02 Missing readings t=0 through 1100 ms. First fault 1000 ms.
VER-04 REQ-03 Latch high, acknowledge at 9 deg C, recover without acknowledgement, acknowledge at 7 deg C. Only final action clears high.
VER-05 REQ-04 Inspect VER-04 records, including unchanged ticks. Exactly assertion at 2000 and clearance at 2300, correct states.
VER-06 REQ-02, REQ-04 NaN through 1000 ms, then valid 7 deg C. Fault and recovery with exactly their two records.

Input-contract rejection and additional boundaries/interactions are in tests/test_reference_model.py, separate from the stored evidence record. None establishes physical performance, accuracy, persistence, or stakeholder acceptance. The tracked evidence is executed against the reference model. Design is proposed; review and hardware acceptance remain separate. Changed hashes or procedures need rerun and applicability review. Structural trace checks do not prove semantic adequacy.

Source: examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/verification.md

Verification procedures

Run python examples/worked/cold-storage-alarm/run_checks.py from repository root. The runner uses explicit inputs, saves observations, and hashes implementation, baseline, procedure, and design sources. No model API or physical equipment is used.

ID Requirement Procedure Acceptance
VER-01 REQ-01 Feed 8 deg C from t=0 through 2100 ms. No early high; first at 2000 ms.
VER-02 REQ-01 High, one 7.9 deg C sample at 1900 ms, then high through 3800 ms. Pending interval restarts; no high yet.
VER-03 REQ-02 Missing readings t=0 through 1100 ms. First fault 1000 ms.
VER-04 REQ-03 Latch high, acknowledge at 9 deg C, recover without acknowledgement, acknowledge at 7 deg C. Only final action clears high.
VER-05 REQ-04 Inspect VER-04 records, including unchanged ticks. Exactly assertion at 2000 and clearance at 2300, correct states.
VER-06 REQ-02, REQ-04 NaN through 1000 ms, then valid 7 deg C. Fault and recovery with exactly their two records.
VER-07 REQ-01–REQ-04 Traverse every reachable finite abstract state against an independent sample-counter oracle, using low/high/invalid temperature and both acknowledgement inputs. No output or event mismatch in any reachable transition.
VER-08 REQ-02 Exercise eight invalid-temperature classes, eight invalid next timestamps, and nonboolean acknowledgement. Invalid readings produce fault at the specified interval; invalid call contracts are rejected without changing state.

VER-07 quotients absolute time by translation and saturates elapsed timers once their decision threshold is reached. The implementation uses only those timer threshold comparisons for control decisions. The oracle counts samples instead of reading the implementation's timestamps. Every transition checks flags, local-alarm output, and exact event production. This establishes equivalence for that finite sampled abstraction and its six input combinations per state; it does not establish real clock, scheduler, sensor, actuator, or persistence behavior.

The runner records start/finish timestamps, command, Python/platform versions, source hashes, and measured observations. Each execution has an immutable file under evidence/runs/; evidence/results.json selects the current record. The previous selected bytes are archived before a replacement. --output refuses an existing file, and --check reproduces observations without rewriting history.

Input-contract rejection and additional boundaries/interactions are in tests/test_reference_model.py, separate from the stored evidence record. None establishes physical performance, accuracy, persistence, or stakeholder acceptance. The tracked evidence is executed against the reference model. Design is proposed; review and hardware acceptance remain separate. Changed hashes or procedures need rerun and applicability review. Structural trace checks do not prove semantic adequacy.

Source: platform/codex/install.md

Codex installation and maintenance

Run the commands from this checkout. Use Python 3.10 or newer: python3 on Linux/macOS, or py on Windows. The installer needs only the standard library.

python3 --version
python3 scripts/install.py --list
python3 scripts/install.py --diagnose --skill mbse-requirements
python3 scripts/install.py --project /path/to/project --skill mbse-requirements --skill mbse-architecture --dry-run
python3 scripts/install.py --project /path/to/project --skill mbse-requirements --skill mbse-architecture

PowerShell accepts quoted paths:

py scripts/install.py --project 'C:\Projects\pump-study' --skill mbse-medical-device --skill mbse-verification-evidence --dry-run

Canonical packages are .agents/skills/<name>. Launching Codex in this checkout uses those packages directly. The installer copies selected packages, references, and license into the target project's .agents/skills/. Use --destination for an explicit different skills directory. Existing project instructions, model settings, and credentials are preserved.

In the destination project, open a new Codex chat and select the skill with $:

Use $mbse-requirements on this brief. Show the source and acceptance condition for each proposed requirement, and identify the decisions that need my input.

If discovery fails, run --diagnose --project /path/to/project --skill NAME, confirm the reported path and host project match, then start a new chat. A ready package report checks files; it does not prove native discovery or answer quality. See the support matrix for the tested boundary.

Inspect and update

python3 scripts/install.py --project /path/to/project --skill mbse-requirements --inspect
python3 scripts/install.py --project /path/to/project --skill mbse-requirements --diff
python3 scripts/install.py --project /path/to/project --skill mbse-requirements --update --dry-run
python3 scripts/install.py --project /path/to/project --skill mbse-requirements --update

Inspection separates local changes since the managed install from changes in the incoming package. --diff displays current-to-incoming text differences; it never merges or writes. For an unmanaged package, the original local baseline is unknown. Review changes in a separate copy before deciding what to retain.

The installer refuses unmanaged or modified targets. It stages and checks every selected package before replacement. A failed commit rolls earlier replacements back; if rollback encounters new local changes or another I/O failure, the error identifies the preserved target and original backup for recovery. Abrupt process termination or power loss is not a transaction guarantee. Successful updates print their backup paths under the skills parent's .mbse-backups/.

Remove or restore a managed package

python3 scripts/install.py --project /path/to/project --skill mbse-requirements --uninstall --dry-run
python3 scripts/install.py --project /path/to/project --skill mbse-requirements --uninstall
python3 scripts/install.py --project /path/to/project --skill mbse-requirements --restore /path/to/project/.agents/.mbse-backups/mbse-requirements/BACKUP_ID --dry-run

Removal moves an unchanged managed package into a backup. It does not delete it. Replace BACKUP_ID with the printed identifier; remove --dry-run to restore. Restore checks the backup, preserves its source copy, and backs up any unchanged current package. Modified current packages and modified backups are refused. For plugin-manager installations, use that host's lifecycle controls instead of this standalone-package installer.

Build a native plugin

Use the plugin build guide for a portable plugin and local marketplace setup. Source compatibility manifests point at .agents/skills/; the built folder supplies the portable root skills/ directory.

Sources checked 2026-11-13: Codex skills and OpenAI plugin packaging.
