Cursor manual context

Use the portable guide and the canonical packages in .agents/skills. Verify the current host's skill/context mechanism before copying. These are skills with local references, not legacy named subagent personas. No supported discovery or invocation syntax for this host is asserted by this release.

Provide only the selected skill and referenced files through the editor's available context controls. See the support matrix for maintained native integrations; no Cursor-specific installer is supplied.

Source: platform/databricks/install.md

Databricks Genie Code

Export only the skills needed for the current task:

python3 scripts/package_plugin.py --target databricks --skill mbse-requirements --skill mbse-architecture --output build/databricks-review --zip

Use py on Windows. The fresh output contains .assistant/skills/<name>/ packages, their licenses, and a combined context.md with the selected Markdown references. The ZIP is a file-transfer artifact, not a claimed Databricks plugin import format. Existing outputs are refused.

For native user skills, transfer the selected package directories into /Users/<username>/.assistant/skills/ in your Databricks workspace. Preserve existing packages; reconcile a name collision before replacing anything. Genie Code also documents registering a different parent skills folder through its settings, which is useful for a Databricks Git folder.

Start a new Genie Code chat and select a skill with an @ mention. Supply the system brief and state the expected artifact. If native skills are unavailable, provide context.md through the chat's available context mechanism. Keep this task-specific material out of workspace-wide instructions.

The export's files, references, and selected contents are tested locally. No Databricks upload, workspace discovery, or engineering behavior evaluation has been performed. This export does not connect to Unity Catalog, deploy an agent, or grant data access. See the support matrix.

Source checked 2026-11-13: Databricks Genie Code skills.

Source: platform/generic/install.md

Portable use

Read the catalog, then provide the chosen canonical SKILL.md and its local references to your assistant through the host's documented context or skill mechanism. Describe the task, inputs, desired artifacts, and completion boundary. If the host lacks skill discovery, load context manually. Do not paste all domains into an always-on system prompt.

Each canonical package is self-contained. Task/domain combinations are optional; select those that improve the current decision. A Markdown file does not grant MBSE tool access or establish certification. Use available authorized connectors or label the output as a proposal.

The installer supports --destination /explicit/skills/directory for hosts that read this skill format. Check that host's current documentation for discovery and invocation. The original named-agent formats are no longer maintained.

Use python3 scripts/install.py --diagnose --skill NAME to inspect a package before copying it (py on Windows). See the support matrix for maintained host paths and test boundaries. A selected context export can also supply one Markdown document plus the original referenced files for manual context loading; native discovery is a separate host capability.

Source: platform/plugin/install.md

Build an installable plugin

From the source checkout, build a fresh folder and optional ZIP:

python3 scripts/package_plugin.py --output build/local-plugin --zip --dry-run
python3 scripts/package_plugin.py --output build/local-plugin --zip

Use py on Windows. The builder reads config/plugin.json and catalog.json, copies canonical .agents/skills/ packages into root skills/, includes the license in every package, and adds a Claude Code manifest. It excludes archived skills, repository instructions, evaluation rubrics, and private host settings. ZIP file order and timestamps are fixed. Existing outputs are refused, including paths created during the build. Completed files are published with atomic no-replacement links on the output filesystem. A publication failure preserves and reports visible outputs; a directory may be partial. Choose a fresh output path for another build. --skill NAME selects a smaller bundle.

The built folder contains:

plugin.json
.claude-plugin/plugin.json
skills/<name>/SKILL.md
skills/<name>/references/
skills/<name>/LICENSE
LICENSE
README.md

The root source checkout supplies compatibility manifests pointing at canonical .agents/skills/; the release build supplies the portable layout above. Build for portable distribution. Building does not install, publish, or modify host settings. After changing config/plugin.json, regenerate source compatibility manifests with python3 scripts/package_plugin.py --source-manifests write; use --source-manifests check to check freshness without writing.

Codex local marketplace

For a local trial, merge this entry into the checkout's .agents/plugins/marketplace.json, preserving any existing entries:

{
  "name": "mbse-agents-local",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "mbse-agents",
      "source": {"source": "local", "path": "./build/local-plugin"},
      "policy": {"installation": "AVAILABLE", "authentication": "ON_INSTALL"},
      "category": "Productivity"
    }
  ]
}

Register the marketplace through your host's plugin interface or the supported CLI command below, then install the listed plugin in the desktop interface:

codex plugin marketplace add /absolute/path/to/mbse-agents

These registration steps are for the operator to run; the builder does not run them. Open a fresh chat and verify that the expected skill is available. For a smaller project installation, use the standalone installer.

Other maintained paths

Claude Code loads the built folder directly. Databricks uses a separate selected-skills export. See the support matrix for what has actually been tested.

Host support and validation

The maintained paths are selected Codex project skills, a portable plugin build with a Claude Code manifest, and a selected Databricks export. Local file checks and host execution establish different things.

Host Maintained path Evidence for this revision Remaining host check
Codex Repository/project skills; portable plugin build Installer/package tests; native source discovery found all 13 canonical namespaced skills with codex-cli 0.169.0 and no model call Behavioral skill activation and packaged-plugin activation remain untested
Claude Code Built plugin with .claude-plugin/plugin.json and skills/ Canonical-file, manifest, license, and archive tests; current official layout reviewed Run claude plugin validate and invoke a skill; Claude Code is unavailable on the validation host
Databricks Genie Code Selected .assistant/skills/ export plus context.md Export content and local-reference tests; official user-skill setup reviewed Import into the target workspace and invoke with @; no workspace integration test was performed
ChatGPT Portable plugin package, or selected manual context Package structure checked Account/workspace import and activation; no universal upload capability is assumed
Claude Desktop chat, Cursor, Aider, other hosts Selected manual context Canonical instructions and references supplied No native adaptation or discovery claim for these surfaces

Run python3 scripts/install.py --diagnose --skill NAME to check a package without installing it. Use py on Windows. A host supports this release only within the path and evidence stated above; tests do not establish engineering quality, domain acceptance, or access to a model or external engineering tool.
